News.title: Missing schoolgirl, 11, found dead in village park after vanishing less than 24 hours ago
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAGIC END Missing schoolgirl, 11, found dead in village park after vanishing less than 24 hours ago







Next

A MISSING 11-year-old schoolgirl has been found dead in a village park after vanishing less than 24 hours ago.

The youngster’s body was tragically discovered near the cricket ground in Elmley Castle, Worcestershire.

She had been reported missing at around 11.20pm yesterday (Sunday, October 4).

Cops say her death is currently being treated as unexplained.





West Mercia Police said an investigation has been launched into the heartbreaking discovery.

Her devastated family have been informed and are being supported by specially trained officers.

Cops are now working to establish what happened to the girl and the circumstances surrounding her death.

A force spokesperson said: “An investigation has been launched after the body of an 11-year-old girl was found in Elmley Castle, Worcestershire.



“The girl was reported missing at around 11.20pm yesterday evening (Sunday 4 October) and was later found deceased in the park near the cricket ground.

“Her family have been informed and are being supported by specially trained officers.

“Enquiries are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding her death, which at this stage is being treated as unexplained.”

Locals in Elmley Castle are expected to see an increased police presence as officers carry out their enquiries.



Cops are urging anyone with information that could help their investigation to come forward.

News.title: Boy, 15, who seems ‘younger than his age’ missing for three days as police launch appeal
News.content:

FIND CONNOR Boy, 15, who seems ‘younger than his age’ missing for three days as police launch appeal







Next

COPS are continuing their search for a 15-year-old boy who vanished three days ago.

Connor was last seen in Llanharan, Rhondda Cynon Taf, in Wales, at around 9am on Thursday.



Officers are growing concerned for the youngster’s welfare.

They are urgently appealing for information from the public to help find him.



Connor is described as 5ft 5in tall and of slight build, with black hair.

The force said he appears younger than his 15 years of age.

South Wales Police said: “If you have seen Connor or have any information, please contact South Wales Police quoting 2600317807.”

Anyone with information can also contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Brits, 19 and 22, arrested in Barbados ‘over nearly £1m drug smuggling plot after being caught with 47kg of cocaine’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

DRUG BUST Brits, 19 and 22, arrested in Barbados ‘over nearly £1m drug smuggling plot after being caught with 47kg of cocaine’







Next

TWO Brits have been arrested in Barbados on suspicion of plotting to smuggle more than £900,000 of cocaine.

Abdul-Rasheed Anjolaoluwa Oduola, 19, and Miraldie Ndunzi, 22, were cuffed after cops allegedly found them with 47kg of the class-A drug.



The pair have been charged with possession, trafficking, intent to supply and attempting to export cocaine.

Barbados cops said Oduola, from Dagenham, and Ndunzi, from Stor Road in east London, were found with about 23kg of cocaine each.



Both seizures were worth roughly $1million Barbados dollars (£440,000) each.

Local police said the arrests were made on September 29.

Oduola and Ndunzi appeared in court in Horse Hill, St Joseph, on October 2.

It is unclear how the drugs were discovered by authorities.

An investigation into the alleged smuggling plot is ongoing.

The Sun reached out to the Foreign Office for comment.



It comes after an OAP tried to smuggle £640,000 of cocaine into the UK from Barbados by stashing it in his mobility scooter.

Canadian Ronald Lord, 71, said he was in Britain for sightseeing when stopped at Gatwick.

Border Force officers put his scooter through an X-ray machine and found 8kg of the Class A drug hidden within the back-panel of his seat.

He denied knowing how the coke got there, but a screw from the panel was discovered in his pocket in the February 2025 search.

Lord admitted drug smuggling at Croydon crown court and was jailed for six years.

News.title: Our scared children couldn’t tell us of ‘brutal torture’ in school’s padded ‘calming rooms’… then we saw the horror CCTV
News.content:
Next

DEBORAH Pritchard remembers how her son Jamie would regularly return from school “highly distressed” and “with ripped clothing” – but as a non-verbal child, he couldn’t tell her what had happened.

It wasn’t until years later that, Deborah, 63, would learn what went on in the eerie, windowless “calming rooms” at Jamie’s former school – horrifying acts that have been described as “nothing short of torture”.



And now Deborah – along with nine other families with similar stories – are desperate for answers and taking action.

Horrifying CCTV showing the padded rooms – which was first made public by the BBC – was discovered by the new leadership at Whitefield School in Walthamstow in 2021.

Memory sticks were found containing some 500 hours of CCTV footage from the seclusion rooms – where children were locked in until they calmed down.

Some of the distressing footage, filmed between 2014 and 2017, appeared to show autistic children and children with learning disabilities being thrown to the floor, abused, restrained, and left alone within the padded rooms.



The footage was handed to police – but no charges were ever brought after a three-year investigation.

However, ten families are now taking legal action against Flourish Learning Trust – which ran the school – and the London Borough of Waltham Forest.

The trust says they recognise the “seriousness” of the events at the school, and the council says they were unaware of concerns at the school until the footage was discovered in 2021 – rejecting any suggestions of a “cover up”.

Jamie’s mum Deborah went to a screening of the harrowing footage put on by police to see how her son had been treated.



She said: “How would they feel it if was their children. Someone they loved being treated like this.

“Why did they think this was acceptable to do this to vulnerable children?”

Jamie, now 27, attended Whitefield School until he was 18 and his mum said during that time he started having epileptic fits and “he would hit himself at night and regularly wake up crying”.

Deborah said she questioned the school several times but never got any admission over the use of the rooms.



She added: “It was a complete cover up. It was fully logged that they had been in there for a long length of time. No window, no natural ventilation, no water, no toilet – how frustrating must that have been.”

Waltham Forest Borough Council has denied all suggestions of a cover up.

Deborah and Jamie are one of 10 families filing the civil case with law firm Leigh Day.

The firm said it began investigating allegations from children and families in September 2023. It is understood a total of 39 pupils have been identified.



The claims include allegations of breach of duty of care, false imprisonment and breaches of human rights arising from the use of the rooms between 2014-2017.

Some of the harrowing footage was later leaked to the BBC and was the subject of a 2024 Panorama which led to widespread calls for the changes to guidance on the use of seclusion in special schools.

Ricardo Gloria, 48, was the first to report concerns as his son David, now 22, was one of the few pupils able to verbally communicate.

The dad, from Chingford, said David returned home from school one day and said he had spent three hours and 45 minutes in one of the locked padded rooms.



He said: “I asked to watch the CCTV footage and it was simply horrible. I just cried.”

He added: “How could they do that? It was just so wrong.”

He continued: “At the time I was a prison officer and it was just like looking at a cell.

“It was padded and hot as hell – and they kept him in there for three hours and 45 minutes.”



No other families were aware until Ofsted instructed the school to stop after it identified the use of the secure rooms and rated Whitefield “Inadequate” in 2017.

The parents were told about the CCTV in 2022 with many, like Deborah, finding out when police knocked on their doors.

Ricardo said: “We can not retrieve time – but I would like some justice.

“They destroyed my son’s future and I’d like some accountability for the damage they have done.



“It was a complete cover up – done with the blessing of the council.

“There was zero explanation and they have just been hoping it all goes away.”

Halima Abuukar, 48, of Walthamstow, also watched her son Adbulhai, now 23, being thrown around on the video as a young boy.

She said Adbulhai was in one of the rooms for four hours at one point “just ignored”.



The mum continued: “The reason we chose the school was we thought he would be loved and cared for. But whatever he went through in the calming rooms he is living with that damage for the rest of his life.”

Maria Franklin, 59, claimed she also watched footage of her son George, 28, being “thrown into the room” by staff who then locked the door behind them.

George has learning disabilities and has never been able to tell his mum what happened in the room, she said.

She added: “This is the sort of thing you might expect in Victorian Britain – not in the 21st century. It is barbaric, especially for a school that was deemed to be a centre of excellence.”



Andrew Pritchard, uncle of Jamie, has launched the Whitefield Advocacy Group to bring the families together and campaign for a ban on calming rooms.

He said his nephew’s treatment had been “inhumane and cruel by any standard”.

In July this year, a Local Child Safeguarding Practice Review was published by Waltham Forest Safeguarding Partners about the use of restrictive practices.

The review found the children’s “dignity, safety and wellbeing were compromised” by being locked in the padded isolation rooms.

One parent told the review “it was similar to a hostage and torture situation”.



It has also made a national recommendation that the Department for Education publish further clarification on the accountability and oversight responsibilities of local authorities, regulators and independent schools, to help ensure stronger safeguarding oversight and timely intervention where harmful or poor practice is known or suspected.

Alison Millar, partner at Leigh Day, said: “The children and families we represent have endured the consequences of a regime of isolation at Whitefield School that should never have been allowed to happen.”

“The review confirms that there was no justification for the restrictive practices in operation at Whitefield School between 2014 and 2017,” she said.

She added: “The use of the so-called calming rooms against children with multiple vulnerabilities was, in our clients’ view, nothing short of torture.”

A council spokesperson said: “We are unable to comment on specific details while the Leigh Day legal action is ongoing. But we can categorically confirm that no safeguarding concerns relating to the calming rooms at Whitefield School were raised with the council prior to the discovery of CCTV footage by the new school leadership team in 2021.



“We strongly reject any suggestions of a cover up. We notified the police as soon as the evidence emerged, and the comprehensive Local Children Safeguarding Practice Review (LCSPR) that thoroughly examined all aspects of the case, including the role of the council, is publicly available in its entirety.”

A spokesperson for Flourish Learning Trust said: “We recognise the seriousness of the events at the school which took place between 2014 and 2017, and our thoughts remain with the children and families affected by what happened.

“The review reports on important learning to assist with the changes which have taken place to offer better protection for children. Flourish Learning Trust no longer operates any schools, and none of the prior leadership are still in post. Interim arrangements are in place to ensure oversight until the Trust is officially closed.

“Whitefield School itself is now being run by a different trust which supports the outcomes from the review and has been working hard to transform the school and give every pupil the care, dignity and support they rightfully deserve.”

A Department for Education spokesman said: “What happened at Whitefield was horrific, and a serious failure to protect children. They deserved so much better, and we recognise the lasting impact this will have on them and their families.



“We have already strengthened safeguards for pupils, including through a new legal duty for schools to record and report to parents all incidents of seclusion and restraint.

“We have carefully considered the report’s findings, are engaging closely with the panel, and won’t hesitate to act to help prevent incidents like this ever happening again.”

News.title: Body of man in his 20s found inside home after ‘unexpected’ death – as bomb squad called in to remove ‘substances’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

DEATH PROBE Body of man in his 20s found inside home after ‘unexpected’ death – as bomb squad called in to remove ‘substances’







Next

THE body of a man was tragically discovered inside a home – before a bomb squad were called in to remove “substances”.

Cops are probing the “unexpected” death of the victim, in his 20s, after he was found in the property in Oxton, Merseyside, on Saturday.

Emergency crews were scrambled to the home in Reedville at around 4pm.

Paramedics tragically found the victim’s body before reporting the grim discovery to Merseyside Police.





Officers quickly launched an investigation into the tragedy, with the man’s death being treated as “unexpected”.

Explosive Ordnance Disposal teams were later called after “substances” were also found at the property.

The force later confirmed there is no wider risk to members of the public.

A file will now be passed to the coroner.

On Sunday, Merseyside Police said: “We can confirm emergency services remain in Oxton today following a sudden death yesterday.

“Shortly after 3.55pm on Saturday 3 October, North West Ambulance Service reported they had attended a property on Reedville where they had found a man in his 20s sadly deceased inside.

“Merseyside Police has launched an investigation and following initial enquiries, his death is being treated as unexpected.

“His next of kin has been informed and a file will be passed to the Coroner.



“As a precaution, Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) have attended to assess and remove substances located inside the premises.

“They have deemed there is no wider risk to the public at this stage.”

News.title: Posh beauty brand launches luxury dog range from £40 perfume to £80 wellness pack – and some items are already sold out
News.content:
Next

THESE could be the pawfect presents for your pampered pooch — part of a luxury range created especially for man’s best friend by posh beauty brand Rituals.

As well as alcohol-free perfume for £40, there are shampoos, paw treatments, grooming products and accessories in the Dog Spa range.



It also includes a £17 dry shampoo, a £14.90 dog mouth spray and a £22.90 air and fabric freshener.

There is even an £80 Dogstar wellness pack with the air and fabric freshener and shampoo plus wipes and paw balm — with a ball thrown in, too.



Despite the range only just going on sale, some items have already sold out online.

But don’t worry, they’ll be bark in stock soon.



Last month we revealed the extreme lengths paw-rents will go to for their dogs – including cooking them bespoke gourmet meals, talking to them as if they were a child, and giving them spa days.

A poll of 1,800 dog owners found other lengths they have gone to included letting them sit in the front seat of the car and purchasing luxury bedding for them.



Typically, owners spend an average of £101 per month looking after their pooch – and are willing to spend £36 on a one-off treat.

A spokesperson for free streaming service, U, which commissioned the research following the launch of its show Wagging Rights, said: “People look after their dog like they’re VIPs, and it’s fascinating to see just how pampered the nation’s pups have become, proving the lengths we would go to for our four-legged friends.

“For many owners, no expense is spared when it comes to keeping their dog happy, healthy and comfortable.

“From luxury dinners to luxury spa days, these findings reveal that Britain’s dogs are truly being treated like members of the family.”

A DELIVEROO rapist who attacked a semi-conscious woman is terrified of prison reprisals.

Algerian migrant Salem Rekoub refuses to leave his cell and has threatened to harm himself.

Rekoub, who was working illegally for Deliveroo, is now said to be “petrified” of fellow prisoners at Wormwood Scrubs.

“There is a lot of hostility to him inside.

News.title: Shabana Mahmood admits foreign worker visas are being requested every week by Cabinet ministers to plug urgent shortages
News.content:
Next

CABINET ministers are begging for foreign worker visas as often as every week because they cannot fill jobs with Brits, Shabana Mahmood has revealed.

The Home Secretary admitted her Labour colleagues routinely come to her asking for permission to bring in overseas staff to plug urgent shortages.



She accused departments of becoming too reliant on “pulling the immigration lever” rather than training workers already in Britain.

Ms Mahmood told The Rest is Politics podcast: “The sheer number of requests I get from colleagues across government from other departments – can I have 10 visas over here for welders or something?”



She added: “I’m like, you’re telling me that we can’t find 10 welders?

“But it’s become a lever that is easy to pull. And everyone always says, well, it’s urgent, and we haven’t got the time. And I just think we should be more in control here.”



Asked whether Cabinet ministers really contacted her asking for visas for workers such as welders, she replied: “I have a conversation like that at least once every week or two. It happens all the time.

“From their side of the equation, they’d be thinking, we’ve got to plug a gap really quickly.

“And this is the best way to do it really quickly. To which I would say you’ve got to be able to do a bit more long term planning for your workforce in your own country. This is how you end up with a million NEETs.”

The Home Secretary singled out social care, saying the sector was “riven with poor pay and conditions” and “often very abusive working conditions”.



But Ms Mahmood stressed Britain would still need workers from overseas where there was a genuine labour shortage.

She said ministers should first improve skills, workforce planning, pay and conditions in Britain before automatically reaching for more immigration.

Her comments come days after she signalled she could soften controversial plans to make some foreign workers wait longer for permanent residency.

The proposals would normally double the route to settled status from five to 10 years, while some health and care workers could face waits of up to 15 years.

Ms Mahmood has faced pressure from Housing Secretary Angela Rayner, more than 100 Labour MPs and unions, who say it would unfairly “move the goalposts” for migrants who came to Britain legally.

News.title: Big Brother stars announce birth of baby boy after meeting on show
News.content:
Big Brother stars announce birth of baby boy after meeting on show

Two Big Brother stars have revealed that they have welcomed a son together just a year after meeting on the ITV show, as their co-stars flood them with support

View 6 Images Marcus and Elsa welcomed their first child (Image: Instagram)

A year on from meeting on Big Brother, two ITV stars have welcomed their first child together. Elsa Rae and Marcus John welcomed their son, Marley, on 2nd October.

‌



‌



Elsa, 22, shared the news with fans via two Instagram posts on 4 October. In one post, she uploaded a picture of her, her baby and Marcus, 23, all sitting in a hospital bed together and smiling at the camera whilst Elsa breast fed her child. Other pictures also showed Marcus grinning in medical scrubs shortly after Marley's birth, and the two stars kissing. In the caption, Elsa wrote: "Marley Isaac Mark John - Born 02.10.26, our greatest creation [blue heart]."

‌



6 View 6 Images Elsa Rae and her son in hospital (Image: Instagram) 6 View 6 Images Marcus John holding baby Marley (Image: Instagram)

‌

Just hours later, Elsa posted another series of pictures of her and her son, as well as one in which she and Marcus were getting ready to leave the hospital. She added underneath: "Best day of our lives, hearts so full."

Marcus shared his own post with an adorable picture of him staring at his baby, covering the child's face with a heart emoji. He said in the caption that he was "locked in for life".

‌



In the comments of their joint post, the stars were given messages of congratulations by their fellow Big Brother alumni. Celebrity Big Brother star Jojo Siwa wrote: "Omg!!! Congratulations". Meanwhile, Zelah Glasson, who was on Elsa and Marcus' season, said: "Awww guys congratulations and welcome Marley."

Elsa and Marcus were both on Big Brother in 2025. Content creator Elsa and engineer Marcus immediately clicked and struck up a romance, going on a first date whilst one of them was locked in a cage in the garden of the house.

They have since also announced that they are engaged to be married. Marcus is said to have gotten down on one knee during a picnic, during which they also learned they were having a son. Elsa showed off her new diamond ring on Instagram, calling it the "most special ring".

News.title: Andrew ‘will take police to court’ over Sandringham Estate home raid that led to arrest
News.content:
Andrew ‘will take police to court’ over Sandringham Estate home raid that led to arrest

The former Prince, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, was arrested on his 66th birthday in February of this year, a few weeks after the King removed his dukedom and titles

View 2 Images Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor lost his titles in late 2025 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is set to take Thames Valley Police to court over allegations that searches of his homes may have broken the law, it has been reported.

‌



‌



The former Duke of York has been granted permission to challenge whether the force acted lawfully over the searches relating to his arrest in February, according to The Telegraph. Andrew’s application for a judicial review is said to have been made earlier this year and recently approved by a High Court judge.

‌



The King’s brother will challenge the legality of search warrants that allowed police to raid his residence on the Sandringham Estate and his former Windsor home, Royal Lodge, according to the report.

‌



It also said a private High Court hearing held in the coming days will decide whether to release certain court documents relating to the judicial review.

View 2 Images Unmarked vehicles enter the gates of the Royal Lodge a day after Andrew's arrest (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Andrew was arrested on his 66th birthday on suspicion of misconduct in public office following allegations he shared sensitive information with Jeffrey Epstein during his time as the UK’s trade envoy.

The King stripped his brother of both his right to be a prince and his dukedom late last year over his association with the convicted sex offender.

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and Thames Valley Police have been approached for comment.

News.title: UK 'desperately needs mass food storage sites in case of national emergencies or war'
News.content:
UK 'desperately needs mass food storage sites in case of national emergencies or war'

Experts have called on the government to ramp-up planning for a possible mass impact on UK food chain - warning households can't afford to stockpile

View 4 Images Failure to prepare for a national food emergency risks shortages - or worse (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire)

Britain should set-up a network of food storage sites to ensure families have enough to eat in the event of a national emergency, a group of 150 experts and others have urged the Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

‌



‌



It came as they warned the country had “no plan” for feeding the country if there was a major crisis, whether due to climate change, a devastating cyber attack or even war.

‌



While drastic, they say alarm bells should already be ringing given what happened during the Covid crisis, which led to panic buying, through to the threat of shortages and price risks following this summer’s record drought and forecasts chaos from the looking El Nino weather phenomenon.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images The UK's parched summer exposed the impact of climate change on the country (Image: Jacob King/PA Wire)

Top academic Professor Tim Lang, one of the leading signatories of the letter to PM and First Secretary Louise Haigh, warns the country risked “sleepwalking” into a crisis unless action is taken immediately. Without proper planning, he said there was the risk of riots and widespread civil unrest.

‌



The letter, signed by academics, businesses, civil leaders, and campaigners, has been sent ahead of today’s call for evidence deadline on updating the Civil Contingencies Act 2004, which allows the government to make last minute and drastic legislative changes on an unprecedented scale. Those behind the letter argue the Act fails to treat the food supply as a national security issue, despite mounting warnings from both within and outside the sector.

They argue that, for those can afford it, there is ready access to food, even though is highly concentrated in the hands of a relatively small number of producers and retailers, and is reliant on imports. However, they warned the UK was entering “a new era in which food supplies will be disrupted, public expectations may not be met and food can be weaponised”.

Among their recommendations is the creation of national, regional, local and community food storage schemes, rather than leaving households to stockpile food. Britain had a network of such sites after the Second World War, but these began to be wound down after the country joined the EU as they were deemed surplus to requirements, and were eventually scrapped altogether in the 1990s.

‌



Professor Lang, a leading expert in food policy City St George’s, University of London, and lead author of the National Preparedness Commission’s Just in Case report, warned the government needed to prepare as it might for war.

View 4 Images The food chain, and other industries, risk the ever-present danger from cyber attacks (Image: Getty Images)

“Everyone in the food system knows that shocks are coming and we are not preparing for them like other countries are doing,” he said. For example, Switzerland has three months’ worth of essentials foodstuffs stockpiled, he said.

‌



The UK’s Prepare website suggests households having enough non-perishable food that doesn’t need cooking, such as ready-to-eat tinned meat, fruit or vegetables, for an emergency lasting “a few days”.

Professor Lang called the advice “hopeless” given many people do not have enough to eat already, let alone stockpile food.

“This is ludicrous,” he said. “You can’t have resilience to individual households are the sole last line of defence.” He said a “just in time” system, meaning groceries are not ordered until as late as possible before they are needed, exposed the UK to even greater risk.

‌



View 4 Images Prof Tim Lang: “Everyone in the food system knows that shocks are coming and we are not preparing for them like other countries are doing." (Image: BBC/RAW Productions)

The danger was highlighted last year when Marks & Spencer and the Co-op were targeted by cyber criminals, resulting to a hit in supplies to both.

“Britain has got this hyper-efficient, super-concentrated food system and every insider knows it,” he said. “The danger is Britain sleepwalks into multiple crises. The worst case scenario, as food insiders say, is riots, it is deep anxiety, it is community against community, it's social division."

‌



Among the letter’s other recommendations is for a new system of local “food resilience committees”, tasked with preventing and mitigating food supply disruptions at the local level. It also suggests renaming the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs but ditching the last part in favour of “food security”.

Professor Paul Behrens, from the University of Oxford said: “The Government’s own national security assessment says the UK ‘does not have enough land to feed its population and rear livestock: a wholesale change in consumer diets would be required’. “That is Whitehall’s own analysis but there is still very little action on this. Food resilience, healthy diet, and environmental benefits all point the same direction: grow more of the vegetables, fruit and pulses people actually need, closer to home.”

Carina Millstone, executive director at the charity Foodrise, said: “Amidst severe geopolitical tensions and the fast worsening climate and environmental crises, food corporations have led us to an impasse that threatens the UK’s food and farming.

‌



“The signatories to this letter call for leadership from the Prime Minister to boost the nation’s food resilience and security without delay.”

A government spokesperson said: “Food security is national security which is why we're ensuring food supply is fully incorporated into our emergency preparedness planning.

"We are taking action now to deal with the impacts of extreme weather - one of the Prime Minister's first visits was meeting farmers hit by recent drought, announcing a £65million package to boost resilience.

Article continues below

"We’re also going further to address the risks of climate change, including a new taskforce to strengthen climate security and working with farmers and industry to build supply chains that can withstand future shocks."

The Cabinet Office announced plans in July fir a campaign to raise awareness of the simple steps households can take to keep themselves safe in everyday emergencies, bringing the UK into line with European countries which run similar campaigns already, with more information expected.

News.title: Hairy Bikers star Si King finds love again with 'very special lady'
News.content:
Hairy Bikers star Si King finds love again with 'very special lady'

Si King has revealed he is dating again after wanting to cut himself off from the world following the death of his close pal and Hairy Biker co-star Dave Myers

View 2 Images Hairy Bikers star Si King has said he is dating (Image: Sam Simpson/Dave Benett/Getty Images for Fortnum & Mason Food and Drink Awards 2026)

Hairy Bikers star Si King has revealed he has found love with a new partner - and called his new girlfriend "very special".

‌



‌



It comes two years after Si lost his best pal Dave Myers. His friend's death left him feeling lost and he admitted he had considered 'riding into the sunset' as he wanted to be left alone and cut off.

‌



Dave, who made up the famous Hairy Bikers with Si, died aged 66 in February 2024. He had been diagnosed with cancer two years earlier and underwent chemotherapy as well as other treatment.

‌



And while his death left his pal feeling like he wanted nobody to be able to reach him, it appears has has let someone break down his barriers. Si gushed he is now "very happy".

View 2 Images Si King and Dave Myers (Image: BBC/South Shore Productions/Jon Boast)

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



Spealng to The Sunday Times magazine, he said "It's been wonderful and continues to be wonderful. And you know, I think the lads [his sons] are really happy, as is my ex-wife Jane, actually."

Si was previously married to Jane Dodd, but the pair separated in 2016 after 27 years together. His career was cited as cause for their breakdown due to its tough demands and his long absences.

Si went on to say he understands he wasn't "present" for many years and that it had affected his home life. But his job went from strength to strength as he and Dave toured the continent for their numerous food shows.

‌



Earlier this month, Si admitted that grief is a 'constant surprise' and he is still processing the loss of his pal. The Bikers came to an end with the death of Dave Myers in February 2024, and his pal Si King has admitted he "doesn't know what else to do" as he deals with his grief.

Si admitted that he was continuing to work following Dave's death in part because he doesn't know what else to do during this period. He added: "I'm all right. I mean, look, it's challenging and I continue to work probably too hard, but I kind of don't know what else to do."

And he previously admitted he felt somewhat guilty for a year after Dave's death. Speaking to Lauren Laverne on BBC Radio 4's Desert Island Discs, he said: "The first year, I didn't want to do anything at all.

Article continues below

"I just didn't have it in me and then when I was shooting the show, I felt a sense of guilt that I was doing something that when he wasn't there.

"It was a very odd experience, because I was having to remember and deliver pieces to camera that I'd go 'ah you can do this'."

News.title: Domestic abusers to be flagged by courts to better track vile criminals
News.content:
Domestic abusers to be flagged by courts to better track vile criminals

Domestic abuse is already recognised as an aggravating factor in a wide range of offences, such as assault or stalking - but until now there has been no consistent way to record it

View 2 Images More than 700 prisoners were freed early from jail last week as part of the first tranche of the early release prison scheme (Image: © 2026 PA Media, All Rights Reserved)

Courts will be ordered to record when an offence involves domestic abuse to better track offenders and beef up protections for victims.

‌



‌



For the first time, perpetrators will be formally flagged as domestic abusers in the system to manage the risks they pose and identify patterns of repeat offending.

‌



Domestic abuse is already recognised as an aggravating factor in a wide range of offences, such as assault or stalking, but until now there has been no consistent way to record it once an offender is convicted.

‌



Frontline staff - including police and probation officers - will now be able to see domestic abuse flags on a criminal’s profile on their system to help them better manage risks.

Victims Minister Alex Davies-Jones said: “Too many victims have suffered because patterns of abusive behaviour have not always been recognised across the justice system.

Prisoner re-arrested immediately after leaving jail as hundreds released early from prisons READ MORE :

View 2 Images Justice Secretary Alex Norris (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire)

‌



"This is an important step towards better identifying dangerous perpetrators, protecting victims and delivering on our commitment to halve violence against women and girls."

London’s Victims’ Commissioner Andrea Simon welcomed the new specific domestic abuse flag, especially given the early release of thousands of offenders.

She said: “Within the context of early prison releases, it is vital that justice agencies can effectively identify and respond to the risks posed by domestic abuse perpetrators and put the right interventions in place to protect victims from further harm.”

‌



More than 700 prisoners were freed early from jail last week as part of the first tranche of the early release prison scheme.

Victims’ groups have raised concerns over the effectiveness of safeguards. On Sunday, Justice Secretary Alex Norris was unable to say how many prisoners freed early from jail have been tagged.

Officials said there was a presumption that all criminals released early would be fitted with GPS tags, but Mr Norris said it was “too soon” to have the numbers.

‌



Asked how many of those released so far had been tagged, Mr Norris told the BBC : “I don’t have that figure today, it only happened on Thursday. You know, there can be a bit of a lag. We don’t have that number. But you know, we’re very candid about who’s leaving prison and when they do.”

Asked if he knew if released domestic abusers have been tagged or not, he said: “It would be too soon to know that, as it was only on Thursday. We’ve been talking to every victim to to offer them the chance to say what controls they’d like to see over that individual.”

Nearly 5,000 prisoners are set to be freed in stages over the next year under the plans.

Article continues below

Meanwhile, Mr Norris also insisted the courts backlog will still be slashed despite ministers U-turning on controversial plans to curb jury trials. He said introducing legislation for judge-only trials would have been “complicated to implement” and would slow down other planned reforms.

Former Justice Secretary David Lammy had previously told MPs the reforms were “desperately needed” to prevent victims facing “agonising delays”.

News.title: KEVIN MAGUIRE: 'Kemi Badenoch’s tax cuts for the wealthy prove the Tories still put the rich first'
News.content:
Fat tax handouts for the highest earners plucked from a phantom magic money tree are proof that under Con woman Kemi Badenoch the Tory Party hasn’t changed.

Championing the fortunate few over the struggling many is traditional Two Nation feather-bedding from a dictatorial leader imposing an intolerant cult to rival fellow Thatcherite Nigel Farage’s tyrannical grip of Reform.

Lurching to the Hard Right, parading as an upmarket defender of vested interests against a poundshop Farage, isn’t pretty and it’s a political strategy that deserves to backfire spectacularly.

Because Nasty Party-bashing of the have-nots and migrants while showering supposedly free money on the already haves doesn’t add up financially or politically if centre voters with good values are repelled.

‌



View 2 Images Where will this endless supply of money fall?

Badenoch is showering tax cuts like confetti and, should she somehow miraculously tie the knot at the election and move into Downing Street, the marriage would be extremely unhappy when she hasn’t the cash to stick by paper vows.

A potential £9billion inheritance windfall for the lucky one in 20 death lottery winners who are currently pocketing up to £1million tax-free is a priority warped to enhance inequality.

Or spending £1.4bn subsidising the private education fees of the one in 14 pupils whose parents shun the real public schools teaching 93% of kids.

‌



I believe strongly in progressive universalism – all of us paying into the system according to our means and benefiting according to our needs, yet committing £700m to fund free childcare for people on £100,000-plus by erasing a Tory cut-off wouldn’t be top of my list.

Then there is last year’s £9bn scrapping of house purchase stamp duty plus the reintroduction of tourist VAT-free bungs on Armani, Louis Vuitton and other luxury goods – dumping another Con policy that reputable experts warn would cost British taxpayers £600m.

Badenoch has a dismal record in government, Farage mini-me values and wealthfare policies that should be sounding alarm bells among those seduced by a newly-developed smileyness.

King of South?

Bolstered by a poll giving Labour (30%) clear leads over fading Reform (25%) and distant Cons (17%), if Andy Burnham triumphs in the South this week, the King of the North will look a ruler of the whole country.

‌



Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali successfully defending on Thursday a 11,500 majority in London’s Holborn and St Pancras after Keir Starmer did a runner would confirm Burnham’s revived his party nationally by uprooting Zack Polanski’s Greens.

And what a result when eight months ago the Greens turned Labour’s Gorton and Denton 13,000 majority into a 4,400 walloping.

News.title: Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia has 'animalistic desire' to war amid further attacks
News.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia has 'animalistic desire' to war amid further attacks

As Russia continues to pound Kyiv, Ukraine vowed to hit back but Vladimir ‌Putin's Defence Ministry has warned any type of retaliation will be met with more severe attacks

View 3 Images Volodymyr Zelensky welcomes a financial boost from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz (Image: dts News Agency Germany Bundesregierung/Tobias Koch/Shutterstock)

Volodymyr Zelensky vowed that Ukraine will strike Russian oil refineries again as the bombardments continue in Kyiv amid 'animalistic' air assaults.

‌



‌



Ukraine's president claims Vladimir ‌Putin is attempting to weaken his country's resistance ‌by escalating attacks on the capital and after Kyiv's Northern Bridge was struck for a second time today. Zelensky says he is sickened by the strikes, which he says are geared at forcing residents to leave.

‌



He says retaliation should be expected, but the Russian Defence Ministry responded to his remarks, vowing to increase attacks on military facilities should Ukraine attempt to respond. Zelensky said in an interview Saturday that the nation would double down on attacking Russian refineries with a new policy of airstrikes.

‌



Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as your Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

View 3 Images Ukraine last attacked a Moscow oil refinery two weeks ago (Image: AP)

Russia vows to continue retaliatory strikes in Ukraine and urge people to leave Kyiv READ MORE :

“The Russian armed forces will intensify strikes against military and military-industrial facilities, as well as related infrastructure in Kyiv and other regions of Ukraine,” the Ministry said on Telegram.

‌



The comments come a day after its foreign ministry warned that foreign diplomats in the city were in “mortal danger” and must leave as soon as possible.

Zelensky told reporters: "They strike bridges, do they really think we will not respond? I am simply astonished by this ⁠animalistic desire to escalate ⁠the situation every day."

Ukraine has been boosted after the German chancellor, who was paying a surprise visit, pledged £850m in military aid as critical bridges were again struck.

‌



Friedrich Merz's show support for President Zelensky amid the escalating Russian attacks saw the nation announce a package of measures including the release the money for repairs in the energy sector.

View 3 Images Russia's President Vladimir Putin has issued further threats (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

“I traveled to Kyiv today because Ukraine needs all our support in the coming weeks,” Merz said, adding that Russian forces were bombing towns and residential buildings. “If Russia is not stopped, sooner or later its war machine will turn against us.

‌



“I will tell President Zelensky today: 'You can continue to count on our help'."

Merz said the partnership between the two countries was “not a one-way street”, pointing to German and Ukrainian companies jointly developing technologies that benefit both sides. “This makes us safer and stronger,” he said.

On Thursday, NATO appeared to call Russia's bluff after being sent an ominous nuclear attack warning as tensions escalate.

‌



Putin dispatched a letter threatening to unleash the weapons should it feel its Baltic territory is coming under threat. In the diplomatic memo, Moscow said it has been made aware of 'information that NATO is preparing an air and naval blockade of Kaliningrad'.

In the alarming letter sent to Brussels , the Kremlin warn it "will be ready to use the entire arsenal of forces and capabilities at its disposal, including nuclear weapons, in order to defend its territory", according to a document sent to member states.

NATO has responded, dismissing the threat as "irresponsible nuclear rhetoric" with Secretary General Mark Rutte stating he doesn't believe Putin will follow through on the latest outrageous threat.

‌



Andy Burnham said days before that he will “stand up to” Russian and Iranian “threats”, adding that his economic and social plans will improve the UK’s security.

He told the Labour party conference: “A country which invests in people’s success, rather than abandoning them and paying for failure.

“A country like that will be much more resilient to the shocks we will undoubtedly face in the rest of this century, and more able to meet its Nato obligations on defence.

Article continues below

“I will be steadfast in my support for Ukraine and stand up to threats wherever they come from, whether Russia, Iran, or anywhere.”

News.title: Polanski banned from Israel after party's motion declaring 'Zionism is racism'
News.content:
Israel's foreign ministry says it has banned Green Party leader Zack Polanski from entering the country, after party members adopted a motion declaring Zionism a form of racism.

Israel's foreign ministry described the motion as a "clear antisemitic text" and beyond "the boundaries of legitimate political debate".

Polanski did not take part in the vote on Sunday. The motion, which has divided senior party figures, defines Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" and backs a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine".

It has been criticised by some Jewish groups, who called the motion an "attack on the Jewish community".

"Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it," the Board of Deputies of British Jews and the Jewish Leadership Council said in a statement.

"Branding most British Jews and Jewish institutions 'racist' stokes anti-Jewish hatred after a year in which British Jews have been murdered attending their synagogue, stabbed in the streets, and seen their community buildings firebombed."

Israel's foreign ministry said the motion was "a stain on the history of the United Kingdom".

The party's joint deputy leaders have been at odds over the subject, with Mothin Ali backing the move, and Rachel Millward describing the wording as "problematic".

But members endorsed the policy motion, which was put forward by a group of activists at the party's conference in Brighton, by 1,022 votes to 813.

"The real, material, manifestation of Zionism has been the historic and ongoing dehumanisation, displacement, dispossession, disenfranchisement and destruction of Palestinians," it says.

Discussion about the vote has dominated the conference, and exposed divisions between the party's newly enlarged membership base under Polanski and its MPs elected at the last general election.

Speaking after the vote, Lubna Speitan, the Green member behind the motion, argued its backers wanted to voice opposition to "racist systems of oppression".

"We stand united against all forms of racism and discrimination - no exemptions," she added.

Polanski did not vote in the debate, having left the conference early to campaign in Holborn and St Pancras, where he is standing in a by-election to be the MP. A full list of candidates in the contest can be found here.

News.title: Protesters scuffle with police as migrants brought ashore on south coast
News.content:
About 150 anti-migrant demonstrators gathered in a south coast town to stop a group of migrants, who had crossed the English Channel in a small boat, being brought ashore by the RNLI.

Some flares were set off and there were a few scuffles with police during the stand-off at a marina in Gosport that lasted into the early hours of Monday morning.

The Home Office said 149 migrants were picked up in a mid-Channel rescue operation by the RNLI alongside a French vessel.

They were taken by coach to a processing centre in Kent. It is the second known landing of large numbers of migrants this far west along the south coast in recent years.

A police cordon was in place on Haslar Road in Gosport, where the atmosphere at the protest mostly remained peaceful.

Some protesters stopped police vans from advancing by standing in front of them and chanting "shame on you" and "deport the lot".

Hampshire Police said it deployed officers to "support our partners in the event of an emergency at sea". The force imposed conditions under the Public Order Act as well as powers prohibiting the wearing of face coverings.

News.title: Shadow chancellor to unveil Tory plans to cut taxes and regulations
News.content:
Conservative shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith is to outline his plans for the UK economy, including hopes to cut taxes, red tape and house-building costs.

Griffith and his colleagues will use day two of the party's conference in Birmingham to also explain how they would want to reduce food costs, support Heathrow Airport expansion and abolish Natural England and the Environment Agency.

Another prospective policy is replacing agreements designed to compel developers to fund community projects and services in areas they want to build.

Griffith will describe his approach as the "most ambitious deregulation project in a generation". Reform UK suggested the Tories were "copying our policies".

Griffith's speech comes after Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch published a 100-page document, external explaining her guiding principles and how her party would act should it return to government by winning the next general election.

Following their historic defeat in the 2024 general election, the Conservatives have been trying to rebuild and convince voters that they can be trusted again.

The Tories have faced repeated attacks from their opponents for their record in government, including on the economy, between 2010 and 2024.

Griffith is expected to say: "No-one else is coming to save our economy. Only we can inject reality, tell the hard truths and make this a country we are proud to hand on to the next generation."

He will accuse Prime Minister Andy Burnham of wanting to pursue a "socialist fever dream of the 1970s", adding the Tories want to deliver "cheaper homes, lower taxes, and less red tape".

Chancellor John Healey last week said all promises the government made would be "built on the rock of fiscal discipline" and the Budget on 28 October would "give families and businesses a bit of breathing space".

During a series of speeches on Monday, Conservative shadow ministers will continue to make their case and provide more details of their proposals.

This will include ditching environmental and energy efficiency regulations, including the future homes standard.

The Tories believe their changes could cut the cost of delivering a new home by up to Â£50,000, which in turn they expect could save money for buyers.

A single levy for developers would be implemented in place of section 106 agreements and the Community Infrastructure Levy, which fund projects in the community when building plans are progressed.

The Conservatives argue this new charge would remove delays and improve how the funds are spent to the benefit of residents.

The party has been critical of the roles of Natural England and the Environment Agency in relation to house building and flood prevention work respectively, and wants to abolish both. Their functions would be looked after by the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra).

The Extended Packaging Responsibility (EPR) scheme, which requires firms to cover the cost of collecting, recycling and disposing of packaging it produces, would also be scrapped by the Conservatives.

The party believes this would help lift a "burden" from businesses and in turn could cut the cost of the weekly shop.

On Heathrow, Griffith is expected to say the next Conservative government would do "whatever it takes to end the delays and boost capacity by backing the third runway".

Plans for expansion were scrapped by the Tory-led coalition government in 2010.

Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves championed the runway to boost the economy after Labour won power, although Burnham has refused to say whether he backs the project since becoming prime minister.

Burnham has described it as "principally... a matter for London and Londoners".

Liberal Democrat deputy leader Daisy Cooper said the Conservatives have "cemented their position as a pointless anti-growth anti-business party" by rejecting closer ties with Europe.

She added: "No-one can take anything the Conservatives say on the economy seriously given their litany of fantasy-land financial pledges."

Reform UK economy spokesman Robert Jenrick accused the Conservatives of "once again copying our policies".

He added the Tories were unable to match Reform's pledge to raise the tax-free personal allowance to Â£15,000.

News.title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk
News.content:
The UK's biggest broadband provider, BT, has agreed to rescue rival operator TalkTalk in a takeover.

The deal, which will need to be approved by the UK's competition regulator, would mark end of months of speculation over the future for TalkTalk, which has been on the brink of administration because of its debts.

TalkTalk has 1.5 million retail customers and one million wholesale customers across the UK. Some have raised concerns about the increased control BT will have over the broadband market as a result of the deal.

BT chief executive Alison Kirkby said the deal provided "a safety net for the households and businesses who rely on TalkTalk".

"TalkTalk's customers will benefit from access to the UK's best network, and the full range of market-leading products and services that BT offers," she added.

BT said the deal would provide "much needed and immediate reassurance" for TalkTalk's employees as well as its UK customers - both retail and wholesale.

"This includes vulnerable households, and connections that support critical national infrastructure providers across health, emergency services, defence, education, transport, banking and government."

News.title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas
News.content:
The number of children who were toilet-trained before starting school this year has increased significantly in a city where parents were given potty training guides with their first school offers.

York was the subject of the city-wide pilot, which also put on workshops for parents and offered special training for early years staff.

Twenty local authorities across England are now signed up to launch similar schemes to tackle the number of pupils starting school without being fully toilet-trained.

The government said the pilot's results were "encouraging", and confirmed they were committed to 75% of pupils reaching a good level of development at the end of their first year in school by 2028.

Since April this year, parents across York have been targeted via GP surgeries, pharmacies, family hubs, schools and nurseries with information and offers of support on how to potty-train their child ahead of starting school.

Potty training guides were sent out to all families across York who had a child starting reception in September - with the aim that all children could use the toilet independently by the time they started school, except those with medical issues or special educational needs.

The results from all 55 mainstream primary schools across the city, shared exclusively with BBC News, suggested there had been a 43% drop since last year in the number of children who were not fully toilet-trained when they started school.

Across York last September, 148 out of 1,364 reception pupils (11%) were recorded as not being toilet-trained when they started school. This year, that fell to 85 reception pupils out of 1,374 (6%).

Parents Natalie and Lucy, who both have daughters starting reception next year, have welcomed the extra support on offer.

News.title: The job interview question you don't have to answer
News.content:
Prepare all you like, but there is often still one job interview question that leaves you feeling uncomfortable.

While employers in the UK are within their rights to ask you how much you get paid in your current role, applicants are not obliged to tell them.

Recruiters have been encouraged to stop posing questions about salary history and, in the EU, new rules will prevent them doing so.

But in the UK, there is still a chance of it coming up, so how best should you answer?

News.title: Forced to call him 'Dad': Trial over sexual abuse in disabled care home shocks South Korea
News.content:
"I was hurting inside, so I came to tell my story."

These were Seo Mi-hyeon's first words to the police.

Seo, who has an intellectual disability, struggles to form long sentences and can only communicate through brief words and gestures. But her memories of the abuse inflicted upon her were clear.

She was one of three residents at a state-run care home in South Korea who were sexually assaulted by the home's director, in a case that has shocked the country and raised serious questions about state care for the disabled.

Earlier this month, a court in Seoul sentenced the director - who has only been identified by his surname Kim - to 15 years in prison. Kim is appealing the conviction.

The court had heard that some residents were made to call the director "Dad", which prosecutors said illustrated the unequal relationship between Kim and those in his care.

The ruling came nearly two years after Seo, who is in her 40s, first disclosed the abuse to her mother.

We have changed Seo's name and the names of another victim in this story to protect their identities.

News.title: 'Money-grab' or celebration? NFL kicks off London series
News.content:
Once upon a time, tickets for NFL games in London were like gold dust.

All 43 games have been near capacity at Wembley, Twickenham and Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

According to the NFL, its UK fanbase has swelled to 18.6 million, with 4.5 million of those considered 'avid' fans.

So in the build-up to this year's London series, why were thousands of tickets still available for two of the three games?

Next week's clash between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham sold out in hours.

But the crowd for Sunday's game at Tottenham between Washington Commanders and Indianapolis Colts only reached 60,907 after ticket prices were slashed, and large sections remain unsold for the Wembley game on 18 October.

The NFL is playing a record nine regular-season games abroad this season but 19 years after the first London game, has the NFL reached a saturation point in the UK?

News.title: Death of girl, 11, 'unexplained' after body found in park
News.content:
An 11-year-old's death is being treated as unexplained by police who say they are investigating after her body was found in a Worcestershire park.

The girl was reported missing at about 23:20 BST on Sunday and she was later found in the park near the cricket ground in Elmley Castle, near Evesham, detectives said.

Inquiries were ongoing into the circumstances surrounding her death, a West Mercia Police spokesperson said.

Nearby residents were warned by the force that there would be an increased police presence in the area.

News.title: Nine fire engines called to Glasgow city centre bar fire
News.content:
More than 40 firefighters were called to reports of fire at a bar in central Glasgow.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said it was alerted just after 14:40 and nine appliances were in attendance on Sunday evening.

Images from the scene showed parts of Renfield Street and West Regent Street were cordoned off, with a number of fire crews gathered outside both the Bistro and Maltman bars.

Crews have now left the scene. There were no reports of any casualties.

Police Scotland has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Early findings in mental health service inquiry could come within weeks
News.content:
The chair of a public inquiry into mental health deaths said she would make interim recommendations if she identified issues that "might pose an urgent risk to patient safety".

Baroness Kate Lampard is examining the deaths of more than 2,000 people who died while under the care of Essex mental health services between 2000 and the end of 2023.

The Lampard Inquiry will hear further evidence during hearings beginning on 5 October before deciding whether recommendations were needed ahead of a final report, Baroness Lampard said.

Any recommendations were expected to focus on inpatient safety, including resuscitation procedures and monitoring technology used to detect patients in distress.

News.title: Court of Appeal to hear residents' parade challenge over Drumcree dispute
News.content:
A challenge to the decision to allow a controversial Orange Order parade to go down a predominantly nationalist road is due to be heard in court later.

The deadlock over the proposed march in Portadown - opposed by residents of the Garvaghy Road - has lasted since last Sunday morning.

The stalemate has reopened what was once the most bitter parading dispute in Northern Ireland, with stand-offs in the mid-to-late 90s accompanied by riots, roadblocks and killings.

The fresh Court of Appeal application argues that the Parades Commission, the organisation that approved the march, had "materially misdirected itself" on the police assessment of the potential for disorder.

News.title: Radical change needed to cut Scottish child poverty, says charity
News.content:
Scotland is on course to miss legally-binding targets to cut child poverty "by a wide margin", according to a report from a leading social reform charity.

The Joseph Rowntree Foundation (JRF) said one in five children was in poverty and "radical change" was needed to put the Scottish government's pledges back on track.

It urged ministers to craft a "much bolder and properly-funded plan to reduce poverty" by rewiring local government, public services and the tax system.

The Scottish government said it had made great strides, with its policies keeping 100,000 children out of poverty this year, but accepted there was more to do.

In 2017, MSPs passed a law requiring ministers to hit four targets, external, including pushing the share of children in relative poverty below 10% by 2030.

But the JRF's Poverty in Scotland report, external found the figure remained stubbornly high, averaging 21% from 2022 to 2025. The UK average is 28%.

Relative poverty means a household has disposable income after housing costs below 60% of the UK median, adjusted for family size and composition.

Overall, the report concluded, 940,000 people in Scotland were in relative poverty â 17% of the population.

News.title: Model boats banned from lake over speed fears
News.content:
People with model boats have been banned from using a park's lake, unless they are taking part in a session run by a local boat club.

Stevenage Borough Council said the sign was erected at Fairlands Valley Park, external to stop people outside of the club from "using high-powered model boats" on Millennium Lake.

Ian Searle, secretary of Stevenage Model Boat Club, said there were model boats you can buy off the shelf that travel at speeds of 60-70mph (up to 112km/h).

"Those without experience, who are generally not insured, can try them out on the lake which is likely to cause an accident," he said.

Searle said restrictions were put on members a few years ago, with boats with internal combustion engines banned.

"The sign by Millennium Lake was aimed at other people, just to take away the free for all for everyone else," he said.

News.title: Matthew Rhys takes Best Actor at Bafta Cymru for performance in Netflix thriller
News.content:
Matthew Rhys has continued his fine form this awards season after being announced as the Best Actor at the Bafta Cymru Awards ceremony.

The actor made history last month when he became the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night at the Emmy's.

Presenter Carol Vorderman said she was "humbled and excited" to receive an award for outstanding contribution, while Lauren Evans took home an award for her contribution to the film I Swear.

Lee Walters, Bafta Cymru chair, congratulated the nominees last month and said "each is a testament to the creativity, skill and dedication of the people working across Wales' screen industries, both in front of and behind the camera".

Rhys was presented the award at the ICC Wales, in Newport, where the event has been held since 2024.

His performance in The Beast in Me earned him his second Bafta Cymru, 29 years after his first for his role in the Welsh-language film Bydd yn Wro, or Be Brave.

Gabrielle Creevy won her second Best Actress award and Y Crwydryn took home the Single Documentary award, with Rhys Edwards winning Director Factual for the same show.

Mari Grug won her first Bafta Cymru award for presenter in Mari Grug: Yn dydd Ar Y Tro.

Elsewhere, Y Golau: Dwr won two awards and Matthew Barry won Best Writer for The Guest.

Amour a Mynydd won the Entertainment Programme award and Stori'r Iaith received the Factual Series award.

Burton won the Feature/Television Film award and the Short Film award was won by Gofod Ymennydd â Brain Space and the Children's Programme went to Itopia.

In total, 17 awards were presented across the evening as well as two Bafta Outstanding Contribution awards.

News.title: Rugby league fans in Wakefield for bus parade
News.content:
Thousands of rugby league fans turned out to watch an open-top bus parade, after Wakefield Trinity were crowned Super League champions.

Trinity beat Warrington Wolves 23-10 in Saturday's Grand Final at Old Trafford - their first title win since 1968, long before Super League was established.

To celebrate the victory, two buses, carrying players and staff, travelled from the club's ground at Belle Vue to Wakefield Town Hall for a civic reception.

Fullback Max Jowitt, who has made 188 appearances for Trinity and scored three goals in the final, said the parade had been an "unbelievable" experience.

"The fans have been unbelievable, the city is unbelievable and the trophy's unbelievable," he said.

News.title: Erling Haaland sparks huge injury concern as Portugal win without Cristiano Ronaldo

Title holders Portugal maintained their 100 per cent record in the Nations League with a 2-1 ​home win over Norway on Sunday to seal a place in the March quarter-finals and shift the focus further away from Cristiano Ronaldo's abrupt exit from the squad last week.

But Erling Haaland sparked concern for Norway and Manchester City by requesting he be substituted in the 67th minute of the tie, and limped off the pitch.

Portugal’s win was soured by a red card for Francisco Conceicao four minutes from time; he gave the referee a cynical thumbs ‌up after receiving a yellow card and was immediately handed his ‌marching orders.

Goncalo Ramos netted 11 minutes from time to ensure Portugal secured a top-two finish in Group A4 as they moved six points ahead of second-placed Denmark, who won 1-0 at Wales.

The Netherlands took over at the top of Group A2, after beating Serbia 2-1 in Eindhoven, but only on goal difference from Greece, who held on grimly for a goalless draw at home to Germany in Thessaloniki.

Portugal were still under a cloud from Ronaldo’s dispute with coach Jorge Jesus, although they were triumphant without him in Denmark last Thursday after he walked out on the squad, and continued their winning ways in Porto on Sunday.

Norway took the lead in the 36th minute from centre-back Kristoffer Ajer, who hit a dipping half-volley from the edge of ⁠the box.

But if that effort was sumptuous, Joao Cancelo’s thrashing effort to equalise two minutes later ​was even ⁠more awe-inspiring. Ramos’ winner came off his calf after Joao Felix had headed across goal for him to score.

In Group D2, Abdulakh ‌Khaybulayev’s first-half goal was enough ​to send Azerbaijan top of the standings with a 1-0 ‌win over previously unbeaten Lithuania, while veteran Teddy ​Teuma came on as a second-half substitute to hand Malta a 1-0 home win over Andorra in Group D1.

Wales goalkeeper Danny Ward made several key saves to keep Denmark at bay in Cardiff, but then conceded a penalty with a foul on Gustav Isaksen, allowing Rasmus Hojlund to tuck away a 75th-minute penalty to win their tie.

open image in gallery Haaland requested to come off and limped off the pitch in Porto ( AP )

The Netherlands, with captain Virgil van Dijk ⁠celebrating a 100th cap, went ahead against Serbia when Teun Koopmeiners’s 31st-minute freekick evaded all in the penalty area and crept into the corner.

But the visitors were level within four minutes as Aleksa Terzic crossed for teenager Mihajlo Cvetkovic to rise over Koopmeiners and head in his first international goal.

It took until the 72nd minute to go back ahead when Denzel Dumfries’ low cross was turned back across the goal by Tijjani Reijnders, sliding in at the far post, and tapped in by Joshua Zirkzee, who received a late ‌call-up to the Dutch squad last week.

Germany dominated against Greece but Jurgen Klopp’s inexperienced side could not find the net, and they have won only one of their first four games under the new coach.

Austria needed a late equaliser ⁠to draw 1-1 at Kosovo but still have a three-point lead at the top of Group ⁠B3 after the Republic of Ireland and Israel drew 1-1 behind closed doors in the Serbian town of Backa Topola.

Families across England could receive expanded assistance to toilet train their young children before they enter primary school.

Dozens of local authorities may adopt a trial pioneered by the City of York Council, which distributed potty training guidance to 1,700 households alongside primary school place allocation letters in April.

Project organisers noted that fewer pupils in York entered reception without toilet training last month compared to the previous intake, following the targeted rollout.

It comes as teacher survey data from charity Kindred Squared indicated that roughly a quarter of children entering reception in 2025 were not toilet trained.

The Government is attempting to raise the proportion of young pupils arriving at reception "school ready".

Financed by Kindred Squared, the York initiative comprised parent workshops, teacher training, and leaflets made available at libraries and GP practices to help families train their four-year-olds.

Overall, 55 mainstream state primary schools in York were asked to compare the number of children who were not toilet trained when they started school in September 2025 with the number this September.

open image in gallery A survey of teachers by charity Kindred Squared suggested around one in four children who started reception in 2025 were not toilet trained ( Getty/iStock )

There has been a 42 per cent decrease in the proportion of children starting school not toilet trained in York, the results from the pilot suggest.

Around 20 councils in England are now looking to use the same blueprint as York including Suffolk, North Lincolnshire, Hampshire, Rotherham, Halton, and the London Borough of Redbridge and Solihull.

Gail Brown, chief executive of Ebor Academy Trust, which had six schools included in the York pilot, said: “I think that there’s been a very clear expectation across the whole city that children who start school, where possible, will start toilet trained.”

She added: “It was very much about supporting parents, not blaming parents.”

Jo Mould, a teacher at Robert Wilkinson Primary Academy in York, one of the schools which took part in the pilot, said: “I think the biggest impact for us has been that we don’t have to spend so much time changing children now.

“For safeguarding reasons it took two people to change a child and that meant taking those two members of staff out of the classroom to go and change the children.

“Obviously, the higher the number of children in nappies, or who were having toilet accidents, that increases that amount of time away from the other children.

“So in terms of that huge reduction, it means that the adults now can spend far more time in the classroom and in the areas with the children.”

open image in gallery The government is pushing to increase the proportion of children starting reception 'school ready' ( AFP/Getty )

She added: “I think in terms of educational outcomes, it is very much a successful initiative.”

Felicity Gillespie, chief executive of Kindred Squared, said: “We know from our annual school readiness surveys that, on average, teachers have been losing the equivalent of a day a week of teaching time helping children who are not able to go to the toilet themselves.

“We also know parents and carers have been calling for clear and concise advice, and this just shows that when the best resources are really targeted, everyone benefits.

“No wonder dozens of other councils are now showing interest in repeating York’s pioneering project around the country.”

Paul Waugh, minister for early education, said: “Toilet training can be one of the biggest milestones in a child’s early years, so it’s encouraging to see this pilot helping more children develop the confidence and independence they need before starting school.

“When children are supported to take these important steps early, it can make a real difference to how they settle in, make friends and start learning.”

Anti-migrant protesters gathered in a seaside town as more than 100 migrants arrived in a dinghy after crossing the English Channel from France on Sunday.

A number of people were seen arriving at a marina in Gosport, having been transported aboard two RNLI boats late on Sunday evening.

The dinghy, which carried 149 migrants, appeared to have set off from near the Utah Beach area of Normandy on Sunday morning. This marks the third such crossing from the area in the space of a month.

Around 100 anti-migrant demonstrators gathered near Haslar Marina in Gosport following reports that authorities were preparing for the arrival of the vessel.

The dinghy was shadowed by French rescue vessels until it entered English waters, where it was met by RNLI boats, according to ship tracking data. The Home Office confirmed the migrants would be processed in Kent after their arrival in Gosport.

Footage capturing scenes near Gosport’s Haslar Marina shows crowds gathered around police vans chanting “shame on you” and “deport the lot”. While the atmosphere was said to be mostly peaceful, there were reports of flares being set off and some scuffles with police.

The demonstration follows heightened scrutiny over migrant arrivals to the UK, where similar anti-immigration protests have flared up across coastal towns including Dover and Portsmouth.

open image in gallery Anti-immigrant demonstrations have broken out across the coastal town of Gosport ( Getty )

A government spokesperson said: “The Border Security Command works around the clock to protect our border. We have established contingency plans to make sure we can securely disembark, check and process all small boat arrivals.

“Migrants will be transported to short term holding facilities in Kent where they will be processed as normal and undergo stringent health, security and biometric checks.”

On Sunday, Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said it had deployed officers to Gosport to “support our partners in the event of an emergency at sea”.

Earlier on Sunday, the Reform leader of Hampshire council George Madgwick, said on X:“I hate to report that Gosport is the planned landing point for today’s migrant boat.

open image in gallery The dinghy was being shadowed by French rescue vessels until it was met by the RNLI boats in English waters, according to ship tracking data ( Getty )

“This is an absolute shambles,” he said, “But there is hope. Last time they planned to dock there they changed course. Let’s hope they do the same today.

“If you’re heading there stay peaceful and calm.”

Similar scenes unfolded in Gosport last month when protesters gathered expecting a landing after coaches and ambulances were spotted nearby.

On that occasion, the passengers – 51 migrants who refused help from the French coastguard, arrived in Dover after being transferred to Border Security Command boats.

A government spokesperson said: “The Border Security Command works around the clock to monitor the Channel and protect our border. It is vital we continue to detain, check and process every small boat arrival.”

open image in gallery Demonstrators are hoping to deter the arrival of a vessel understood to be hosting immigrants ( PA Wire )

The provisional total for Channel crossings this year is 19,451.

This is down 43 per cent on this time last year and 23 per cent below the figure at this stage in 2024.

Authorities have since placed a dispersal order under Section 34 of the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 to cover the town of Gosport.

This order is in place until 7am on Tuesday, 6 October. Those who refuse to comply with the order are committing a criminal offence and are liable for arrest.
