Six people aboard a medical transport plane that went missing off the coast of Massachusetts are presumed to be dead, the aircraft's operator said.

The Gulfstream G100 lost contact with air traffic control in the early hours of Saturday and the US coast guard ended its search for survivors on Sunday evening in the waters off Nantucket island.

Latitude Air Ambulance, the Canadian company that operated the flight, said soon afterwards that all six people on board were presumed dead.

“We must now face the heartbreaking reality that the four members of our Latitude team, our patient and the patient's family escort, who were aboard Heartbeat 104, are presumed to have died,” the company said in a statement. "Our thoughts are first and foremost with their families, loved ones, friends, and colleagues."

The company's president described it as “an unimaginable loss for our Latitude family and for everyone who loved the six people aboard Heartbeat 104”.

“Our focus now is on supporting their families, supporting our people and assisting the authorities,” Peter Byl said.

There were four Canadians and two Bermudians on board.

Canada's transport minister, Steven MacKinnon, said Transport Canada was working with authorities on the search and rescue effort.

Clarence Togeretz, Latitude's director of flight operations, told CBC News that two pilots and two medical staff, all Canadian, had flown to Bermuda to collect a patient and a relative.

The jet left Bermuda’s LF Wade International Airport at 11.40pm local time on Friday, according to FlightAware flight data, and was due to land at Boston's Logan International Airport at 1.30am EDT. The Federal Aviation Administration lost contact with it just after 1am.

Authorities found a debris field on Saturday evening, which was confirmed to be from the aircraft.

FlightAware's tracker showed the plane dropped sharply from about 7,300m to 3,300m before its communications went dark.

Air traffic control audio posted by LiveATC captured the flight's final exchanges.

"Roger, you said you’re coming in blind. Is that what you said?" a controller asked the pilot, whose reply was difficult to hear on the recording.

The Boston Globe reported that the controller then said: "You're coming in a little weak, so I didn't hear what your response was, if you were declaring an emergency or not." The controller later confirmed the pilot had declared an emergency.

Just after 1am EDT, an area fire dispatcher asked emergency crews to prepare to meet a plane with an "electrical issue", the BBC reported. The dispatcher later said "the aircraft has lost radio and radar".

The National Transportation Safety Board said on Saturday morning it was gathering information and had no further update.

Latitude said that it would continue to cooperate with authorities during ongoing recovery efforts and investigations.

"Determining the circumstances and cause of an aviation accident is a careful and methodical process, and we will not speculate about what occurred," the company said.

Brazil’s presidential election will go to the second round after far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro narrowly outpolled incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva but failed to secure the majority needed to avoid a runoff.

Mr Bolsonaro took an early lead as the South American nation began reporting results on Sunday afternoon in the first round of a tight election, following a campaign dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling.

The field of 13 candidates had been led by two clear frontrunners – Mr Lula da Silva, 80, who was seeking a fourth term, and Flavio, the 45-year-old son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.

With 99.9 per cent of the votes counted, Mr Bolsonaro had won 47 per cent, compared with 45.1 per cent for the incumbent. Mr Bolsonaro received 56.1m votes to Mr Lula da Silva’s 53.8m.

They will now contest a 25 October runoff.

Early results had shown southern states leaning towards Mr Bolsonaro reporting faster, while votes from Mr Lula da Silva’s northeast stronghold were tallied slower.

Mr Bolsonaro-aligned politicians won several key races, including three seats for members of his family. As many as 34 of the 54 newly elected senators are from the right or the far-right.

Mr Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party emerged with the largest number of governors, senators and federal deputies elected so far, putting it in a strong position to wield influence in Congress.

The runoff will determine whether Brazil joins a wider wave of electoral gains across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US president Donald Trump, or whether Mr Lula da Silva will secure another term despite tensions between his government and Washington over trade and security.

Despite growing worries over Brazil's public finances and sluggish economic growth, the campaign ⁠had offered meagre policy debate, as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates.

Addressing his supporters, Mr Bolsonaro said that the result pointed to “the end of an era” for the ruling Workers’ party.

“Lula has fought seven presidential elections. He’s worried about power. I am worried about the future of Brazil,” he said.

open image in gallery Supporters of Brazil's president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva react after the first results of the presidential election in Sao Paulo, Brazil, on 4 October 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

While polls right up until Saturday showed ​Mr Lula da Silva would ⁠likely lead the first round but not avoid a runoff, Mr Bolsonaro told journalists earlier in Rio de Janeiro he was confident he could win the presidency in the first round, citing voters’ frustration with his chief opponent.

He was counting on "a protest vote from people who would otherwise vote for another candidate but are opposed to Lula", he said. "I hope it’s enough to secure a victory in the ⁠first round."

Thaise Lima, a 41-year-old lawyer on her way to vote in Sao Paulo, said her main goal was to get the Workers' Party out of office.

"I don't think Flavio is the best candidate, ​but I might decide to ⁠vote for him in the next few minutes," she said, adding that she ‌wished psychiatrist and author Augusto Cury were a more viable candidate.

Fernando Tempel, 49, a management consultant, told Reuters he was voting for Mr Bolsonaro despite initially planning to vote for Romeu Zema, the former governor of Minas Gerais state.

open image in gallery Supporters of Brazil's presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro react as they wait for the first results in Porto Alegre on 4 October 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

On the other hand, Mr Lula da Silva’s allies had warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognise election results if he won, pointing to an aborted effort to send US officials to Brazil.

"What is at stake ‌is the future of Brazil," the president said earlier after voting in Sao Bernardo do Campo, in Sao Paulo state.

Mr Trump has not formally ‌endorsed a candidate, though he had hosted Mr Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly.

Speaking after the results, the incumbent president said: “We have just had a lesson in Brazilian democracy. The result is often unexpected. We can never get everything we want. I confess to you that I was convinced I was going to win the election in the first round. But we have a second round.”

“From tomorrow we will launch a new campaign,” he added, “and in a campaign with only two candidates we will be able to show the difference between our proposals for Brazil.”

open image in gallery Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva addresses supporters in Sao Paulo, Brazil, on 4 October 2026 ( Reuters )

Cristiano, 34, a doctor in Brasilia who voted for the president and preferred to withhold his surname told Reuters: “I'm a little worried about everything that's been happening recently, including internationally. I feel this election has had a lot of outside influence, more than in previous elections.”

"We are confident in our President Lula, who will fight for national sovereignty," said Pedro Palacio, 45, who was voting in Brasilia alongside his wife, Andreia, and their two sons and two dogs, all of whom wore ⁠outfits supporting the president.

Earlier, Brazil's electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques said in a press conference that “teams monitoring international risks have not identified any risks whatsoever”.

It was reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials had briefed a French and German delegation on alleged US and Russian interference before the election. The US has rejected claims of interference in Brazil's affairs.

open image in gallery Flavio Bolsonaro speaks to the press after the votes are tallied in Brasilia, Brazil, on 4 October 2026 ( Getty )

Despite falling inequality and unemployment, Mr Lula da Silva has struggled to win over voters grappling with high living costs, heavy household debt and the threat of street crime and more pervasive gang activity.

Mr Bolsonaro had sought to capitalise on cost-of-living concerns, while Mr Lula da Silva had moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families.

Rising spending and public debt above 82 per cent of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil's next president will need to address. The government lowered its economic growth forecasts for this year and next to 2.0 per cent and 2.3 per cent respectively.

"I voted for Brazil to start growing again," said Marciano de Souza e Silva, a 52-year-old public servant in Brasilia and former Workers’ Party voter who ‌moved right, voting for Jair Bolsonaro in 2018 and 2022 and Flavio on Sunday.

"The best social program is one that encourages people to start businesses, to actually produce real wealth," he said.

open image in gallery Supporters of Flavio Bolsonaro await the first results of the election in Porto Alegre on 4 October 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

Overshadowing the policy debate, a scandal surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master has engulfed much of Brazil's political class and renewed public anger over corruption.

Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier ‌this year and accused of a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme. The investigation has probed the banker's ties to ⁠figures from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to Mr Bolsonaro, who is being investigated for money laundering tied to the case by the federal police.

The candidate has denied any wrongdoing, although ⁠he confirmed raising millions of dollars from Vorcaro to make a movie about his father.

The banker's connections to Mr Moraes, widely perceived as an ally of the president, plunged the court into crisis a month before the vote, creating fresh problems for the president. Mr Moraes has said the case against him is ‌politically motivated for his role in the conviction of the elder ​Bolsonaro.

Congress has gained greater influence in Brazilian politics since the impeachment of ​former president Dilma Rousseff, an ally of Mr Lula da Silva, in 2016, raising the stakes of those legislative races.

The pilot who allegedly attempted to seize control of an Israel-bound Flydubai flight and crash it likely acted alone, according to an initial investigation.

Multiple American and Israeli officials briefed on the investigation said it appeared that the co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, 29, was a “lone wolf” rather than a member of an organisation or foreign government, CBS and NBC News reported.

Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu had claimed last week the pilot “underwent Islamist radical indoctrination” and Israeli officials said they were looking into his links with terrorist organisations and enemy states.

Australian authorities are also looking into his links to the country. Confirming the investigation, an Australian ⁠Federal Police spokesperson said they would provide an update “at ​an appropriate time”.

The Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology said he was enrolled at the school for a time, but did not complete his engineering qualification, the Associated Press reported.

The pilot allegedly visited extremist websites in Australia, reported Financial Times, citing two sources familiar with the probe. The outlet reported that the intelligence services of the country also held a file on him.

open image in gallery Dubai’s crown prince, Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum, meets Smit Machchhar, captain of the Flydubai flight who was stabbed by his colleague ( Reuters )

In the UK, Buckinghamshire New University previously confirmed that Mr Hammami had done a distance-learning course in aviation management at the institution.

Mr Hammami allegedly grabbed an emergency axe and slashed Smit Machchhar, the captain of the Flydubai aircraft, with the struggle sending the Boeing 737 Max into a sudden 17,000ft plunge.

Despite sustaining severe injuries, Mr Machchhar said he was able to unlock the flight deck door, allowing passengers to force their way inside, subdue Mr Hammami, and stabilise the plane before making an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

open image in gallery Yaniv Hayun was one of the passengers who reportedly helped incapacitate the attacker on the Flydubai flight ( Reuters )

Amid increasing scrutiny of security lapses that led to the incident, Mr Netanyahu told the head of the National Security Council to appoint an examiner to review “all security aspects regarding foreign civil aviation to Israel”.

Regional officials said the Omani pilot was barred from flying in his own country due to concerns over his extremist views. It was also unclear how a citizen of Oman, a country with no diplomatic ties with Israel, was allowed to fly a planeload of Israelis to Tel Aviv.

The officials also said authorities in the UAE had shared a list of passengers and crew, including their nationalities, with Israel ahead of the flight, raising questions about how the alleged attacker evaded detection. Israel had not raised red flags for any passenger or member of the crew, said the officials.

Shin Bet, Israel’s domestic security agency, said the transportation ministry was responsible for vetting passenger lists from foreign flights. Transportation minister Miri Regev said the security agencies were responsible for flight security and that her ministry wasn’t given a list of passengers or any warnings.

Sharing the list is standard aviation procedure. But the head of aviation security at the transportation ministry, Dvir Rubenstien, told Army Radio the ministry relied on local security checks and didn’t have the tools or the ability to run checks on each passenger on every flight.

News.title: Jibulu emerges as England World Cup bolter in Sale defeat of Saracens
News.content:
Could Nathan Jibulu, the Sale Sharks hooker, emerge as a bolter for England’s World Cup squad? With Steve Borthwick, the England head coach, watching from the stands, the 23-year-old produced the kind of “wrecking-ball” performance in this surprise victory for the North West side that suggested he is on course to do so.

After their tame defeat by Bristol Bears in the opening round, few had predicted that Alex Sanderson’s side had much hope against Saracens, who were looking to back up their impressive win at Welford Road last weekend. But Jibulu’s powerhouse display on either side of the ball typified their stout and physical resistance, backed up by a masterly display by George Ford.

Given the age and injury profile of England hookers Jamie George and Luke Cowan-Dickie, who both missed this contest, and the fact that Theo Dan has yet to make a forceful challenge for the position in the national side, Sanderson is in no doubt that Jibulu has the X factor required to break into Borthwick’s squad this season.

“This is the player that any time you watch him play, he impacts – he takes metres either side of the ball – and we knew that he had that in him,” Sanderson said.

“It shows he’s of international class. He nailed his line-outs, on the back of that he was a wrecking-ball runner causing havoc around the field.

“This is the person that we knew, this is the player that we knew we had in him. It could be the year where he explodes onto the international scene. I hope it is, but it’s early days.

“He’s that quality, he’s that kind of an athlete. You can get away with being fast and skilful in the Prem, but it’s another level again in terms of the power that’s required at international level. And he’s got that ability, he’s immensely strong.”

Borthwick will have left the StoneX Stadium on Sunday evening with a full notebook. Ben Bamber, Sale’s 6ft 9ins lock, has also been attracting his interest and it was Bamber who crossed for the decisive try, Sale’s third, hitting a great line off Ford to finish like an outside centre.

News.title: Brilliant Hamilton storms to podium despite another Ferrari blunder
News.content:
One of the big talking points heading into the weekend has been the cooling vests drivers wear under their overalls (as opposed to the jacket-like ones they wear when they’re out of their cars). Russell told us in our Brits media session on Thursday that Mercedes had decided to forego the vests here, since the technology was not yet refined. The system works by pumping a coolant through thin tubes stitched into the vest.

Drivers have complained that the connecting valve to the pump, which was originally placed on the side of the vest, proved uncomfortable when combined with the high G-forces experienced in an F1 car. On some vests the connector has been moved to find a more comfortable position, but the thick material and tubing have also proved cumbersome under the driver’s fireproof overalls. There are also concerns over the reliability of some systems and the possibility that a failure will mean the vest will have the opposite effect and work as a heat insulator.preferring to spend that money instead on car upgrades. The money to develop the vests comes out of the budget cap.

But Russell added that the FIA should make the tech mandatory and develop it themselves, describing this race as like being in a “sauna”.The Briton’s comments prompted a sarcastic response from Verstappen - who doesn’t wear the vests either, out of choice - who said Russell “shouldn’t make a fuss”.

“I don’t need it,” Verstappen said. “Maybe I suffer a bit less from the heat.. I find a Finnish sauna at 85 degrees a lot hotter... You shouldn’t make a fuss. Yes, it is hot, but that’s part of it. You have to train for that.”

The Dutchman added: “When I was 18, I had a bit more trouble with these conditions. But after that, I started training more in the heat, such as in the sauna and a steam room, so that I can handle the sweating better and the fact that your head gets very hot. Maybe I should take him (Russell) to the sauna a few times.”

These two have history, of course. They’ve sniped at each other for years. In 2024, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, it reached a peak when Verstappen described Russell as being “two-faced” and said he had lost all respect for him. Russell responded by saying Verstappen was “a bully”. Earlier this year, the Mercedes driver said Verstappen could always retire from the sport and drive sports cars if he didn’t like the regs.

News.title: Rees-Zammit taunts Pollock as Bristol outplay Northampton
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Bristol Bears vs Northampton Saints from the Gallagher Prem, with both teams looking to build on winning starts following the opening weekend of action.

Last season’s champions Northampton kicked off their title defence with an emphatic 59-26 victory over a new-look Newcastle Red Bulls outfit at Franklin’s Gardens.

While Henry Pollock’s new cornrow hairstyle was the centre of attention at kick-off, the limelight was soon stolen by Tommy Freeman and James Pater, who both notched hat-tricks for Phil Dowson’s side.

Of 19-year-old full-back Pater, who starts on the bench today, Dowson said afterwards: “He doesn’t let the occasion get to him. He has an incredible skill set, great speed and ability to manoeuvre away from defenders.”

Bristol, meanwhile, began their season with an impressive 34-24 victory away at Sale Sharks, with Pat Lam’s side ensuring Courtney Lawes’s return to the English game was a disappointing one.

Louis Rees-Zammit was operating in his favoured wing position and got Bristol off to a strong start with two tries in the opening 23 minutes, offering Lam hope of a fruitful campaign from the Welshman.

“When you look at our wingers in the past, they scored a lot of tries and Louis is a world-class finisher,” the Bristol director of rugby said. “You get the ball to him in space and you create the opportunity, there’s a good chance he’ll finish it.”

Northampton will be hoping for a repeat of the meeting between the sides at Franklin Gardens in May when they thumped Bristol 94-33, but they have not won at Ashton Gate since 2021.

Both teams have made a pair of changes following their opening-weekend victories, with England international Ellis Genge among the players to drop out after spraining his wrist against Sale.

News.title: Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade
News.content:
We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

News.title: Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying
News.content:
The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

News.title: Bath complete revenge mission on Exeter despite imperious Feyi-Waboso
News.content:
Bath held off a furious comeback from Exeter, led by the irrepressible Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, to avenge their Gallagher Prem semi-final defeat here in June.

It felt as if lightning might strike Bath twice. Once again Exeter overturned a 26-10 half-time deficit, to manufacture a second-half lead thanks to a pair of blistering finishes by Feyi-Waboso. Four months ago, Bath failed to take a drop goal in the closing stages, but this time with the reassuring presence of Finn Russell at fly-half, they kept their cool.

The Scotland playmaker twice sent penalties deep into the Exeter 22 from where Stephen Varney conceded a yellow card and penalty try before Bath replacement Ted Hill powered through a thicket of Exeter tacklers.

“Finn is one of the best 10s in the world and I thought he had a very good game,” Johann van Graan, the Bath head of rugby, said. “His decision making is above most players in the world and I thought that came through tonight.”

Despite the appearance of yet another high-scoring shoot-out, both teams defended with real bite, although Bath struggled to lay a finger on Feyi-Waboso who ended up in a scrap with a fan in the stands here when he was a spectator in May. He exacted a measure of revenge beating eight defenders and carried for 132 metres.

“Manny still needs game time,” Rob Baxter, the Exeter director of rugby, said. “When he’s on the ball, you see something incredible, but it is his ability to get on the ball again. He is just getting his game minutes and match fitness up.”

News.title: FTSE 100 tumbles amid bond market sell-off
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. House prices fell unexpectedly last month as mortgage borrowers prepare for a jump in interest rates.

Typical property values declined by 0.2pc during September, reversing 0.2pc growth in August, according to the Nationwide house price index.

The figure was much worse than analysts had forecasts, with most expecting prices to remain steady.

Over the course of the year to September, the rate of house price growth halved from 1.6pc to 0.8pc, which was the weakest rate since December 2025.

The value of the average home has fallen to £274,251 over concerns the Bank of England is on the cusp of raising interest rates, making borrowing more expensive for mortgage holders.

Money markets indicate there is an 84pc chance policymakers will raise rates from 3.75pc to 4pc in November in an effort to bring down inflation caused by the Iran war energy shock.

Robert Gardner, chief economist at Nationwide, said:“Market activity and house prices have remained subdued in recent months, in part reflecting the uncertain economic backdrop.

“Geopolitical tensions remain high, with the conflict in the Middle East exerting upward pressure on energy prices, fanning inflation concerns.

“This in turn has led to mounting financial market expectations of Bank Rate increases, which has maintained upward pressure on the market interest rates which underpin mortgage pricing.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Polanski urges Miliband to block Rosebank oil field over Israel links | Green leader claims North Sea project is a test of Foreign Secretary’s proposed sanctions regime

2) Netherlands ditches wealth tax over exodus fears | Dutch PM scraps plan to target paper profits, instead introducing a more convention capital gains levy

3) Diesel crisis deepens as UK’s biggest refinery shuts for 10 weeks | Fears of squeeze on supplies after fuel costs rise higher than £2 per litre

4) Debt-ridden France branded ‘the new sick man of Europe’ | Investors hope the European Central Bank sees the struggling country as ‘too big to fail’

5) Britain blocks foreign lawyers after surge in south Asian applicants | Bar Standards Board halts scheme unless candidates have already secured a position

What happened overnight

The cost of government borrowing edged higher in Asia as soaring energy costs sparked inflation fears.

Bond yields, a benchmark for what governments pay to borrow money, surged in September as investors brace for a period where interest rates stay higher for ​longer.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes hit 5.31pc, the ‌highest level since mid-June 2007. The 10-year yield gained 87 basis points in the July-September quarter, the biggest quarterly rise since 1994.

Market focus has been on how long US Treasury yields stay above the psychologically important 5pc level, while some investors even contemplate the possibility of yields breaching 6pc.

Yields in Japan have climbed to multi-decade highs too, while those in Germany, France and Britain have all hit 17 to 19 year peaks.

On Thursday, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government ​bond yield was at 3.11pc, not far from the 30-year high it hit last week.

Asian technology stocks rose after a boost from AI chipmaker Micron, ​although US bonds struggled ‌after their sharpest quarterly sell-off in more than three decades as inflation risks from elevated energy prices linger.

Stalling peace talks between the US and Iran to end the seven-month-long war in the Middle East have kept crude prices aloft.Brent futures surged 42pc in the July-September quarter.

The high-stakes earnings from Micron, a key supplier to AI bellwether Nvidia, signalled strong demand for AI memory chips, with financial commitments under long-term supply agreements at $32 billion, up from $22 billion in June.

That helped push tech-heavy stock markets in Asia higher. Japan’s Nikkei jumped over 3pc, and South Korea’s Kospi reversed earlier losses to gain 1.7pc. Taiwan’s stock benchmark was 0.8pc higher.

News.title: Chewing tobacco killed 250,000 people in one year, study shows
News.content:
Chewing tobacco killed around a quarter of a million people in 2023, with use of the product remaining stubbornly high, according to research.

The smokeless tobacco, which is placed between the cheek and lower gum, is particularly popular in south Asia. It is flavoured and sometimes sweetened, and users often spit out unwanted juices while chewing. It is often viewed as safer than smoking but it is a major cause of stroke, as well as head and neck cancer.

Chewing tobacco is different to white snus or nicotine pouches, which contain no tobacco. These white pouches are also made up of flavourings and sometimes sweeteners, and deliver a hit of nicotine through the lining of the mouth.

Despite a successful fight against smoking over the last few decades, rates of chewing tobacco use have fallen little and it has often been overlooked in tobacco control efforts, researchers point out. In a study published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in the US estimate that 241 million people aged 15 years and older used chewing tobacco in 2023.

Researchers looked at data on use in 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 and found that there was no significant decrease in the number of users of chewing tobacco over that period. And in 24 countries there was a significant uptick in the number of people using the product. Researchers estimate that about one in five men and one in 10 women in south Asia chewed tobacco in 2023.

Bangladesh has seen the biggest increase in the number of people using the product with 15 million new users between 1990 and 2023. Nepal, Madagascar and Yemen also saw increases in the number of users.

In India 105 million people chew tobacco regularly, accounting for just over two thirds of users globally. Historically, Indians would chew paan, tobacco in its raw form which was mixed with betel leaf and areca nut, a mild stimulant. But the use of chewing tobacco exploded in the 1980s when manufacturers began grinding these into a powder and selling them in packets known as gutkha. This was banned in 2012 but is still widely available. Chewing tobacco is also popular in Pakistan, China and Vietnam.

Sports.title: Man City women’s team targeted with ‘inappropriate’ abuse after guilty verdict as Maresca’s stars warned they face same
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY stars have been warned they will be in the firing line everywhere — after the Prem’s guilty verdict.

Ex-City defender Nedum Onuoha revealed the women’s team were targeted with “inappropriate” abuse as they arrived at a London hotel ten days ago.



That was as news leaked that City had been found guilty of widespread breaches of Prem financial rules.

Onuoha has family who work with the women’s team and says it was a tough night ahead of facing Charlton on September 26.



He feels the appeal and potential sanctions hanging over the Etihad makes it “ten times harder” for players.

Onuoha said: “The news broke as the women’s team were on the way to London.



“I know this from people who travelled with them — they were shocked, they weren’t expecting it.

“They got to Euston and there was a bus there with a City badge on.

“When they arrived at the hotel, some of the stuff being said, to call it inappropriate would be an understatement.

“There are people in the set-up who have had nothing to do with what this is all about.



“But they are having to live with that, it comes as a consequence. Their job is ten times harder.

“Every time they wear that kit, travel on that bus, people are going to want to ask about it.”

Onuoha, 39, came through City’s academy and made 100-plus appearances for the club.

From there he moved to QPR and played against City as Sergio Aguero scored THAT goal to win the Etihad club the title back in 2012.



Onuoha added: “The most difficult part is not knowing what will happen.

“With every day that passes, you hear more. It was already the biggest story in the history of the Premier League.

“But now you’re hearing Andy Burnham, treasuries, tax, investments. It’s turned geopolitical.”

City’s squad is due back in training by Thursday.

Enzo Maresca has to get them ready for nine games in four weeks – starting with a daunting trip to Anfield on Sunday.



Meetings are planned with police and the authorities this week to ensure the fixture passes off smoothly.

JUNINHO rolled back the years to score on his Middlesbrough return as a sold-out crowd witnessed his final goal at the Riverside.

The Brazilian World Cup winner was back on Teesside to play on his former stomping ground for a special legacy game to mark the Championship club’s 150th anniversary.



And ‘The Little Fella’ – who enjoyed three spells as a player for Boro – gave his adoring public the moment they had been waiting for when he slotted home a penalty to send fans wild.

Juninho, 53, was not the only star name in town for the clash, as legendary names young and old took the pitch.





The icon’s former team-mate Fabrizio Ravanelli, 57, was back too. The pair fired the team to both domestic cup finals for the first time during that rollercoaster 1996/97 season which ended in relegation.

Unfortunately the deadly Italian striker, nicknamed the ‘White Feather’ and who scored 31 times during that epic campaign three decades ago, was unable to play, meaning he had to watch on enviously as his old partner stole the headlines.

Ravanelli told Sun Sport: “It was very lucky for Juninho that I wasn’t on the pitch or I’d have taken the penalty!”

Juninho said: “I think that’ll be the last time [I score]. When you get over 50 it’s not easy to play football. But I hope to be back here at the end of the season to commemorate the team’s promotion.



“The penalty… we’ll not say much about that! It doesn’t matter about the score. It matters who was here and who came to enjoy the day and to see all the faces of the old players. To see the full stadium once again, it means a lot for all of us.”

Boro shocked the football world when Bryan Robson signed Juninho in 1995. That was the first of his three stints on Teesside for Juninho, who is widely-regarded as Boro’s greatest player.

The beauty, from Solihull, West Mids, had been scouted as a model aged just 13.



Now signed to Elite Model Management and boasting more than 306,000 Instagram followers, business is booming for this Wag, who has a net worth of around £1million.

She has bagged a five-figure deal with PrettyLittleThing, lucrative skincare partnerships with L’Oreal, plus modelling contracts with brands, such as Boohoo and GHD.

Sasha spent years modelling for other big names like House of Fraser and Lipsy before becoming a regular in the VIP stadium boxes.

TOLAMI BENSON

£500,000



Engaged to: Bukayo Saka

TOLAMI isn’t your average influencer making her mark after dating a footie hero.

She was at university studying hard when she got together with Arsenal ace Bukayo in 2020, and has built a professional career doing PR and marketing while dazzling fans at his games.

Now worth an estimated £500,000, she has become a viral sensation in London and recently attended the Prada show at Milan Fashion Week.



This savvy Wag is now commanding six-figure campaign deals with top-tier luxury ­fashion houses alongside High Street brands, such as her River Island edit.

And with her 299k Instagram followers, Tolami – who regularly models her favourite designers like Tom Ford and Prada – is able to bring in big commercial deals for her online audience.

Sports.title: MOTD hosts Mark Chapman & Kelly Cates dating after he splits with ex… who confronted him with suspicions they were close
Sports.content:
Next

MATCH of the Day host Mark Chapman has been dating his co-presenter Kelly Cates.

Friends say 52-year-old Chappers split from Dubai-based estate agent Clere Collier in April.



It is understood Clere then confronted him with her suspicions he had become close with Kelly, 51.

A source said: “Mark admitted the relationship but insisted there was no overlap between the two women and that he hadn’t cheated on her.”



The popular presenter was in a three-year relationship with Clere Collier.

Following their split estate agent Clere confronted Mark with suspicions about him and Kelly, who has hosted the BBC1 sports show with him since last year.

Chappers told 43-year-old Clere they were getting close but maintained that he had been faithful.

An associate of the former couple said: “Mark split with Clere out of the blue, without much explanation.

“They had been making plans for the future and their relationship had been going strong.

“They stayed in touch after the split, but Clere soon realised that Mark and Kelly were close and she accused Mark of dating Kelly.



“Mark admitted the relationship, but insisted there was no overlap between the two women and that he hadn’t cheated on her.

“He told her that he had been a single man when he started spending time with Kelly. Of course, it left a bad taste in Clere’s mouth, and she didn’t believe him.”

Dubai-based mum-of-two Clere regularly travelled to the UK to see Mark and they were pictured house-hunting last year.

Mark, one of the BBC’s highest paid broadcasters on £335,000 to £340,000 a year, was announced as a new MOTD host alongside Kelly and Gabby Logan last year.



This July he and Kelly teamed up on the Celebrity Gogglebox sofa.

Kelly, daughter of Scotland and Liverpool great Kenny Dalglish, split from TV producer husband Tom in 2021. They have two children.

Speaking about working with Mark and Gabby, Kelly said: “Being on a team with them is genuinely really exciting. I feel like I’m in a great little group.”

Chappers lost his wife of 19 years Sara to cancer when she was 44 in 2020. They had three children together.



At the time, a source told The Sun: “Sadly Sara passed away on June 3.

“Mark and the kids are absolutely devastated. The family were there and it’s just a really sad situation.

“They’re an extremely private family and would appreciate people respecting that.”

Following Sara’s death, Mark continued his bid to become a prominent voice in sports broadcasting.

Having become a firm fixture on BBC Radio 5 Live and filling in for Gary Lineker on Match of the Day, he also moved away from football to cover rugby league, the Olympics, NFL and both the Ryder Cup and The Open golf championships for the Beeb, as well as crossing over to Sky Sports to front its Carabao Cup coverage.



He also hosts The Sports Agents podcast with 53-year-old Gabby.

The pair, alongside Kelly, replaced Lineker full time on Match of the Day at the start of the 2025/2026 season after a shake-up instigated by director of BBC Sport Alex Kay-Jelski.

The decision to replace the ex-England striker, who had hosted the BBC’s flagship football show for 26 years, with a rotating trio of presenters was slammed by critics.



Former presenter Des Lynam said he felt Kelly should have got the job on her own as “viewers like consistency”.

Lynam said: “My wish would be to see Kelly Cates become the sole presenter and have her as the face of the programme, exclusive to the BBC.

“It used to be said the audience wanted a man in front of the camera, but I do not go along with that now — times have changed.

“Kelly is the man for the job, so to speak!”



Kelly praised both Mark and Gabby shortly after the trio were announced as permanent hosts, claiming the lack of egos between them meant job-sharing such a coveted role would be straightforward.

She said: “To be in the mix with Chappers and Gabby, who I really like as people, first of all, but really admire as broad-casters as well . . . it’s just a really lovely group to be in.

“People have this perception that it is a massive ego-filled world, and it is at times. You need a certain sort of ego to feel like you can do the job because you need a certain amount of confidence.

“But you don’t want to be in a position where we’re all trying to scramble over each other.



“The fact we’re all the same age, we’re at the same stage of our careers, we’ve all got other things outside of Match of the Day that we are all passionate about and really invested in, it means none of us are treading on each other and preying on each other’s insecurities.”

She added on the White Wine Question Time podcast: “We’re all really comfortable about who we are and where we are in our careers, so it really works.

“We’re all at a stage in our lives as well where we want to spend time with our families.

“We have kids of different ages and different things going on in our home lives as well.

“It’s really nice to be able to keep all that in the mix.”



Mark made his name at the Beeb working as a sports reporter on Radio 1, and became a fixture on Sara Cox’s show before working alongside shamed DJ Scott Mills.

The Lancashire-born star then bagged his own weekend show alongside Dave Vitty, Chris Moyles’ former sidekick, before progressing up the ranks of Radio 5 Live.

In August, The Sun revealed Kay-Jelski had clashed with members of the MOTD team and that there were fears of an exodus of the show’s top stars.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Some pundits were said to have been tempted to follow Lineker into podcasting — which the BBC denied.

The BBC declined to comment last night. Representatives for Kelly and Mark were asked for comment.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland DEMANDS to be subbed by Norway as he limps off in major Man City injury blow with issues piling up
Sports.content:
Next

ERLING HAALAND demanded to be substituted during Norway’s clash with Portugal in a major worry for Manchester City.

The superstar striker, 26, limped off shortly after the hour mark.

The score was level at 1-1 when Haaland was withdrawn for Crystal Palace forward Jorgen Strand Larsen on 67 minutes.



Brentford ace Kristoffer Ajer brilliantly fired Norway into a first half lead in Porto, only for Joao Cancelo to level before the break.



Barely 10 minutes after Haaland went off, Goncalo Ramos scored to complete Portugal‘s turnaround.

The potential injury suffered by Haaland adds to what’s been a nightmare international break for Man City.

Enzo Maresca‘s side were found guilty of more than 100 of the 130 charges levelled against them by the Premier League.

City are awaiting news of what their sanction will be, although they strongly maintain their innocence and have launched an appeal.

The Etihad club are set to return to action for the first time since their guilty verdict next weekend.

Maresca’s men will travel to Liverpool on Sunday, where they are set to be met by a big atmosphere.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS



And the City boss will be desperate to have Haaland available, the towering forward having scored five goals in as many Prem appearances so far this season.

Haaland is not the only City star to have endured an injury issue during the international break.

Nico O’Reilly was sent home from England duty with an issue, with Rico Lewis being promoted from the Under-21s to replace him.

The Three Lions are set to play their fourth and final match of this international break against Czechia at Wembley on Tuesday night.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Premier League teams split on punishment as manager claims 'everyone knew'
Sports.content:
The latest news on the Manchester City charges as the club launches an appeal on the guilty verdict on 114 of the 115 charges

Hello and welcome to today's live blog, where we will bring you the latest on the guilty verdict for Man City on breaches of Premier League financial rules.

The appeal process has been triggered by the club with them confirming that they had submitted an appeal in a statement over the weekend. That will now be heard by a new independent panel.

It comes after both the Premier League and City exchanged strong statements on the situation. The Premier League confirmed the guilty verdict on 114 of the 115 charges, stating that the panel found that City had used 'sham' sponsorship deals to inflate their income by almost £900 million during the nine-year period.

City hit back, stating that there were 'clear material errors' in the findings. One argument City are said to be using during the appeal is that the extra funding came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's owners, Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), something which is allowed under Premier League rules.

However, a statement from the main sponsors, Etihad, back in 2015, appears to contradict it.

There is still a lot of talk over what could happen. Stay right here for all of the latest...

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo given Portugal ultimatum as Jorge Jesus sets conditions for return
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo given Portugal ultimatum as Jorge Jesus sets conditions for return

Cristiano Ronaldo left the Portugal camp midway through their Nations League fixtures after being an unused substitute in their second match, plunging his international career into jeopardy

View 2 Images Jorge Jesus has put the ball in Cristiano Ronaldo's court (Image: Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images)

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus has told Cristiano Ronaldo that it's up to him to decide his future with the national team. Ronaldo, 41, fled the Portugal camp last week after a fallout with Jesus, who told the forward that he'd come on as a substitute during their 2-1 win away to Norway.

‌



‌



Instead, Ronaldo spent the entire game on the bench and stormed down the tunnel at full-time. Following talks with the president of the Portuguese football federation a few days later, the Al-Nassr superstar took off in a private jet.

‌



His replacement, Goncalo Ramos, scored in both subsequent games - including Sunday's victory over Norway on home soil by the same scoreline - making it four wins from four under Jesus. Post-match, the Portugal boss addressed Ronaldo's future and put the ball in his court.

‌



"We can talk before the next call-up, but Cris is the one who's going to decide," Jesus, who managed Ronaldo at club level last season, declared.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Cristiano should end his time in the national team the way he wants, he's the one who will decide how he wants it. In my first call-up, I said, 'I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you'. And now I'm saying the same thing."

Portugal's next fixture is at home to Denmark on November 14 before they travel to face Wales three days later. Ronaldo's team-mates are keen to have him back in the fold, with Joao Cancelo telling RTP: "Cristiano is our captain, the best player Portugal has ever had.

"Things will certainly end in the best way [with him] but the important thing is the four victories."

‌



Nuno Mendes added: "Any player who comes to the national team is welcome, obviously. If Cris returns, we'll be here to receive him with open arms."

In Portugal's pre-match press conference, Bruno Fernandes revealed that he'd spoken to Ronaldo since his departure. "Regarding Cristiano, I had a conversation with him," the midfielder confirmed.

Should Cristiano Ronaldo retire from international football? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo walked out on Portugal last week (Image: Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty Images)

"What I told him, and what I repeat here, is regardless of what happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football, and of the country, for what he has done not only in Portugal but throughout the world.

"He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people, and the most important thing is that we stop dividing things. There are no divisions in the national team. It is one and will remain so, despite any noise that may come from outside.

Article continues below

"We are outside of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices, that it respects all sides. Cris is and will be the biggest icon of our national team, he deserves everyone's respect, regardless of who likes him more or [who likes him] less."

Ronaldo himself wrote in a post on social media that he'd 'tell the truth to all the Portuguese people' about why he left the national team. The five-time Ballon d'Or winner is expected to return to action when Al-Nassr continue their title defence against Diriyah in the Saudi Pro League on Friday night.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Star targeted for defensive rebuild as Jurgen Klopp makes admission
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Star targeted for defensive rebuild as Jurgen Klopp makes admission

Liverpool return to Premier League action this week with a blockbuster clash against Manchester City at Anfield

View 3 Images Jurgen Klopp has been open about his return to football (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

The Liverpool players will slowly begin to return to domestic training this week as they prepare for the visit of Manchester City. Andoni Iraola will aim to continue the Reds' unbeaten run and take points from the current league leaders in the process.

‌



‌



Eighteen Liverpool players departed last month to represent their countries, including Jeremy Jacquet's first call-up for France. Boss Zinedine Zidane was full of praise for the young defender, stating her was "very, very good" and "brave" against Italy in the Nations League last week.

‌



With a handful of games left on the international schedule, Iraola will soon welcome back his senior stars as they look ahead to Enzo Maresca's side and the challenge of October. Here, Mirror Football has the latest coming out of Anfield.

‌



Rio Ngumoha reveals what Mohamed Salah told him before leaving Liverpool READ MORE :

Juve eye Italian Red

Juventus are looking to "rebuild the Italian DNA" of their club and will start by pursuing Giovanni Leoni, it's been claimed. Gazzetta dello Sport states that the Serie A side are looking for "Premier League defenders" that can bolster their backline while bringing back a national identity to the Old Lady.

The 19-year-old has barely featured for the Reds since joining in August 2025, putting in a man-of-the-match performance against Southampton before suffering an ACL rupture. Leoni's debut season was over after just 80 minutes of action and he is yet to grace the pitch again for Liverpool.

View 3 Images Juventus are eyeing up Giovanni Leoni (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

‌



It seems that Iraola has big plans for the teenager despite transfer interest, confirming in September that he will reintegrate the centre-half back to the main group over the international break. Speaking before the Ipswich Town win, the Reds boss said: "I think the next one probably should be Giovanni Leoni. I think the plan is also to start training during the break, with the group.

"I think even Fede [Chiesa] should be around those dates and probably Conor [Bradley], and especially Hugo [Ekitike], will go later, yes."

Jurgen Klopp's 'love lost' admission

Jurgen Klopp believes he has found the "love" for football once again after it was drained out of him at Anfield. The former Reds boss made a shock departure from Anfield in 2024 after citing that he was "running out of energy."

‌



View 3 Images Florian Wirtz is full of praise for the former Liverpool boss (Image: Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND / AFP via Getty Images)

After two years away from the dugout, Klopp returned to take on the role of head coach of his country. Ahead of his fourth game in charge of Germany against Greece, the 59-year-old insisted he is back in a romance with the sport.

Klopp said: "I missed nothing, but I realised I still love what I’m doing. It’s a blessing to work together with players like [Aleksandar Pavlovic]. It’s a pure joy. I’m blessed to watch the group I have from close. We’ve only just started, I’m looking forward to our common future."

Article continues below

Liverpool winger Florian Wirtz has also fallen in love with his new international boss, dubbing Klopp a "true master" after a 2-0 win over Serbia. Wirtz said: "He has a very good rapport with every player.

"[He tries] to approach every player and make him feel important and that he deserves to be here. It’s important that every player feels valued. And I think Klopp is a true master at that."

Sports.title: Arsenal news: 'Next Bellingham' race entered as silence broken on 'intense' transfer saga
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: 'Next Bellingham' race entered as silence broken on 'intense' transfer saga

Arsenal are showing interest in a midfielder who has been likened to Jude Bellingham

View 3 Images Arsenal are eyeing a Borussia Dortmund wonderkid (Image: Mike Hewitt, Getty Images)

Arsenal's stars continue to impress on international duty as Gunners fans wait patiently for the return of club football. An impressive 17 Arsenal players were selected to represent their nations for the recent international break.

‌



‌



Several of them have thrived and even got on the scoresheet in recent days, including Mikel Merino, Viktor Gyokeres and Bukayo Saka, who bagged a brace in England's 7-0 win over Croatia on Saturday.

‌



But while Gunners boss Mikel Arteta will be happy that some of his players have found form, others have suffered injury scares during the break. Martin Odegaard seems to have recovered from Bernardo Silva's rogue challenge on him, though Christos Tzolis and Kai Havertz may face late fitness tests ahead of the reigning champions' return to Premier League action.

‌



They face Leeds United on Saturday as they look to put things right after the shock 3-0 defeat to Brighton before the break. Now, Mirror Football takes a look at two of the latest transfer stories involving the north Londoners.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal injury blow prompts £34m January transfer plan with bid prepared READ MORE :

Arsene Wenger was right to be fuming about Man City - now football owes him an apology READ MORE :

'Next Jude Bellingham' eyed

Arsenal are reportedly serious contenders to land Borussia Dortmund wonderkid Justin Ejodamen, who has been described in the media as the next Jude Bellingham. The 15-year-old midfielder’s profile has been likened to the Englishman, who signed for Dortmund as a 17-year-old and has gone on to become one of the best midfielders in the world.

‌



The teenager is already being tracked by some of Europe’s biggest clubs, including AC Milan and Juventus, although Barcelona reportedly lead the chase. English clubs Chelsea and Arsenal are keen on the player too given his huge potential.

View 3 Images Bellingham became a star at Dortmund (Image: Alexandre Simoes/Borussia Dortmund via Getty Images)

TEAMtalk reports that Arsenal’s recruitment team has been monitoring Ejodamen’s performances and may look to land him if the opportunity presents itself at a later date. However, they face a significant hurdle.

‌



The midfielder turns 16 in April, after which clubs within the EU can sign him, while English teams are unable to until 2029. Dortmund also remain confident of keeping hold of the talented teenager, given their long-standing reputation for developing youngsters into world-class players.

Ejodamen currently represents Italy at youth international level despite being born in Germany. He is also eligible to play for Nigeria.

Fabio Vieira breaks silence

View 3 Images Fabio Vieira completed a move to Hamburg late in the window (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Fabio Vieira has opened up about his nerves in the final days of the transfer window, before he sealed his deadline day move to Hamburg. The German club, where the 26-year-old spent last season on loan, were reluctant to meet the Gunners’ asking price for much of the summer, with neither side willing to budge.

Vieira’s preference for a move to Hamburg was always clear, given he was clearly not part of Arteta’s plans. He had to remain patient throughout the negotiations, which made for a tense final few days ahead of deadline day. Eventually, Arsenal were forced to accept a cut fee of £8.6million as Vieira was left delighted, having secured his preferred move.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Vieira said: "The last two or three days in particular were quite intense. I was a bit nervous because I didn’t know if everything would really work out. But in the end, everything went well. Now I’m here and very happy about it."

Sports.title: Ireland coach makes half-time 'spit' allegation against Israel player
Sports.content:
Ireland coach makes half-time 'spit' allegation against Israel player

The alleged incident took place during the half-time interval between Ireland and Israel during their Nations League clash

View 2 Images Israel and Republic of Ireland players clash in their Nations League encounter. (Image: (Photo by Srdjan Stevanovic/Getty Images))

An Israeli player has been accused of spitting at a member of the Republic of Ireland coaching staff during Sunday's Nations League clash. Fitness coach Damien Doyle was spotted protesting following an incident involving an unnamed Israeli player as both teams made their way towards the tunnel at half-time.

‌



‌



It is claimed he was spat at as tensions boiled over - with the incident unfolding in front of stadium security and local police. The flashpoint triggered a confrontation between the two camps, and Spanish referee Juan Martínez Munuera, who had awarded Troy Parrott a first-half penalty following a VAR review, intervened to separate the feuding players and coaching staff.

‌



He is understood not to have witnessed the spitting incident, reports the Irish Mirror. However, the Irish Independent claims that Serbian security staff did see the incident take place.

‌



Ireland repeat Israel gesture after week of Nations League hostilities READ MORE :

Before the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists whose questions had prompted an abrupt end to Heimir Hallgrímsson's pre-match press conference were prohibited from attending either manager's post-match briefing.

One Israeli journalist had tried to ask Hallgrímsson whether he supported an "ideology based on murder" - referencing an attempt to crash an aeroplane bound for Tel Aviv.

‌



Another made a claim that "your players called our players monkeys during [last Sunday's] match" - before being swiftly interrupted by FAI media officer Kieran Crowley.

He responded firmly, saying: "That's that's completely untrue, that is completely untrue, that is completely untrue."

As Crowley escorted Hallgrímsson and the Irish media away, the reporter persisted with further accusations.

FAI officials are currently examining audio recordings from pitchside microphones after Jayson Molumby approached the match official last Sunday to raise concerns about racist abuse directed at Adam Idah and James Abankwah from the Israeli supporters.

The fixture took place without any spectators present, having been staged behind closed doors on Sunday evening.

Article continues below

The encounter ended 1-1, with Israel finding an equaliser shortly after the interval. The FAI have been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland repeat Israel gesture after week of Nations League hostilities
Sports.content:
Ireland repeat Israel gesture after week of Nations League hostilities

There were no pre-match handshakes between Ireland and Israel's players for the second time in a week in the UEFA Nations League

View 2 Images A view of the Ireland team during the Israel national anthem (Image: ©INPHO/Ryan Byrne)

Players from the Republic of Ireland and Israel once again refused to shake hands ahead of their UEFA Nations League clash on Sunday evening.

‌



‌



The two sides met for the second time in the space of a week, following Ireland's dominant 3-0 win against Israel seven days ago.

‌



Ireland's players once more bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem as a show of protest, while two different captains from last week's encounter - Caoimhin Kelleher and Dor Peretz - decided NOT to shake hands following the coin toss.

‌



It was confirmed prior to kick-off that Israel would be wearing black armbands in tribute to those who lost their lives in the October 7 attacks, after UEFA granted their request to do so. Ireland also wore black armbands "in recognition of all the lives lost in the conflict" in the Middle East.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Scenes descended into chaos at Saturday's pre-match press conference when Heimir Hallgrímsson was quizzed about the incident earlier in the week aboard a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, in which the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the pilot and attempted to bring the aircraft down.

The FAI press officer intervened, stating that the Ireland manager would only be fielding football-related questions, before Hallgrímsson was then asked whether Finn Azaz would be named in the starting XI.

He responded by saying: "You will see the starting line up tomorrow. I'm not going to give the media the starting line up."

‌



View 2 Images Heimir Hallgrímsson (Image: ©INPHO/Ryan Byrne)

An Israeli journalist subsequently alleged that a racial slur had been directed at an Israeli player during last Sunday's fixture, a claim the FAI press officer flatly denied, stating "that is not true", before bringing the press conference to a close.

The Israeli reporter pushed back, saying: "This is a press conference, we have been invited to ask questions."

Article continues below

Ireland have picked up four points from their three Nations League matches during the extended international break. They were beaten at Kosovo 1-0 before winning against Israel and then drawing 2-2 to Austria.

As for Israel, they have endured a miserable international hiatus having failed to win each of their three matches so far, losing against Austria and Ireland, then picking up a point at home to Kosovo.

Sports.title: England new boy Alex Scott sends Thomas Tuchel clear message and hails 'scary' team-mate
Sports.content:
England new boy Alex Scott sends Thomas Tuchel clear message and hails 'scary' team-mate

Alex Scott produced a statement performance on his first start for England, helping the Three Lions thrash Croatia 7-0 to make it back-to-back wins in their Nations League campaign

View 3 Images Alex Scott has broken into the England team (Image: Michael Regan - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

Alex Scott says his World Cup heartbreak gave him “more hunger” to force his way into Thomas Tuchel's plans. Bournemouth midfielder Scott, 23, went to the pre-tournament training camp in Florida but did not get a cap in the friendlies and also missed out on the squad in the summer.

‌



‌



But Scott has started the season in brilliant form for his club and made his first start for England in Croatia having come on as a substitute in the Czech Republic. Scott now looks made to measure for England's midfield and looked at home straight away even on his full debut.

‌



Scott said: "It gave me more hunger but I've said there's so many top players for this country, it's a tough squad to get into. There was no bad feelings about not going to the World Cup, I went to the prep camp, I wanted to do that and learn as much as I can and it helped me coming into this camp and starting to play games.

‌



"Off the pitch, the stuff that I learned there, being around the group, it's made me feel way more comfortable. It can be challenging but for me it's not been at all. The lads and the group we've got here have made it so comfortable for me.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Leading up to the game I've been on a few camps now, they make it easy for you and make you feel as comfortable and confident as possible. I just want to go and play my normal football. I spoke to a few of the lads before the game and they said exactly that, 'Go on and do what you do for your club, be confident, be brave'."

England boss Tuchel has described Scott as the most in-form midfielder in the Premier League and admitted it was tough to leave him out in the summer. But Scott says there was no special advice from the England boss after he did not make the cut - but just to keep pushing.

Scott said: "I wouldn't say he said anything, probably just get your head down and keeping playing as well as possible. I've started the season pretty well with Bournemouth - that was important to me and coming into this team and pushing the lads who have been playing well and have been mainstays in midfield, that was what I wanted to do."

‌



Scott also answered the notion that England do not have midfielders with possession and ball retention in their DNA. He also relished the partnership with Elliot Anderson who he knows well from England under-21 duty. Scott added: "First start and they don't come much better than that.

Should Alex Scott keep his place against Czechia? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 3 Images Alex Scott shone on his full England debut (Image: Michael Regan - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



"Seven goals and we were deadly from the off. That front four we've got and players coming off the bench is frightening. It's an honour to be part of that group and be part of this team.

"Me and Elliot work really well together. We saw that last year at the Euros and we've been speaking about it ever since, playing this midfield together. I thought we did really well out there, of course the result probably shows that.

"I love playing with Elliot, he makes life so easy for me as his partner in there. He's probably one of the best midfielders in the world at the moment. I think we just bounce off each other very well, we both like getting on the ball, aggressive off the ball, we suit each other the way we play so playing next to him is great for me and I know he enjoys it as well.

‌



"We were ruthless off the ball, our counter press and on the break we scored a few goals and had a few chances. That's what we do really well, the players we've got in this team it suits them really well. We did perfectly and everything came together nicely."

Scott also says that “scary” Jude Bellingham is even better in person. The Real Madrid superstar has been in superb form in the Nations League and could easily become one of England’s greatest ever players.

View 3 Images Jude Bellingham is 'the best midfielder in the world', according to Alex Scott (Image: Michael Regan - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



Scott said: "Honestly, I've never seen anything like it. He's even better in person, seeing it up close and being on the same pitch as him... he's the best midfielder in the world, one of the best players in the world for sure and a great human being.

"Everyone knows that - the fans know that, everyone in the world knows what he's like as a person. On the pitch his ability is scary and that's the benchmark we need to live up to."

Scott says England are now clicking and there seven goal thrashing of Croatia will make the rest of Europe sit up and take notice. He added: "It's hard work, it's the level we've got in our team. The front four were unbelievable and it makes it easy playing behind that. Anthony Gordon is deadly making runs in behind, his pace and ability.

Article continues below

"Jude was everywhere on the pitch, Harry Kane the same and Bukayo Saka was ruthless as well. Playing behind these guys is great for me and Elliot and the backline were excellent with a clean sheet. It feels like the perfect performance.

"I think we've had tough games - Spain was a tough game and we did really well in that one. Unfortunately we didn't get the win. But we beat Czechia and then come here and beat Croatia so we know how good we are and how good we can be so it's important to put these markers down and beat teams like that to scare opposition in the future."

Sports.title: Premier League icon sacked from first managerial role at crisis club after cryptic interview
Sports.content:
Premier League icon sacked from first managerial role at crisis club after cryptic interview

Former Sunderland midfielder Lee Cattermole, 39, has been sacked by crisis-hit Gateshead, having overseen a disastrous start to the season in the National League

View 2 Images Lee Cattermole has been sacked by Gateshead (Image: Ed Sykes/Getty Images)

Lee Cattermole has been sacked by Gateshead after suggesting there were people at the club who didn't want the team to succeed.

‌



‌



Cattermole landed his first managerial role at Gateshead in June and oversaw a disastrous start to the season. The 39-year-old, who spent 10 years playing for Sunderland, managed to record just one win from their 12 league games and departs with the club rock bottom of the National League.

‌



Gateshead were beaten 2-1 by Worthing on Saturday, prompting a fiery post-match interview from Cattermole, who alluded to issues behind the scenes. The club failed to pay their staff and players for September after director Mark Nellist resigned and withdrew his financial support.

‌



"Everyone has to be united, this club is nowhere near that, nowhere near that," Cattermole said after the loss to Worthing. "The club is nowhere near where it should be, it’s been disappointing. Press goes out about the players wages not being paid. That’s disappointing but it happens.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"But it goes from before that, well before that. We need to figure out who wants to be part of the new regime or whatever you want to call it and find out who wants to be part of it. If we do, we will get the club going because a club like Gateshead has been really competitive in certain spells and that is when everyone is united and everyone is together.

"I’ve been fully aware for the whole time I’ve been here, that isn’t the case. I’ve been managing it, I’ve been dealing with it, I’ve been trying to put a positive spin on it and prepare the team.

"But ultimately, there are people in this building that don’t want the team to move forward and I know that. I can feel it, I see it and the clearer that we can be, that’s staff, players, fans, we might start winning games but it can’t happen, it doesn’t just happen."

‌



View 2 Images Lee Cattermole made 262 appearances for Sunderland (Image: Steven Hadlow/Getty Images)

The club is "appealing to shareholders to continue funding support" in the wake of Nellist's efforts to hand over his shares to fellow shareholder Stephen Paylor.

Gateshead have lost 10 of their 12 league games and are already eight points adrift of safety. Ben Clark has been appointed as interim manager to replace Cattermole.

‌



"There’s been a lot of change and the moment we iron that out and get it going and get everyone aligned, so there’s no hiding place," the former Sunderland star said before the sacking. "Because what happens when you have a struggled, you have people that want to move it forward and other people play hide and seek.

"That happens in every club up and down the country. I’ve been part of it, I’m now trying to lead it and I need every staff member on board so we can go forward. If they are not, the players can feel it, staff members feel it and once we do iron it out, we might have a chance of winning some games."
