Sports.title: Erling Haaland limps off during Norway's Nations League clash with Portugal to leave Man City sweating just a week before Liverpool showdown
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland limps off during Norway's Nations League clash with Portugal to leave Man City sweating just a week before Liverpool showdown

Manchester City are sweating over Erling Haaland's fitness after the forward limped off during Norway's Nations League defeat against Portugal on Sunday night.

The 26-year-old had signalled that he wanted to come off with a hand motion during the second half.

His withdrawal comes just a week before Manchester City travel to Liverpool, with their guilty verdict in their batle with the Premier League hanging over them.

The forward was able to walk off the pitch unaided with the score at 1-1, but a 79th-minute goal from Goncalo Ramos saw Portugal win 2-1 in the absence of Cristiano Ronaldo.

Haaland started all four of Norway's Nations League matches in a 10-day spell, scoring in earlier fixture against Denmark and Portugal.

It remains to be seen how much of a headache this could be for City, who also saw Nico O'Reilly withdraw from England duty mid-way through the international break with an injury.

More to follow.

Erling Haaland asked to be subbed and limped off during Norway's 2-1 defeat by Portugal

Haaland has enjoyed a flying start to the season, scoring seven in as many appearances for City, who are top of the Premier League with a perfect record.

He did not get much of a summer break, with Norway having reached the quarter-finals of the World Cup, where they lost to England.

His success is partially built on his capacity to play plenty of games without getting injured. Last season he only missed one match with a knock, and the longest injury of his career in 2023-24 did not even keep him out for two months.

It has been a tough international break for City after the Premier League condemned them for making 'sham' agreements to manipulate their financial accounts to the tune of £900million over a nine-season period which saw them win eight trophies.

On Friday last week, Daily Mail Sport reported how City had been found guilty of 114 of 115 charges against them.

However, there had been no official comment from the Premier League on the findings of an independent panel who oversaw a hearing that concluded in December 2024.

That then dramatically changed. In a lengthy statement, the Premier League say City arranged 'sham contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on "sham" agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs'.

It also says the club falsely altered the financial picture at the Etihad to the tune of £900m. The club had agreed exorbitant sponsorship deals with a number of companies, but those sponsors only paid part of the fee.

The rest was propped up by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club.

Premier League CEO Richard Masters claimed that the commission's verdict had 'vindicated' the league's decision to pursue the charges

As the Premier League note, this allowed City to 'artificially inflate the club’s revenues' and therefore spend more under Premier League rules. The higher the revenue a club records, the more they are permitted to spend.

Moreover, further 'sham' deals, funded by ADUG, allowed the club to 'record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred'.

The Premier League say that revenues were inflated and costs reduced to the tune of £900m in an attempt to comply with spending rules. The result was that the club 'filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators'.

It added that the club was 'significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits' during the time period in question, 2009-2018 when it won eight major trophies.

Had City reported accurately 'it would have been in breach of both the League's and UEFA's spending limits by a very substantial amount'.

The panel also found that City committed multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and good faith in that it failed to assist the Premier League's four-year investigation, triggered by the emergence of club emails obtained by a hacker.

Indeed, City had 'made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the PL investigation'.

Richard Masters, Chief Executive of the Premier League, said: 'The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

'It also vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

'It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

'This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches. Now we have the Commission's decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans.'

Manchester City have insisted on their innocence throughout the saga (Pep Guardiola pictured with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak)

In a statement released a short time later, City said it was ‘disappointed and surprised’ and referred to the ‘opinion of the Premier League Commission’.

It added: ‘The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

‘The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

‘The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete.’

City have until Friday to appeal.

Man City were first charged with the 115 breaches in February 2023. While that totemic number stuck, the figure – as they subsequently corrected – was actually 130.

Of those, 54 were charges of ‘failure to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information’ while there were 14 charges of ‘failure to provide accurate financial reports for player and manager compensation’.

Both sets related to alleged offences between 2009 and 2018 (2009-2018), an eight-year period which saw the club win four Premier League titles, the FA Cup, and three League Cup competitions.

There were also five charges of ‘failure to comply with UEFA’s regulations, including Financial Fair Play Regulations’ and seven charges of breaching the Premier League’s profit and sustainability regulations (PSR) between 2015 and 2018.

There were also 35 counts of failure to co-operate with Premier League investigations between 2018 and 2023.

The hearing into the 130 breaches began last September at London’s International Dispute Resolution Centre, with the Premier League sparing no expense and enlisting KCs Adam Lewis and Andrew Hunter to take its case.

Sports.title: Tom Brady owns up to rookie on-air mistake that sparked technical issues behind the scenes on Fox broadcast
Sports.content:
Tom Brady owns up to rookie on-air mistake that sparked technical issues behind the scenes on Fox broadcast

Tom Brady owned up after accidentally causing audio issues in the Fox Sports booth during their Week 4 assignment.

Brady and the Fox A-team were in Philadelphia to watch the Eagles take on the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field.

But he inadvertently silenced his producers, causing disruption for him and partner Kevin Burkhardt in the first half before realizing what happened and the fact he was to blame in humiliating circumstances later exposed live on air.

'You want to fess up?' Burkhardt asked his partner. 'The mic issue?' before Brady took the opportunity with both hands.

'Okay, my fault,' Brady said. 'I have this big clunky board which I have all this information about what I want to say all day.'

He showed a large fold-up card filled with notes about the two teams, an insight into his level of preparation, before explaining the chaos it caused.

Tom Brady owned up to a humiliating mistake in the Fox booth during NFL Week 4 action

Now that's a QB owning up to his mistake �� @TomBrady https://t.co/wUt5Zagrpz — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) October 4, 2026

'And I dropped it on the talk back button' he continued. 'And I'm sitting here going, 'guys, I can't hear anyone', and it's my fault the whole time.

'That's like a quarterback owning up to his mistakes, that's what it is.'

Brady was back on air for the first time since an explosive, tell-all book about his life was released.

Lars Anderson, the man who wrote 'Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness,' dove into the seven-time Super Bowl champion's split from the actress and his subsequent romance and marriage to supermodel Gisele Bundchen.

The Daily Mail exclusively published the first extract of the book last week sharing the ugly details of his marriage to Gisele and details of their split.

A second extract from the book shared insight into Brady's private life dating back to his college career and the secrets stashed from the years long before his fame.

Anderson, a Sports Illustrated writer, has previously written a book on the Manning Family and explained his desire to try and give readers an insight into who the seven-time Super Bowl champion 'really is' behind the scenes.

'Numerous books have been written about different aspects of Tom Brady's career, but no one has authored the definitive biography on him: a meaty, deeply reported narrative that gives readers a 360-degree view of his iconic life,' Anderson said to PEOPLE.

A new book on Brady's life has shed light on his marriage and divorce with Gisele Bundchen

'This was the goal as I spent two years digging into the bedrocks of Brady to explain him, interpret his story and answer the fundamental question of who he really is.

'I explore what he represents, what makes him tick, and why he inspires so much passion — you either love him or loathe him.

'I looked at why his relationships with the two famous women who bore his children failed, examined the price of genius and probed his category-five obsession with perfection.

'Employing put-you-there storytelling techniques, my goal was to place the reader next to Brady at all the key moments of his life, recreating scenes to show sides never before seen of the winningest player in NFL history.'

PART ONE: Every ugly detail of Tom and Gisele's marriage... the secret letter stashed in a drawer... and her savage last three words

PART TWO: Why Tom Brady's college teammates were convinced he was gay... until one uninhibited night proved the truth: Secrets from his years before fame - and existential crisis that drove him to the brink

Sports.title: Phil Mickelson is tipped for stunning return to the PGA Tour by LIV Golf's biggest critic in the wake of his 'family trauma' rehab
Sports.content:
Phil Mickelson is tipped for stunning return to the PGA Tour by LIV Golf's biggest critic in the wake of his 'family trauma' rehab

Phil Mickelson's biggest critic has tipped him for a shock return to the PGA Tour after it emerged he has been in rehab amid ongoing personal issues.

Mickelson reportedly entered and has already left an addiction center. His representatives told TMZ: 'Phil was seeking treatment for family trauma and addiction.'

The news comes after the 56-year-old, a six-time major champion, stepped away from professional golf this year.

In the meantime, LIV Golf has been torn apart after the withdrawal of Saudi funding, leading to questions over the future of its stars.

Brandel Chamblee, now lead analyst on Golf Channel after his own playing career ended, has been the most outspoken critic of those who turned their backs on the PGA Tour for LIV Golf.

He also has a long history with Mickelson in particular, who told GOLF Magazine in 2018: 'He and I don't see eye to eye on anything.'

Phil Mickelson has been tipped for a PGA Tour return after spending time in a rehab facility

Brandel Chamblee has long been one of Mickelson and LIV Golf's most vocal public critics

But Mickelson has found a surprising olive branch from Chamblee, who believes the legendary leftie would be forgiven and welcomed back if he wanted to be.

Speaking on the We Need a Fourth podcast, Chamblee was asked whether Mickelson has tarnished his legacy for good.

'I don't know about forever,' he said. 'I think we're in a pretty forgiving world. He's obviously got his demons that he fights, and I wouldn't wish them on anybody, but he's not alone in fighting demons.

'I think if he hadn't gone to LIV, he would have been Arnold Palmer reincarnated. He would have been Ryder Cup captain numerous times. He would have been an honorary starter at Augusta. He would have been the lead analyst at CBS. He would have been the pied piper everywhere he went.

'But I think if he came back and said 'look, I've made mistakes, I've tried to deal with them. Sorry for the damage I've caused.

'The game's been so good to me. And for the rest of my life, I'm going to try and be good back to it', I think everyone would put their arms around him and go 'welcome back, sorry you had so much trouble, hope you get your life straightened out'.

'Life's hard, it doesn't matter who you're talking into, running into. Everybody's dealing with something. Everybody's got some battle that they've faced or will face.

'I started doing commentary in 2004, so 2004 until Phil left, I used to say Phil was a gift to the game of golf. His talent, his showmanship, his look at me quality, it was incredible. What a talent, what an amazing talent.'

The golfer and his wife are seen taking in the action on the Sunday of the 2021 Ryder Cup

Mickelson and Amy are pictured with their children, Evan, Sophie and Amanda, after his victory at the 2013 Open Championship

Mickelson stepped away from golf earlier this year and cited an unspecified private family matter involving his wife, Amy, for his absence.

Mickelson has been married to Amy, 54, for almost 30 years after tying the knot back in November 1996. The couple share three children together in Evan, Sophie and Amanda.

He has been candid about his struggles with gambling, previously opening up on his addiction in 2023.

He said at the time that he had 'crossed the line from moderation into addiction which isn't fun at all.'

'The money wasn't ever the issue since our financial security has never been threatened, but I was so distracted I wasn't able to be present with the ones I love and caused a lot of harm,' he said.

He also described how this 'lack of presence' has been 'so hurtful' for his family, saying he's been 'often' told throughout his addiction, 'You're here, but you're not with us.'

'It affected those I care about in ways I wasn't aware or could fully understand,' Mickelson said. 'It's like a hurricane is going on outside and I'm isolated in a shelter oblivious to what was happening.'

'When I came out there was so much damage to clean up that I just wanted to back inside and not deal with it,' he added.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon is playing with swagger and belief - and his telepathic connection with Lewis Hall could mean Thomas Tuchel FINALLY solves a problem area in his team
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon is playing with swagger and belief - and his telepathic connection with Lewis Hall could mean Thomas Tuchel FINALLY solves a problem area in his team

It’s a goal and an assist once an hour for Anthony Gordon in an England shirt at the moment. Eight of those vital contributions in his last six games since clambering off the bench for the rescue act against DR Congo, another two added to the growing collection during Saturday’s demolition job in Croatia.

Count winning a penalty in the Azteca as the assist it was and the statistics are even more favourable: a goal contribution every 53 minutes.

Whatever the numbers, something has clicked inside somebody who has felt somewhat underappreciated by the English public and actively wanted to leave the Premier League to alter perceptions of his abilities.

Barcelona suits him, the £68million man whose performances in Catalonia are delighting Culers in much the same way as his use of Spanish at the summer unveiling.

Thomas Tuchel has noticed an extra air of confidence to him through this international camp (three goals and an assist), a sense of greater understanding around new-found seniority and a belief that he is now one of England’s main pillars.

Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Bukayo Saka are locks in three of the attacking positions. It’s impossible to argue against Gordon’s inclusion as the fourth after the past few months.

Anthony Gordon (centre) and Lewis Hall (right) have a flourishing understanding

‘Anthony plays with a lot more edge,’ Tuchel said. ‘He’s for sure found another level, another gear, and is very decisive.’ The very best grow the higher they climb.

Gordon believes that Congo, changing the game in Atlanta’s indoor arena when the air was rapidly leaving England’s World Cup balloon, positively shifted his international arc.

By his own admission, it takes him a while to settle within a group – although that hasn’t seemed a problem at Barca – and now approaching 30 caps, it has become time to take ownership of the left wing. Particularly as Marcus Rashford nudged himself back into the frame last season and provided stiff competition in America.

Gordon’s goal in Rijeka on Saturday evening, England’s third of the night, was a flying header to follow up another smart header in Prague days earlier. To highlight just how things are landing for him right now, the former Newcastle United forward has not scored a single header across 248 career club appearances.

There is a swagger, noticeable in how he toyed with markers at the weekend. Josip Stanisic of Bayern Munich will have endured nightmares. The way Gordon stopped an attack dead, stood Stanisic up and then strutted past provided embarrassment for a full back who started both legs of the Champions League semi-final under Vincent Kompany last season. Croatia might as well have picked one of the kids in the stands.

Poor Stanisic was only provided mercy by Slaven Bilic once Gordon had earned his rest, which in itself felt unfair. Yet there might be some relief that the 25-year-old didn’t make the experience even more chastening, missing three big chances across his 70 minutes. It really could, and should, have been 10.

One of those arrived seconds after Kane’s early opener and engineered by Lewis Hall, his former team-mate at St James’ Park. Hall’s had a strong week himself after Nico O’Reilly’s injury and the connection between the two is obvious, a telepathy that Tuchel must want to tap into more.

Quieter and more reserved, Hall is offering evidence that an incisiveness from the middle third – the pass for that Gordon chance had precision and perfect weight – is being matched by defensive doggedness. Possessing both is a rare find in modern full backs.

Gordon's form for Barcelona and England has taken him to a different level this season

To illustrate that, during a brief moment of England panic – Croatia breaking and the visitors defensively misshapen – Hall held up the galloping Franjo Ivanovic to allow others a return to their normal positions and the danger was adequately snuffed. Later on, and with England already five goals up, it was Hall’s relentless pressing inside the Croatia box that prompted a gift for Saka to smash into the net’s roof.

Hall had to deal with the setback of missing out on the World Cup squad and felt he was worthy of a spot, the response being an encouraging start to this campaign and carrying on where he left off for Newcastle. Hall, 23, has spoken openly about having to ‘play catch up’ with Tuchel’s general messaging during the camp, with the majority of the players familiar after seven weeks together Stateside.

Individually things are going well and as a pairing, they look a proper package. Tuchel loves his combinations – Bellingham and Kane, Guehi and Konsa, Quansah and Saka when Reece James isn’t fit. He wants them all over the pitch and the left-hand side has felt like a forever problem for England.

Gordon has unequivocally done more than anybody else to nail down the attacking spot, with Hall now in a straight battle with O’Reilly for the supporting role. Even before this week, the left has appeared in ruder health than for some time.

In the knockout stages of 2021, 2022 and 2024 tournaments, Luke Shaw had the place sorted for himself but there was uncertainty about what lay ahead of him. Phil Foden’s versatility meant he was shunted wide in 2022 and two years later, in a bid to play the Manchester City star inside, Shaw operated as a wing back as Gareth Southgate went to a back three to the detriment of any real flair.

The combinations weren’t quite there and Tuchel has had some questions answered across his tenure, with some crystallised during the first camp of the season.

‘I don’t want to write Nico O’Reilly off because he played for us in the first match,’ Tuchel said. ‘Lewis had two good matches now. He loves to play in the offensive full back position, he’s very good on the ball. He loves ball possession. He is very clinical, loves these little movements.

‘He played very well with Anthony. You can see that they’ve played many seasons together in the coordination of their movements. He helped Anthony a lot.’

Gordon has now taken ownership of the left wing position under Thomas Tuchel

Saturday was their 58th start together for club and country; as Tuchel alluded to, it showed. There is a little more power and physicality than advertised in them, Gordon leaning into his wiry frame and hustling in recovery runs to back up his mate, with Hall’s engine providing a different dimension going the other way.

‘I’m nowhere near the player I can be,’ Gordon told ITV last week when dissecting the move to Barca and his increased international standing. He regularly journals private targets and starring in La Liga appears to have been one. ‘Maybe delusionally I’ve [envisioned] it from a young age. Why would I have so much confidence from a young age? It makes no sense. I can’t explain why.

‘I’ve become a different player in a lot of people’s eyes. I always felt in England that people respected me because I was fast and I pressed but they never actually respected the quality and IQ that I play with. Only the players I play with seem to notice that. Now that I’m at Barcelona and playing a different style, those qualities are highlighted much more and people are starting to take notice that I’m not just quick.’

He spoke at length with Kane about the prospect of Barca, the side effects of leaving familiarities, and given the captain’s explosion at Bayern – in the running for this year’s Ballon d’Or – the feedback was to go for it wholeheartedly.

Gordon has never been shy, Everton fans will tell you that with the way he moved to Newcastle, and is still surprised at coming off against Argentina as England retreated. In being honest with himself in the quest for constant improvement and proving he deserves a place on this stage, he vows to become more selfish around the box.

Five assists in his first four Barca matches suggests that might need a bit of work. Not a lot else does and it is inarguable that Gordon looks even slicker with his mate behind him.

Sports.title: Former Premier League boss Jesse Marsch claims 'EVERYONE knew' about Man City's cheating - and calls for club to be relegated after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Former Leeds United manager Jesse Marsch has insisted 'everyone knew' about Manchester City's cheating and has called for the club to be relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching financial rules. Marsch was appointed as Leeds boss in February 2022 but was sacked 12 months later as the club battled to avoid relegation from the Premier League. The 52-year-old, who is now in charge of Canada, was asked about an independent commission ruling verdict that ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period peppered with ‘sham’ deals. In a damning 40-page verdict, published on Tuesday, found City artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules. While the ruling covered the period between 2009-2018, Marsch expressed his belief that there were 'inconsistencies' even during his time in the Premier League. Marsch told the Guardian that Man City should be relegated from the top flight as a result of the verdict. Man City confirmed on Friday that they have lodged an appeal to overturn the independent commission's verdict. Jesse Marsch, left, has claimed 'everyone knew' about Man City's cheating as he called for the club to be relegated from the top flight Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of charges against them by the Premier League, but have launched an appeal against the decision 'I think Man City should be punished severely. I think they should have to go down, and by the way, everyone knew about it. Everyone knew,' Marsch said. 'That summer [2022], us and Man City were the only teams that said we made money. 'For us, we did make money, because we sold Raphinha, we sold Kalvin Phillips [to City]. We had a lot left over from what we bought. 'At the time, we weren't in a position financially to not save. Our ownership didn't have deep pockets. 'Whereas when Man City says this, I was literally like, "Are you kidding me? Is this some kind of joke?" 'When they said they got Erling Haaland for £52m, it's like: "Yeah, OK, sure". 'So, I knew there were inconsistencies in it, but what can you do? You just put your arms in the air and go, "This is football". The 2022 summer referred to by Marsch had seen clubs reveal their accounts for the 2020-21 season, which had been played behind closed doors due to the Covid-19 pandemic. Marsch questioned Man City announcing profits in the summer of 2022, along with questioning their £52m deal to sign his former player Erling Haaland from Borussia Dortmund Man City signed Kalvin Phillips from Leeds in the summer of 2022 in a £42million transfer Leeds announced an operating profit of £5.5m, with the club's income having been boosted by their return to the top flight following promotion from the Championship the previous campaign. Man City reported a narrow £2.4m profit in the same period having reported losses of £126m in the 2019-20 season. The club's run to the 2021 Champions League final and their fourth Premier League title under Pep Guardiola were cited as key reasons for their financial success. Marsch's comments also highlighted the summer transfer window in 2022, which saw Man City sign Haaland for £52m and bring in Phillips from his Leeds side in a £42m deal. Leeds also sold Brazilian star Raphinha to Barcelona for £55m, with the club using the finances from both deals to fund close to £140m of incomings. Leeds, who sacked Marsch in February 2023, were relegated at the end of the season. Daily Mail Sport reported last week that the Premier League could review transactions following 2018, the final year covered by their investigation into Man City. Man City's appeal against the independent commission verdict was made on Friday, with the club stating it 'maintains its innocence'. Much of their defence will claim commercial contracts were paid for by the Abu Dhabi government rather than their owner.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland goes off injured for Norway as Man City handed another blow
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland goes off injured for Norway as Man City handed another blow

Manchester City have endured a miserable week after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules - and now star striker Erling Haaland has picked up an injury

View 2 Images Erling Haaland asked to be substituted (Image: Miguel RIOPA / AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester City's week may have just got even worse, with star striker Erling Haaland going off injured while playing for Norway.

‌



‌



Haaland gestured to be substituted during Norway's Nations League match against Portugal on Sunday night. The City striker was replaced by Jorgen Strand Larsen in the 67th minute in Porto with the score at 1-1 after signalling to manager Stale Solbakken.

‌



Portugal then netted a second goal through Goncalo Ramos to take the lead. The home side held on to clinch the victory 2-1, despite a red card for Francisco Conceicao in the closing stages.

‌



Haaland had played every minute of Norway's previous three Nations League matches in this international break. He scored twice in the 3-2 win over Denmark before scoring in the 2-1 defeat by Portugal in the first meeting.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The City star went goalless in the 2-1 defeat by Wales before limping off against Portugal on Sunday night. City manager Enzo Maresca will now be concerned ahead of their trip to Anfield to play Liverpool on October 11.

Haaland has scored seven goals in seven games across all competitions for City so far this season. His form has been crucial to their perfect record in the Premier League, with Maresca's side sitting top with five wins from five games.

City will already be without Phil Foden for the Liverpool game, after the midfielder was sent off for kicking Bruno Fernandes in the Manchester City. There are also doubts surrounding Nico O'Reilly, who was forced to leave the England camp with injury, and Antoine Semenyo, who didn't play for Ghana during the break.

‌



City are preparing to return to action in the league following the bombshell news that they have been found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges by an independent commission.

View 2 Images Erling Haaland embraced Stale Solbakken as he went off (Image: Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty Images)

The club have submitted an appeal, having been found to have used a "disguised funding scheme" between 2009 and 2018 to hide secret funding of more than £830million.

‌



They said in a statement: "The club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

"We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."

Sports.title: DAVID YATES: Secret Arc draw should never be repeated
Sports.content:
THE mob custom of calling for people’s heads - professionally speaking - is a scourge of the social-media age, and I can’t stand it. Imagine if the rest of us had to resign - or face the sack - every time we made a mistake. But - you knew there was a ‘but’ coming, didn’t you? - I do wonder whether the person responsible for the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe draw farce last week is in the right line of work. The final field for Europe’s middle-distance championship was, as usual, declared last Thursday morning. But the stalls allocation was kept a closely guarded secret until Thursday evening. We finally got to learn that Diamond Necklace, who went on to finish third in the race to winner Daryz, was on the outside in stall 16 and Benvenuto Cellini was on the inside in one at just after 7.45pm, UK time.

View 2 Images Mickael Barzalona and Daryz win the Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe from Bacy City Roller and Diamond Necklace (Image: Getty Images)

Let’s put to one side the scope for skulduggery - and it’s greatly to the credit of the draw custodians that there were no suggestions of leaks during the day.

You can’t put interest, and betting, on one of the world ’s most important horse races into cold storage - 72 hours before it’s due to be run - while the champagne is in the fridge. Punters need information as soon as it’s available - it can’t be locked away for hours, just for the sake of some swanky Parisian soirée. God forbid any of the British Horseracing Authority top brass were watching and thought it was a good idea. This was the first time there has been such a hiatus between the release of the declarations and the draw - and it must be the last.

‌



GAMBLING COMMISSION STATISTICS ARE NOT TRUE

ANOTHER bad week for the wretched Gambling Commission, the unelected body that wields huge power over how we bet. The anti-gambling commission’s Young People and Gambling Survey, formalised in a report published last year, found that 7% of those questioned had been “prompted to spend money on gambling” by advertising. This statistic, which translates to approximately 200,000 people between 11 and 17 in Britain, has been quoted multiple times in Parliament, and is worrying, if true. It isn’t. The commission has admitted respondents could merely be reporting “feelings” of being prompted, rather than actually gambling. A big difference, as anyone who has experienced “feelings” about doing something - but hasn’t actually done them - will attest. These facts and figures are being used to reshape, and constrain, the gambling landscape - but the numbers are built on quicksand.

MILLIONS WILL BE TRADED IN YEARLING SALES

AUTUMN means the yearling sales, and the brand leader is indisputably Tattersalls Book 1, which begins on Tuesday. Three days of feverish bidding in the famous auction ring, with the sport’s global superpowers locking horns to secure the most-prized young stock. What could be more dramatic? You certainly have to admire those prepared to put their hands in their pockets - for no guarantee of return. The 10 top lots at last year’s Book 1 sale cost a combined 20,000,000 guineas. So far, they’ve won £62,333 on the track.

Sports.title: Rico Lewis gets first England call for two years as stars recover after Croatia thumping
Sports.content:
Rico Lewis gets first England call for two years as stars recover after Croatia thumping

Thomas Tuchel has turned to Manchester City full-back Rico Lewis to bolster the numbers for England's Nations League match against Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday

View 2 Images Rico Lewis has been promoted from England under-21s to the senior team (Image: Nigel French/Getty Images)

Rico Lewis has been called up England’s senior squad for the Nations League clash with Czech Republic on Tuesday.

‌



‌



Manchester City full-back Lewis, 21, has been promoted from Lee Carsley’s under-21s squad who he helped secure qualification for next year’s Euros. Lewis has five senior caps but won the last of those in November 2024 and this his first big chance under current boss Thomas Tuchel.

‌



Versatile Lewis can play both full-back roles and has played in midfield. He gets his chance after City team-mate Nico O’Reilly went home injured from Croatia.

‌



England’s thumping seven-goal win in Croatia puts them in a strong position to qualify and if they beat Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday it will be a huge step to reaching the latter stages.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Tuchel has admitted that it will be difficult for players to start all the games and calling up Lewis gives him more options. The Manchester City star played in the under-21s' 0-0 draw against Slovakia in Stoke on Friday night, a result which assured them of qualification for next summer's European Championship.

Lewis Hall and Jarell Quansah started the Croatia trashing in the full-back positions, with Myles Lewis-Skelly and Trent Alexander-Arnold also in the squad.

O'Reilly played the full 90 minutes in England's 3-2 defeat by Spain but was absent from the squad that defeated the Czech Republic 2-0 in Prague. England had originally decided not to call up a replacement, but that stance has changed after the thrashing of Croatia.

‌



View 2 Images England have been doing reformer pilates as part of their recovery after thrashing Croatia (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

Tuchel spoke about his approach to squad rotation in the build-up to the first game against Czech Republic in Prague on Tuesday. “Why would I do this and start giving the players the impression that it’s OK to take a step back or share a half or to rest one match?" he said.

"I would never. It’s madness. We want to win the next match. I would love not to rotate but I am not sure if it’s possible. An ideal scenario would be to go again and go again and go again. With six or seven players minimum that start again – to put the responsibility on them and for them to feel the trust.”

Article continues below

England started the three-week international break with five withdrawals from the original squad. Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento all pulled out, raising the issue of the fixture schedule once again.

Lewis has two goals in 12 appearances for the England under-21s and has featured three times across all competitions for Enzo Maresca's City this season. He's been an unused substitute in each of City's last four Premier League matches, with Josko Gvardiol preferred at left-back and Matheus Nunes at right-back.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes changes his Cristiano Ronaldo tune after refusing to take Man Utd stance
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes changes his Cristiano Ronaldo tune after refusing to take Man Utd stance

Bruno Fernandes has made his feelings clear on Cristiano Ronaldo's spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes and Cristiano Ronaldo may have played together for the last time (Image: Getty Images)

Bruno Fernandes has performed a U-turn in the wake of the former Manchester United star's fallout with Portugal boss Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo stormed out of the Portugal camp after being an unused substitute for the 2-1 Nations League win over Norway.

‌



‌



They then won 4-2 in Denmark without Ronaldo, who announced on Instagram that he would in "due course… tell all the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons" behind his decision to walk out on his country.

‌



Current United captain Fernandes, who also played alongside Ronaldo during his second spell at Old Trafford, maintains that whenever the dust settles from the fallout, there can be no question of just what the 41-year-old has achieved for his country, calling him the "greatest symbol of our national team and country for everything he has done in Portugal and around the world."

‌



He added: "He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of the Portuguese people."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd legend makes 'worried' claim about Liverpool star with Premier League prediction READ MORE :

It's a far cry from the frosty response Ronaldo got from Fernandes following his acrimonious departure from United four years ago in the wake of his infamous Piers Morgan interview.

‌



On that occasion, Fernandes refused to take sides, saying: "I don't feel uncomfortable. I don't have to pick a side. It was a dream come true to play with Cristiano [at United] but nothing lasts forever."

View 3 Images Fernandes appeared to snub Ronaldo in 2022

At the same time, footage emerged of the pair sharing an awkward handshake as they joined up for international duty. Fernandes later insisted he was joking with Ronaldo and that there was no issue between the pair.

‌



Asked if he had a problem with Ronaldo after a 4-0 win over Nigeria, he told Sky Sports: "I have no problem with anyone. I do my job and as a manager once said to me, everything that you can control is yourself. I think everyone thinks the same way, you have to control yourself, give your best and that's it."

Fernandes and Ronaldo may have played together for the final time after Ronaldo reportedly rejected peace talks with Jesus, his former manager at Al-Nassr.

View 3 Images Ronaldo wasn't happy about being an unused substitute against Norway (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Jesus said he would be willing to meet with Ronaldo but only after the Nations League game against Norway on Sunday. Ronaldo seems to have shunned that option after arranging to fly back to Saudi Arabia on a private jet, according to the Portuguese outlet Abola .

It had been claimed by Record that a meeting between Ronaldo and Jesus could have taken place in Madrid in the coming days, but that now looks unlikely.

Sports.title: World's largest stadium twice the size of Anfield takes shape in £28billion build
Sports.content:
World's largest stadium twice the size of Anfield takes shape in £28billion build

The world's largest stadium is set to open its doors for the first time next summer

View 3 Images The Trong Dong Stadium is set to look like this and hold 135,000 spectators (Image: TRONG DONG STADIUM)

Extraordinary images have emerged showing the building works for what is set to become the world’s largest stadium. Construction of the 135,000-seater VinFast Trong Dong Stadium in Hanoi, Vietnam, began nine months ago.

‌



‌



The stadium, named after and modelled on a traditional Vietnamese bronze drum, will have the largest capacity out of any stadium in the world, capable of hosting more than twice the number of Liverpool’s home, Anfield. It is hoped that it will open its doors by July 2027.

‌



It is being built at the centre of the broader Olympic Sports City development, which Reuters reports will cover around 22,200 acres on the outskirts of Hanoi. The total cost of the project is reportedly around $38billion (£28.8bn).

‌



Construction teams are working non-stop shifts to meet a demanding schedule. The reinforced concrete structure must be completed by December 2026, after which the installation of the dome system, electrical systems and finishing work will begin.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The retractable roof is reportedly scheduled to be in place by May 2027, with the goal of opening the completed stadium in July 2027, one year ahead of the original target date of August 2028.

‌



Recent images of the building site show the ambitious project taking shape, with several cranes visible as the eye-catching vision comes to life. The colossal stadium already features steel columns, understood to be hydraulic jacking towers weighing more than 15,000 tonnes and rising 80 metres.

View 3 Images The project is currently nine months in as part of the Olympic Sports City development (Image: VTCNEWS)

Their function is to lift the steel arch modules, which will form the stadium's retractable dome, from the ground. Once completed, it will be the largest roof of its kind in the world.

‌



Designs suggest it will have a circular gold dome shaped like a trong dong drum, with a diameter of 408 metres. Its architecture reproduces the motifs of Dong Son bronze drums, considered a symbol of ancient Vietnamese culture.

They represent "the spirit of community, strength, and longevity," according to the project's architects. The stated intention is for the stadium to become "an architectural and cultural icon representing Vietnam in the new era."

View 3 Images The stadium will have the largest capacity in the world (Image: Trong Dong Stadium)

Article continues below

Vietnamese authorities are hoping that the facility will enable them to bid to host events on the scale of the World Cup or the Olympic Games.

The projected capacity of 135,000 will easily surpass other football stadiums. The biggest football ground in the world is currently the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium in Pyongyang, North Korea, which can host around 114,000.

Morocco’s Hassan II Stadium (115,000), is second. The ground is currently under construction for the 2030 World Cup.

Sports.title: Arsenal star has perfect chance to restore Mikel Arteta's faith after double injury blow
Sports.content:
When Viktor Gyokeres trudged off the pitch at Brighton, he must've thought that his Arsenal career was at its lowest ebb. No goals this season and no starts in the Premier League saw Gyokeres jet off to Sweden with his shoulders down.

But he'll be walking chest out when he steps off his flight to London next week after three goals - and counting - for his country. The striker broke his duck in Stockholm against Romania, sealed Sweden's win over Poland and then helped them earn a handy point away to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

He'll no doubt be looking to cash in when Sweden play winless Romania again on Monday, but he'll also have one eye on making sure that he's fit for Saturday's clash with Leeds. That's because, as fate would have it, Kai Havertz is a major doubt for Arsenal's next fixture after suffering an injury for Germany.

The Gunners were then hit with another blow when Christos Tzolis went down in Greece's game on Thursday. It means that Arteta is likely to be forced into making two changes to his starting line-up against Leeds.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Gyokeres has largely played second fiddle to Havertz this season, featuring in only five of Arsenal's seven games. Arteta clearly favours the German and his decision has been justified, with Havertz starting the campaign strongly by scoring three goals. But injury could curtail his good form.

In contrast, Gyokeres is just hitting his stride. His run of goals has seen him break a record by becoming the first player to score in six successive Nations League matches, stretching back to the 2024-25 edition.

‌



Even Arsenal's next opponent is favourable for Gyokeres. The 28-year-old scored three times in two games against Leeds last season, including a brace on his home debut.

After the visit of Leeds, the games come thick and fast. Arsenal resume their Champions League campaign at home to Lille on October 13 before travelling to Nottingham Forest and Bayern Munich over the following eight days.

Should Viktor Gyokeres start against Leeds? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 2 Images Viktor Gyokeres has found his shooting boots again on international duty (Image: Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Gyokeres' situation is a reminder of how quickly things can change in football. A matter of weeks ago, the former Sporting Lisbon hitman was being tipped for the exit door.

A swap deal involving Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez was mooted but never materialised. Gyokeres, though, is 'extremely happy' to be at the Emirates.

"Of course, there was a lot of speculation," Gyokeres acknowledged earlier this week. "But I had a full pre-season, and it felt good. I was fully focused on Arsenal. For me, staying was a given. I'm extremely happy at the club.

"It's clear that I want to play football as much as possible. Hopefully that will come, too. You always want to be on the field as a football player. Of course, you expect more playing time, but we have an extremely good squad with a lot of good players and have been doing well here at the start."

‌

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
