Sports.title: “I guess it’s my fault” says Norris as stewards reprimand him for near-miss under Safety Car | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris admitted he was caught out by how quickly the field slowed ahead of him during the Safety Car period.

The McLaren driver almost ran into his team mate Oscar Piastri as they approached turn one in the queue behind the Safety Car. The incident occured as George Russell ahead of them slowed unexpectedly and came to a stop on the right-hand side of the track next to the pit lane entrance.

Norris said he noticed the Mercedes slowing but was unsure how much the cars ahead of him were reacting.

“I couldn’t see from the angle, and just from where I was, how much everyone had stopped because of George on the inside,” said Norris. “By the time I kind of looked at George and looked back, I could see them, but it’s hard when you’re directly behind to see if they’re going 100 [kph], 200 or 10.

“They were going 10, so I just got completely caught out. I guess it’s my fault in the end of the day. I was just unlucky with it everyone just checked up so much and I just got screwed over by it, that’s all.”

Norris narrowly missed hitting Piastri, ran onto the gravel trap on the outside then rejoined the queue having lost several places.

The stewards have summoned Norris for “driving erratically under Safety Car conditions, leaving the track and re-joining unsafely and/or overtaking another car behind the Safety Car.”

Alexander Albon is also under investigation for driving erratically in another incident which involved Piastri. The Williams driver, who was following his team mate Carlos Sainz Jnr into the pits during an earlier Safety Car deployment, appeared to slow, causing Piastri to take avoiding action.

Update: Norris has been reprimanded for his incident and Albon has been cleared.

Stewards’ verdict on Norris

While following the Safety Car, [Norris] approached turn one behind a group of cars. Car 63 (George Russell) had stopped with a mechanical problem ahead of turn one, which caused the cars ahead of Norris to slow down. Norris explained that, due to the low sun and resulting visibility conditions, it was difficult to recognise that the cars ahead had started to slow earlier than would normally have been expected. Norris consequently misjudged his closing speed and approached the cars ahead too quickly. When he realised this, he braked heavily and deliberately steered to the left, onto the kerbs and then into the gravel bed in order to avoid contact with the cars ahead. By driving onto the kerbs, Norris had reduced grip available for braking, which further limited his ability to slow the car. In doing so, Norris momentarily overshot car 81 (Oscar Piastri), who was directly ahead of him. The stewards considered whether this constituted an overtake while the Safety Car was deployed. Although Norris momentarily moved ahead of Piastri, this occurred solely as a consequence of Norris leaving the track while taking avoiding action. [Piastri] immediately repassed Norris while Norris was off the track. The stewards therefore determined that this did not constitute an overtaking manoeuvre and take no further action in respect of this aspect of the incident. The stewards also considered that, particularly while driving behind the Safety Car, Norris should have managed the gap to the cars ahead and his closing speed with greater care. The prevailing visibility conditions were circumstances which Norris should have taken into account when determining an appropriate speed and gap to the cars ahead, rather than a reason which excused the resulting driving. The need for heavy braking and an avoiding manoeuvre into the gravel demonstrated that Norris had not maintained an appropriate margin in the circumstances. The stewards therefore determined that Norris had driven erratically in breach of Article B5.13.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations. Such a situation should not arise while driving behind the Safety Car, and Norris was required to maintain a sufficient margin to the cars ahead. However, taking into account that Norris reacted promptly once he recognised the situation and successfully avoided contact, the stewards consider a reprimand as appropriate. The stewards separately considered Norris’s return to the track. Although car 18 (Lance Stroll) was in relative close proximity, Norris returned progressively and without requiring [Stroll] to take avoiding action or otherwise creating an unsafe situation. The stewards therefore determined that the re-join was safe. The stewards also reviewed whether, after having re-joined the track, Norris had overtaken Stroll while the Safety Car was deployed. The video evidence showed that, as Norris returned from the gravel, he had already crossed the white line with at least one wheel and, as such, was back on track. At this point, he was ahead of Stroll and at no point did Norris pass Stroll. Rather, Stroll approached Norris while Norris was already in the process of returning to the track. The stewards therefore determined that Norris had not overtaken Stroll under Safety Car conditions and as such also take no further action for this part of the incident. Accordingly, the stewards impose a reprimand on Norris for erratic driving. No further action is taken in relation to the re-join or the alleged overtake while the Safety Car was deployed.

Stewards’ verdict on Albon

On the approach to the pit entry, [Albon] reduced his speed, causing Piastri, who was following closely behind, to brake and take avoiding action. No collision or contact occurred. Albon explained that immediately before entering the pit entry road he became aware that he was below the required delta time and therefore reduced his speed in order to comply with the applicable delta requirement. Piastri confirmed, having heard Albon’s explanation, that he considered the reason for Albon’s actions understandable. While the situation required a significant reaction from Piastri and could potentially have developed into a dangerous situation, the stewards were satisfied that Albon’s actions were taken in an attempt to comply with the applicable delta requirements and explained the otherwise unusual reduction in speed at that location. His actions, therefore, did not constitute erratic or unnecessarily dangerous driving in the circumstances. Having considered the matter extensively, the stewards determine that no infringement occurred and accordingly take no further action.

Sports.title: Hadjar had “no battery” to defend from Hamilton and Leclerc in final laps | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar said he was unable to defend his podium position in the final laps of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The Red Bull driver held third place behind his team mate and Andrea Kimi Antonelli during the final Safety Car period. However he had both Ferraris close behind him.

Once the race restarted, Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc quick picked him off. Hadjar took the chequered flag in fifth place.

Hadjar successfully resisted Hamilton for many laps earlier in the race when his rival was on the medium tyre compound. However once Hamilton switched to soft tyres under the Safety Car, Hadjar fell prey to the Ferrari.

“I had no battery, something like that,” he explained. “So there was no contest against the Ferraris in the straight.”

However Hadjar was unhappy with his pace earlier in the race as well. “I don’t know what happened in terms of the grip I had on the car,” he said. “The whole race I was so slow.

“I don’t know what happened to my pace, but [it] really [was] one race to put in the bin.”

“We’ll fix the issue and understand why we are so bad today,” he added.

Sports.title: George Groves Questions Ben Whittaker’s Knockout Power
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker’s recent knockouts built an image that Conor Wallace put under pressure on Saturday. Against an opponent who kept answering, the 29-year-old Olympic silver medalist could no longer rely on speed and clean punches to control the exchanges.

Whittaker won a unanimous decision in Birmingham and secured the IBF mandatory position for Dmitry Bivol. His desperate final round nevertheless raised questions about how much his earlier stoppages had demonstrated.

“The knockout wins of late – are they a tiny bit generous in what they now spell? Maybe he’s not the murderous puncher that the record suggests,” George Groves said on his YouTube channel.

Matchroom and Boxxer before them repeatedly placed Whittaker in showcase fights. Those bouts gave him opportunities to display his movement and finishing punches, but offered limited preparation for sustained resistance. At 29, with extensive amateur experience, he needed a more demanding progression.

Braian Nahuel Suarez had lost three of his previous six fights. Richard Rivera arrived after roughly 17 months out, with his two most recent victories coming against Roger Guerrero and Devaun Lee. Their records entering those fights were 17–8–1 and 11–11–1, respectively.

The warning had already appeared against Liam Cameron in their first meeting. Before both fighters went over the ropes, Whittaker was struggling with Cameron’s pressure. The fall and injury dominated the aftermath, overshadowing the uncomfortable exchanges that preceded them. Cameron was below world level, yet he had disrupted Whittaker’s control.

Wallace brought that concern back. As Groves observed, he threw alongside Whittaker rather than waiting for the faster fighter to finish and escape. Landing first did not prevent Whittaker from being hit in return.

His upright retreats and reliance on holding became liabilities as Wallace closed the distance. Too little short offense discouraged the Australian from continuing forward, while retreating toward the ropes reduced Whittaker’s room to escape.

That is the developmental cost of repeated showcases: weaknesses can remain unresolved while expectations rise. Whittaker has earned his mandatory position, but Wallace showed how much work remains before a Bivol fight.

Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr Faces Smaller Money Beyond Benn
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr’s possible fight with Michael Zerafa presents a funding problem after two lucrative bouts against Conor Benn. Zerafa accuses him of pricing himself out, but matching Eubank’s financial expectations could be difficult for a fight without the same commercial appeal.

A promoter would have to make the numbers work. Without Saudi backing, that means relying on ticket sales, broadcast revenue, sponsorship and any outside funding secured in Australia. A $10 million purse for Eubank would be difficult to justify against Zerafa, however competitive the fight might be.

“We want the Eubank fight. Our teams have been back and forth. I believe I beat him. I believe that love for the sport’s not there anymore. He’s chasing just money fights,” Zerafa told iFL TV. “I feel like he knows I’m a risk … that’s why he’s pricing himself out a little bit.”

Zerafa’s view of Eubank’s motivation is his own. Waiting for another Benn payday would make financial sense, particularly when Zerafa offers a potentially difficult fight for less money. Eubank could lose and damage the appeal of a trilogy before getting back to the opponent who produced his biggest earning opportunities.

The Australian acknowledges that Benn is competing for the fight, accusing him of trying to prevent their matchup by pursuing a third meeting with Eubank.

Zerafa also claims his team and Matchroom have pursued government support to stage the contest in Melbourne. That suggests they are seeking additional money to meet Eubank’s demands, although Zerafa confirms that official contracts have not been completed. He provides no agreed purse or confirmed funding amount.

Two large paydays can change what a fighter considers an acceptable offer. Eubank may still want to compete, but returning to smaller money against a dangerous opponent is a harder proposition when Benn remains a possibility.

Zerafa can push for the opportunity. Getting Eubank to accept it requires an offer attractive enough to compensate him for risking his next bigger payday.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Pushes Zuffa to Fund Costly Opponents
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson wants Zuffa Boxing to pay for fights against Gary Antuanne Russell or Raymond Muratalla, claiming on X that both want $3 million to face him. That would leave the promoter with a substantial opponent bill before covering its own headliner.

“Gary & Muratalla want 3ms to get in the ring with me.. I would love to fight both them guys tho Zuffa gotta cough that 💰 up!” Shakur wrote on X. “I’m the biggest risk in the sport the Teo fight didn’t do nun but make it worst lol.”

The $3 million figures are Shakur’s account of their demands. His post does not reveal his own purse or establish how close Zuffa is to securing either opponent.

That missing number is significant. If Shakur’s payday exceeds what Russell or Muratalla would receive, Zuffa could face more than $6 million in main-event purses alone. The undercard, production, and other event expenses would increase the cost further.

Neither matchup looks like an obvious pay-per-view seller. Russell and Muratalla offer credible opposition, but neither has established himself as a major commercial attraction. Shakur has yet to demonstrate that he can consistently generate the paying audience needed to make purses at that level profitable.

The sporting appeal is easier to explain. Either opponent would give Shakur a meaningful fight at light welterweight and give Zuffa something substantial to promote. Turning that quality into enough revenue to cover the bill is the harder task.

Zuffa could still justify the expense through subscriptions, audience growth, and establishing Shakur as a regular headliner. An individual event does not necessarily have to turn a profit to serve those goals.

Even so, willingness to spend heavily does not make every asking price worthwhile. Shakur has publicly identified two opponents he would accept. Now Zuffa must decide whether the business either fight could generate supports the money required to deliver it.

Sports.title: Four Perfect Boxing Records Leave Unanswered Questions
Sports.content:
Rocky Marciano, Floyd Mayweather Jr., Joe Calzaghe and Terence Crawford each reached retirement with at least 40 professional victories and no losses or draws. Those records deserve recognition, but they cannot answer what would have happened against the dangerous opponents each left unfought.

An unbeaten record reflects completed fights. Retirement closes the book before another challenger can change it. The question is how much the zero tells us when assessing these four champions.

Rocky Marciano: 49-0, 43 Knockouts

Marciano won the heavyweight championship by knocking out Jersey Joe Walcott in the 13th round in September 1952. He made six successful defenses before retiring in 1956, including victories over Walcott, Roland LaStarza, Ezzard Charles and Archie Moore.

Floyd Patterson subsequently won the vacant championship, while Sonny Liston developed into the division’s most destructive challenger. Patterson’s speed and combinations would have presented a different test for Marciano. Liston’s jab, reach, and power make him an especially difficult hypothetical opponent.

The timing needs qualification. Liston was still an inexperienced professional and was inactive when Marciano retired. Marciano would have needed to extend his career for several years to face the Liston who later dominated the division. That remains an unanswered matchup, rather than evidence that Marciano avoided an established challenger.

Floyd Mayweather Jr.: 50-0, 27 Knockouts

Mayweather’s five-division championship career included immediate rematches against Jose Luis Castillo and Marcos Maidana, two opponents who troubled him in their first meetings. Those return victories strengthened his unbeaten record.

However, Keith Thurman remained an unanswered welterweight test when Mayweather stepped away from conventional championship boxing. Crawford and Errol Spence also became formidable champions, although their strongest claims emerged later. Facing them would have required Mayweather to continue competing against the next generation as he aged.

Instead, his 50th victory came against Conor McGregor, a UFC champion making his professional boxing debut. It extended the number beyond Marciano’s famous 49-0, but offered less evidence about Mayweather’s ability to beat the leading active boxers. His subsequent announcement of a professional comeback also complicates describing his retirement as final.

Joe Calzaghe: 46-0, 32 Knockouts

Calzaghe made 21 successful defenses of his WBO super middleweight title and defeated Jeff Lacy, Mikkel Kessler, Bernard Hopkins and Roy Jones Jr. before retiring in February 2009.

Carl Froch and Chad Dawson were younger opponents who could have tested him further. Froch offered durability, pressure and a willingness to sustain a physical fight. Dawson presented a different challenge through his size, southpaw stance, and boxing ability at light heavyweight.

Calzaghe had already achieved enough to justify retirement. Nevertheless, beating Hopkins and Jones did not settle how he would have handled those younger challengers. His perfect record leaves that debate open.

Terence Crawford: 42-0, 31 Knockouts

Crawford’s unanimous decision victory over Canelo Alvarez in September 2025 completed a remarkable climb through five championship divisions. He announced retirement that December after becoming undisputed champion in three weight classes.

Yet Christian Mbilli, Osleys Iglesias, Lester Martinez and Hamzah Sheeraz offered further potential tests at super middleweight. Jaron Ennis remained another compelling possibility, subject to an agreement on weight.

Those opponents would have asked different questions. Sustained pressure, punching power, size, and youth could have forced Crawford into fights unlike the one he won against Canelo. None was guaranteed to beat him, but defeating one champion did not establish that he would defeat every challenger around that division.

All four fighters earned their perfect records. The limitation comes when those records are treated as proof of invincibility. Retirement preserved the zero while leaving difficult fights unresolved, and those unanswered tests belong in any assessment of their careers.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Sr. Questions Chicago’s Title Fight Weight Restriction
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield Sr. is questioning how his son’s team allowed Kid Austin to approach his Chicago title fight against Lucas Bahdi without explaining Illinois’ 10-pound weight restriction. He claims the fighter discovered the requirement online himself rather than hearing it from the people handling his career.

“My whole team, nobody said, ‘Yo, listen.’ It wasn’t in the contract. Nothing. So to me, you know, it’s like, ‘All right, cool. I understand the playing field now.’ You know, luckily Kid went online yesterday, and he found out himself,” Schofield Sr. said to MillCity Boxing.

Illinois’ boxing rules limit contestants in title bouts to gaining no more than 10 pounds above their official weight by the fight-day weight check. A fighter recording 135 pounds would therefore have a 145-pound limit at that check. This is a state requirement that applies to both contestants.

Sr. argues that Chicago was a questionable choice for a large lightweight, particularly when neither fighter has an established following there, in his view. He also claims Oscar De La Hoya’s side told him they were unaware of the restriction.

The strongest complaint is the alleged failure to communicate. A second weight requirement affects how a fighter plans his recovery after making the lightweight limit. Discovering it late creates an avoidable complication during the final preparations, even if the team can comfortably meet it.

However, Sr.’s suggestion that the location was deliberately selected to disadvantage his son is unsupported by evidence in the interview. The restriction itself does not establish that anyone targeted Kid Austin.

Sr. also insists the limit will have no effect, claiming his son is already 146 pounds, fully hydrated, and completing 15 rounds in training. That makes this primarily a dispute over preparation and trust.

If Kid Austin is as close to the required weight as his father claims, the team can manage the restriction. What Sr. wants explained is why his son had to discover it himself.

Sports.title: Jermall Charlo Targets Jaime Munguia for Houston Fight
Sports.content:
Jermall Charlo wants Jaime Munguia in Houston as he pursues a world title at super middleweight. The matchup gives Charlo a recognizable opponent with an attacking style that would test whether his confidence at 168 is backed by enough remaining ability to contend.

“The fight with [Munguia] makes the most sense,” Charlo said to Fight Hub TV. “I’d love to fight him right here in Houston. Mexican crowd, sold out.”

Charlo also floated appearing on a Canelo Alvarez card in Mexico, although he gave no indication that negotiations with Munguia have begun. Houston is his preferred location, and the appeal is straightforward: a hometown appearance against a popular Mexican fighter offers a bigger occasion than another routine comeback bout.

The harder question is what Charlo would have to produce once the punches start flying. Munguia’s willingness to exchange would give him opportunities to land his jab and right hand, but it would also demand sustained work. Charlo could not count on controlling the fight through isolated bursts if Munguia kept pressing and throwing combinations.

That makes this a useful test of Charlo’s stated ambition. He insists he feels stronger and mentally focused, but a busy opponent would require him to demonstrate those qualities across rounds. Looking sharp early would only be part of the job; maintaining his timing and output as the pressure builds would be more revealing.

Charlo clarified that his description of a “last run” refers to pursuing another world title, rather than announcing that retirement is approaching. He wants to become a champion in a third division and has no intention of moving to light heavyweight.

A Munguia fight fits that goal, provided Charlo can earn it with his performances. Winning would strengthen his case for a title opportunity at 168. Merely securing the Houston date would deliver the occasion he wants, while leaving the toughest part of his comeback to be settled in the ring.

Charlo’s prolonged inactivity makes his championship talk impossible to take seriously. At 36, he crawls back from a 17-month layoff following his May 2025 mismatch against Thomas LaManna. That blowout was supposed to launch a real schedule, yet he immediately went missing again. Managing three fights since 2021 tells fans everything about his reliability against live contenders at super middleweight.

Munguia demands more than empty talk about feeling rejuvenated. Relentless pressure and combination punching will expose whether Charlo possesses the engine to survive deep water after wasting prime years on the sofa. Title dreams require round-by-round ring work, not endless vacations between appearances.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Rematch Tests Queensberry’s Faith in Itauma
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic wants another fight with Moses Itauma and believes he can improve on his first performance. Whether Queensberry would approve another meeting with the heavyweight champion remains uncertain after the Croatian exposed Itauma’s difficulty sustaining his attack.

Hrgovic first needs to deal with mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez. Even if he wins, there is no assurance Itauma’s promoters will send their young heavyweight back against someone who absorbed his punches and stopped him in the ninth round on August 29.

“It was a big win and a big achievement, but I feel I can do better. I should throw more and be faster. He was countering me. He was really fast, and he put me in a little bit of insecurity, but I should have thrown more and been more aggressive. If a rematch happens, I’ll smash him,” Hrgovic told The Stomping Ground.

Hrgovic’s proposed approach has risks. Throwing more punches could increase the pressure on Itauma, but it would also give the faster heavyweight additional countering opportunities. Hrgovic needs better entries and punch selection to avoid repeating the difficulties he experienced before Itauma faded.

Queensberry faces a more consequential decision about Itauma’s development. Returning him to aging opponents who cannot withstand his early attacks might restore confidence, but quick knockouts would offer little evidence that he has learned to pace himself.

Itauma entered the Hrgovic fight with just 31 professional rounds. His matchmaking had given him limited experience of opponents remaining dangerous after surviving his opening assault. Another series of short fights would leave that question unanswered.

He needs opponents capable of extending him and making him work through rounds without an immediate finish. That would give his team a better measure of his progress before considering another Hrgovic fight.

Waiting alone will not solve the problem. Itauma cannot assume his exceptional hand speed will remain unchanged throughout his career, and maintaining his conditioning as his body develops will require discipline.

Queensberry can rebuild his confidence through favorable matchmaking. Preparing him to beat Hrgovic requires something more demanding: fights that test whether he can remain effective when an opponent refuses to go away.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker’s Showboating Gives Opponents Another Opening
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker’s showboating gave Conor Wallace opportunities to hit him after seemingly losing an exchange on Saturday night. Tony Bellew believes Whittaker has the talent to pull off those antics, but Wallace exposed what happens when an opponent keeps attacking instead of admiring them.

Whittaker would make Wallace miss or land a shot, then pause to showboat. Wallace pursued him and punched again. Making the first attack fail did not leave Whittaker safe from the next one, particularly when his attention shifted toward entertaining the crowd.

“You’re either good enough to do it, or you’re not. He is good enough to do it,” Bellew said on DAZN’s Beyond the Bell. “I don’t care if anyone’s a fan of it or you’re not. Are you good enough to pull this kind of stuff off? Are you good enough to try and be another Naseem Hamed? He is good enough.”

That defense overlooks the work Whittaker still needs to do after a successful exchange. He must leave punching range, recover his position, or stay ready to defend. Celebrating a slip or a landed punch gives a persistent opponent time to close the distance.

The same weakness appeared against Arlen Lopez in the Olympic final. Whittaker’s showboating did little to discourage the Cuban, who cut off the ring and landed punches. Against that kind of pressure, the extra movement becomes wasted energy when it fails to create a safer position or another scoring opportunity. Whittaker had nowhere to go because his feet were out of position from the routine.

Bellew described Whittaker’s late trouble against Wallace as switching off. Yet the showboating itself encourages those interruptions in concentration. An opponent does not have to accept that an exchange is finished simply because Whittaker starts performing.

Whittaker’s survival showed toughness, but it did not validate the antics that helped put him in danger. Wallace supplied a practical reason to shorten the performance between punches. Better opponents will keep working through it.

Prince Naseem Hamed had explosive, one-punch equalizer power that made opponents hesitant to rush him even when he clowned. Whittaker does not possess that kind of stopping power at light heavyweight. If he continues to pause for dramatic effect instead of completing his defensive recovery, world-class operators will time those mental lapses and put him on the floor.

Ghana News.title: NPP’s new executives will not alter our 2028 preparations – Tanko-Computer
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Sofo Tanko Rashid Computer, Deputy National Director of Elections and IT for NDC

The National Democratic Congress (NDC) says the outcome of the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) national executive elections will not change its preparations or political strategy for the 2028 general elections.

NDC Deputy Director of Elections and Information Technology, Rashid Tanko-Computer, said his party remains focused on its own organisational processes and on selecting leaders it believes can advance its agenda ahead of the next presidential and parliamentary elections.

Speaking in a media interview after the NPP’s national executive elections on Saturday, October 3, Tanko-Computer said the NPP had failed to produce the calibre of national executives he expected and argued that the outcome did not present a significant challenge to the NDC.

According to him, the NDC had expected the NPP to emerge from the elections with a leadership team capable of mounting a stronger challenge in 2028, but he said the composition of the new executive body fell short of that expectation.

“They have missed a glorious opportunity to give us a run for our money because the kind of officers I was expecting them to bring, they didn’t. This will not even impact anything due to the way we choose our leaders,” he said.

“We have a style of choosing our leaders, and you saw how we did it in 2022 and then when we were going into the 2024 election,” Tanko-Computer added.

He also compared the newly elected NPP executives with the NDC’s current national officers, arguing that his party’s leadership structure would be more attractive to voters if the two organisations were placed side by side.

“Even currently, if you look at the officers that they have elected and our national officers currently, put them side by side and ask Ghanaians to vote for a party that will mean business and that will bring something on the table for them, and they will definitely go for the NDC,” he said.

Tanko-Computer’s comments come after the NPP completed its national executive elections at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi, with the party’s new leadership now expected to begin preparations towards the 2028 elections.

Ghana News.title: Tema East MP urges men to take active role in breast cancer awareness
Ghana News.content:
Tema East MP Isaac Ashai Odamtten has called on men to take a more active role in breast cancer awareness by encouraging women to pay attention to unusual breast changes and seek medical care promptly.

He said breast cancer should not be viewed solely as a women’s health concern, arguing that the disease affects husbands, children, families, workplaces and communities. Mr Odamtten made the call at the launch of Breast Cancer Awareness Month by the International Maritime Hospital (IMaH).

The MP urged husbands and partners to support women in prioritising their breast health and seeking professional advice when they notice warning signs such as lumps, changes in breast size or appearance, skin changes and abnormal nipple discharge.

He also called for breast health education to move beyond October and become part of everyday conversations in homes, churches, mosques, schools and workplaces.

He said sustained public education was needed to address fear, stigma and misinformation that could prevent people from seeking timely medical attention or push them towards unverified treatments.

Mr Odamtten stressed that early detection and timely treatment should remain at the centre of breast cancer awareness efforts, urging Ghanaians to take practical steps towards protecting their health rather than limiting the campaign to wearing the pink ribbon.

He further announced his commitment to fully sponsor this year’s Manhean Breast Cancer Month as part of his contribution to awareness and prevention efforts.

The Tema East MP commended IMaH and its partners for launching the campaign and encouraged men in particular to become active participants in promoting breast health among women in their families and communities.

Ghana News.title: Hawa Koomson vows to bring experience and maturity to NPP women’s wing
Ghana News.content:
Newly elected National Women’s Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Mavis Hawa Koomson, has pledged to draw on her experience and maturity as she assumes responsibility for the party’s women’s wing.

Madam Koomson secured the position at the NPP’s national elections after defeating her main contender, Hajia Safia Mohammed, who conceded defeat and congratulated her on the outcome.

Speaking to the media after the election, the former Awutu Senya East Member of Parliament expressed gratitude to supporters who backed her campaign and to the party’s election committee for overseeing the process.

“I want to thank every person who supported me till today. Their efforts have resulted in this victory,” she said.

She also acknowledged the contribution of other party leaders and officials who played roles in ensuring the successful conduct of the elections.

Asked about the kind of Women’s Organiser she intends to be, Madam Koomson pointed to her experience and maturity as the qualities she would bring to the position.

“A woman with experience and maturity,” she said.

Her election places her in charge of the NPP’s women’s wing as the party begins work under a new national executive team following its delegates conference.

She will be expected to coordinate the party’s women’s structures and contribute to its organisational activities at the grassroots and national levels.

Ghana News.title: Opare Addo cautions NDC against adopting NPP’s aggressive politics
Ghana News.content:
george opare addo

National Youth Organiser of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment, George Opare Addo, has called on the party to make ideas, policy and organisation the centre of its political competition as it prepares for its own national executive elections.

Mr Opare Addo said the NDC should resist any temptation to mirror what he considers an aggressive style of politics associated with some political actors, insisting that the party’s response to the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) newly elected leadership should not be based on confrontation.

“The NDC must not answer the NPP by becoming the NPP,” he said in a statement on Facebook on Sunday, October 4.

His comments followed the NPP’s election of a new national executive team at its National Delegates Conference in Kumasi on October 3.

John Boadu was elected National Chairman, while Justin Kodua retained the General Secretary position. Daniel Nii Kwartei Titus-Glover became National Organiser and Abanga Fuseini Yakubu was elected National Youth Organiser.

Mr Opare Addo said the NDC had an opportunity through its upcoming leadership contest to define the kind of political organisation it wanted to become, rather than allowing its internal elections to be reduced to a contest for positions.

He urged delegates to assess the party’s future in terms of its ideas, policies, organisational strength and intellectual capacity.

“We must compete with ideas. We must compete with organisation. We must compete with policy. We must compete with intellectual strength,” he said.

The NDC Youth Organiser also cautioned against political competition spilling into intimidation and violence, drawing a clear distinction between vigorous political mobilisation and actions that threaten democratic participation.

“There is a difference between being politically tough and being politically violent. There is a difference between mobilisation and intimidation. There is a difference between political competition and political warfare,” he said.

“And Ghana must never cross that line.”

Mr Opare Addo said the NDC’s forthcoming national executive elections should therefore serve as a broader conversation about the party’s political direction. He challenged delegates to consider not only who should occupy the various leadership positions but also “what kind of NDC do we want to build, and what kind of politics do we want Ghana to experience?”

Reflecting on the party’s recent history, he cited the NDC’s 2022 leadership elections as an example of an internal process that, in his view, helped reposition the party and broaden its appeal. He also pointed to the youth wing’s Green Army mobilisation as evidence that young people could be organised around political purpose and consciousness.

He warned, however, against a return to what he described as “personality, insults, factionalism and permanent confrontation”, saying such an approach would undermine the broader objectives of the party.

“The answer to aggressive politics cannot be greater aggression. The answer to political intimidation cannot be political intimidation of our own. The answer to violence must be a stronger commitment to democratic mobilisation,” he said.

Mr Opare Addo said the NDC should be prepared to compete vigorously while maintaining responsibility in the exercise of political power.

“We must be fierce in competition but responsible in power,” he said, adding that electoral victory should not become the party’s ultimate measure of success.

“Building a better Ghana is,” he said.

Ghana News.title: NPP has 35 months to prepare for 2028 after early reorganisation – Political strategist
Ghana News.content:
The New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) early completion of its internal reorganisation gives it about 35 months to prepare for the 2028 general election, political marketing strategist Dr Bernard Tutu-Boahene has observed.

Dr Tutu-Boahene, a lecturer at the Department of Entrepreneurship and Marketing at the University of Education, Winneba, said the time available could benefit the NPP if the party uses the period to develop effective strategies, rebuild public trust and strengthen its organisational structures.

He was commenting on the NPP’s national executive elections held at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3, which brought the party’s reorganisation process to a close.

The party had earlier completed elections at the polling station, constituency and regional levels and selected Dr Mahamudu Bawumia as its flagbearer for the 2028 election.

“Starting early and completing the process early enough can be advantageous because you have enough time,” Dr Tutu-Boahene said. “But it depends on what you do with your time.”

He cautioned, however, that having a longer preparation period would not automatically translate into an electoral advantage. He said the NPP’s ability to make effective use of the available time, resources and organisational capabilities would be more important than simply starting early.

“The fact that you have a longer period of time does not necessarily mean that you may be able to gain competitive advantage. What could help you to gain that competitive advantage could be the resources available to you, how best you are able to use your time, and your capabilities and competencies,” he said.

At the national executive elections, former General Secretary John Boadu was elected National Chairman with 2,888 votes, while Justin Kodua Frimpong retained the General Secretary position with 4,486 votes.

Kojo Fosu Boadu, Henry Nana Boakye, and Nana Akomea were elected First, Second, and Third Vice Chairpersons, respectively. Other elected executives included Daniel Nii Kwartei Titus-Glover as National Organiser, Alfred Kojo Thompson as National Treasurer, Abagna Yakubu Fusani as National Youth Organiser and Mavis Hawa Koomson as National Women’s Organiser.

Mohammed Ali Suraj was elected National Nasara Organiser, while Dennis Edward Miracles Aboagye was elected National Communications Director unopposed.

Dr Tutu-Boahene described the new executive as a combination of experienced politicians and younger members, saying their election placed a significant responsibility on them to restore confidence in the NPP following its defeat in the 2024 general election.

He urged the new leadership to demonstrate honesty, commitment and discipline in the discharge of their responsibilities and work to convince Ghanaians that the party could be trusted with the responsibility of governing.

The lecturer also stressed the importance of unity within the new leadership, warning that personal differences should not undermine the executives’ ability to work towards shared objectives.

“If you show that you cannot work with any member of your team, there is nothing wrong with resigning from your position for a new person to be elected,” he said.

Dr Tutu-Boahene further urged the NPP to use the 35-month period to reconnect with supporters who had become apathetic or drifted away from the party. He said the party should focus not only on its internal structures but also on rebuilding relationships with voters and communicating its plans effectively.

Although the National Democratic Congress (NDC) is yet to complete its own reorganisation, he cautioned the NPP against becoming complacent. He pointed to the NDC’s past ability to win elections despite having shorter preparation periods as evidence that the length of a campaign period must be matched by effective organisation and strategy.

“The early bird catches the worm,” Dr Tutu-Boahene said, while stressing that the NPP’s early start would only become meaningful if the party translates the additional time into concrete organisational and campaign work.

Ghana News.title: All six passengers presumed dead after plane went missing off US coast
Ghana News.content:
Six people aboard a medical transport aircraft that went missing on Saturday while it was travelling from Bermuda to Boston are presumed dead, according to a statement from the flight's operator.

On Sunday evening, the United States Coast Guard said it was ending its search for survivors off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island.

"We must now face the heartbreaking reality that the four members of our Latitude team, our patient and the patient's family escort, who were aboard Heartbeat 104, are presumed to have died," Latitude Air Ambulance said in a statement shortly thereafter.

"Our thoughts are first and foremost with their families, loved ones, friends, and colleagues."

The Federal Aviation Administration lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 plane just after 01:00 local time (05:00 GMT) on Saturday morning.

On Saturday evening, authorities located a "debris field" confirmed to be from the aircraft.

The plane departed from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at 23:40 local time on Friday night, according to FlightAware data, and was due to land at Boston's Logan International Airport at 01:30 EDT (05:30 GMT).

Four Canadian nationals and two Bermudian nationals were onboard.

"This is an unimaginable loss for our Latitude family and for everyone who loved the six people aboard Heartbeat 104," said Peter Byl, President of Latitude Air Ambulance, on Sunday evening.

"Our focus now is on supporting their families, supporting our people and assisting the authorities. We will honour our colleagues by remembering the care, professionalism, and commitment they brought to their work every day."

Latitude Air Ambulance is a Canadian company that provides international medical flights for patients returning home.

Two pilots and two medical staff, both Canadian, had flown to Bermuda to collect a patient and their relative, Clarence Togeretz, director of flight operations at Latitude, told CBC News.

FlightAware's tracker shows that the aircraft significantly dropped in altitude before its communications went dark, plummeting from around 7,300m (24,000ft) to 3,300m (11,000ft).

Radio transmissions show trouble with communications between the air traffic controller and the pilot, the Boston Globe reported, based on transmissions provided by LiveATC.net.

"You're coming in blind? Is that what you said?" the air traffic controller asked. "Are you declaring an emergency, or no?"

The pilot's response was inaudible.

"You're coming in a little weak so I didn't hear what your response was, if you were declaring an emergency or not," the air traffic controller said, according to the Globe.

The air traffic controller later confirmed the pilot had declared an emergency.

An area fire dispatcher asked emergency crews just after 01:00 EDT to prepare to meet a plane with an "electrical issue".

The dispatcher later said "the aircraft has lost radio and radar".

Latitude said in a statement on Sunday evening that it would continue to cooperate with the relevant authorities in ongoing recovery efforts and investigations.

"Determining the circumstances and cause of an aviation accident is a careful and methodical process, and we will not speculate about what occurred," the company said.

Ghana News.title: Teachers’ promotion arrears to be paid by Oct. 30 – Education Minister
Ghana News.content:
Haruna Iddrisu, Minister of Education, has pledged to settle teachers’ promotion arrears from January 2026 by October 30, 2026.

He said Government had accepted responsibility for its obligations as the employer of teachers and would honour the arrears owed them.

Mr Iddrisu made the pledge at a two-day symposium and exhibition organised for teachers by the National Teaching Council (NTC) at the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) Hall in Accra.

“Government have accepted that I am responsible to honour my obligations as an employer to all teachers. And we have accepted that we will pay their arrears from January 26 to yesterday. We will honour them.

“If by October 30, 2026, your promotion arrears are not paid, then I will have no honour,” he said.

The event preceded the Ghana Teacher Prize grand durbar scheduled for Monday, October 5, at the University of Professional Studies Accra Auditorium, where outstanding teachers would be honoured and rewarded.

The Minister said the Government was intensifying engagements with teacher unions to address their concerns and find lasting solutions to challenges confronting the profession.

He said the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission would engage the teacher unions on Tuesday, October 6, to consider a new collective agreement for teachers.

“Indeed, I am reliably informed, and you are aware, that almost all the other unions have concluded their negotiations with the Fair Workers and Salaries Commission and signed on.

“We give you one week to one month to conclude and sign within the framework of what has been agreed with the other teacher unions,” he said.

On the 20 per cent deprived-area allowance, Mr Iddrisu said a committee comprising representatives of the teacher unions and the Ghana Statistical Service had been established to determine eligible teachers and communities.

He explained that the allowance was location-specific and not permanent, saying a teacher posted to Tumu in the Upper West Region could qualify but would lose the benefit when transferred to schools in areas such as Osu Presby or PRESEC.

Dr Christian Addai-Poku, Registrar of the NTC, said teachers should be celebrated for their critical role in shaping the future of learners. ‎

‎“The pivotal role of teachers is imperative that they are empowered in terms of skills set and capacity to deliver,“ he said.

‎Dr Addai-Poku said the role of teachers went beyond classroom lesson delivery to shaping the values, skills and knowledge that formed the foundation of Ghana’s future.

Ghana News.title: Stop talking too much on stage – Kafui Dey warns MCs
Ghana News.content:
Veteran broadcaster and Master of Ceremonies (MC), Kafui Dey, has cautioned MCs to cut down on excessive talking when hosting events.

According to Kafui Dey, who spent 17 years in sales before becoming a full-time MC, many MCs today ruin events by talking too much and promoting themselves instead of the event.

“They talk too much. They need to reduce the talking. Bring that down. They promote themselves. Promote the event. Make the speaker look good. Make the event look good. Take yourself out of the situation,” he warned.

He said the best MCs are often invisible, making guests feel comfortable without drawing attention to themselves. “I always smile when they do thank-yous, and they thank everybody, but they don’t thank the MC,” he explained.

“The highest compliment is when after a banking event somebody asks, ‘Which bank do you work with?’ It means they’ve identified me with them so much that they think I’m one of them.”

He also slammed the habit of MCs announcing their phone numbers on stage to chase the next gig. “I’ve heard MCs giving their telephone numbers on stage – 024… You’re trying to secure the next job. No. Your excellence speaks for you. Do a good job. At the end they will say, ‘Can I have your card? Can I have your number?’ Don’t worry too much about the next week. If organisers are happy with you, they will book you for the next one,” he stated.

Kafui Dey advised MCs to ask for testimonials instead, urging them to have organisers record a one-minute video mentioning their name, company, and what they liked about the MC’s performance, which goes beyond self-praise. “Don’t talk too much. Keep it down,” he stressed.

In an exclusive interview with Ned Ankrah on DGN TV, recounting his over 30-year journey, Dey said his MC career started by accident when his French boss, Mr Louis Leroux, drafted him to host a company event.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Djokovic defeats top seed Zverev to reach China Open semifinals
World.content:
Novak Djokovic to face Daniil Medvedev in the semifinals in Beijing after the Russian defeats Francisco Cerundolo.

Share Djokovic beats Zverev at China Open in stunning comeback from injury on social media

Novak Djokovic has brushed aside ongoing injury-related struggles and produced a trademark comeback to defeat top seed Alexander Zverev 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 for a place in the China Open semifinals, extending his unbeaten record in the tournament.

Playing the ATP 500 event in Beijing for the first time since 2015, the six-time champion was pushed to the limit by reigning French Open and US Open champion Zverev, who delivered 19 aces in the match on Sunday.

Meeting for the first time in nearly 16 months, Djokovic struggled to contain the German’s power in the early stages as the 29-year-old Zverev claimed the opening set, but the Serb gradually worked his way into the match and refused to let his opponent pull away.

“I had a terrible start – two double faults at the beginning. It was quite cold, and honestly, I didn’t feel warmed up, but my fault,” Djokovic said.

“I gave him an early break, and then it was hard to come back in the first set.”

The contest was briefly interrupted by a moment of controversy when Zverev argued that the electronic advertising signage had gone dark during a rally and requested a video review after losing the point.

Replays showed a section of the signage had switched off although not as Zverev was missing the forehand. The chair umpire ordered the point to be replayed, prompting a frustrated exchange from Djokovic.

‘Held my nerves’

The turning point came late in the second set when Djokovic broke at 5-4 to level the match, shifting the momentum in his favour after a tightly contested battle.



With little separating the pair in the third, the Serbian struck again at 5-4 on the Zverev serve, securing the decisive break to seal the victory in two hours and 35 minutes.

“I was trying to be aggressive and come to the net and change up the pace, not giving the same pattern,” Djokovic said.

“I am just glad that I held my nerves, played good shots at important moments, 5-4 in the second and third.”

The pair had not met since Roland Garros in 2025, where Djokovic won in four sets, and Sunday’s encounter again highlighted the Serb’s ability to deliver under pressure despite a season disrupted by physical issues.

With the victory, Djokovic moved a step closer to a seventh China Open title and an elusive first trophy of the year while denying Zverev another opportunity to strengthen his bid for the world number one ranking.

Djokovic will face Daniil Medvedev in the semifinals after the Russian defeated Francisco Cerundolo 7-6(4), 6-3 earlier.

Rybakina withdraws from Wuhan after China Open exit

World number one Elena Rybakina withdrew from this month’s Wuhan Open due to a foot injury, tournament organisers said on Sunday, a day after the Kazakh suffered a shock defeat in her opening match at the China Open.

Rybakina, who lost to world number 118 Alina Charaeva in Beijing, said she would take time away from competition to recover.

“I’m very sorry to the fans who were looking forward to seeing me play,” Rybakina said in a story posted on the tournament’s Instagram account.

“I’ll take some time to rest and recover. Thank you for your understanding and continued support.”

The 27-year-old has been managing a lingering lower leg and foot problem that also forced her to retire from her Cincinnati quarterfinal against Iga Swiatek in August.

Despite the setback, Rybakina recovered in time for the US Open, where she claimed her third Grand Slam title, rose to world number one and became the first player to qualify for the season-ending WTA Finals.

Rybakina is next expected to compete this month in the Ningbo Open in China, where she will try to defend her title.

The Wuhan Open is scheduled to take place from October 12 to 18.

World.title: Middle East oil exports surpass pre-war levels despite tensions, data shows
World.content:
IRGC commander says oil flows through US-supervised route in Hormuz are ‘negligible’.

Crude oil exports from the Middle East have risen above pre-war levels on four of the seven days in the last week of September, provisional data from ship-tracking firm Kpler showed.

However, senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) commander Ali Fadavi said in a televised interview on Sunday night that only three to four million barrels of oil per day (bpd) are now moving through the route, dismissing the amount as “negligible” when compared with pre-war traffic.

Fadavi said, for the first time, no US vessels were present in the Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, the Sea of Oman or even the northern Indian Ocean and US warships are “100 percent vulnerable” to IRGC attacks.

Kpler data showed crude exports from the region exceeded pre-war levels on September 24 and between September 27 and 29, rising to 19.5-22.5 million bpd.

Around that time, Iran claimed success in attacking ships – including US Navy vessels – near the Strait of Hormuz, saying the strikes had forced Washington to move its warships further from the Iranian coast.

Before the US-Israel war on Iran began, exports averaged 18 million bpd between March 2025 and February 2026.

According to Kpler data, the overall tally for crude, oil products, chemicals and non-gas liquids averaged 22.4 million bpd in the seven days to September 30.

On October 1, the seven-day moving average for crude exports was at 18.5 million bpd. This includes transits via the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, exports from terminals and ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman.



The number of liquefied natural gas cargoes exiting the Strait of Hormuz also rose in September to its highest monthly level since February.

The figures exclude any vessels that might have crossed the strait with their automatic identification system transponders turned off to avoid detection.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency reported at least one attack a day in the Strait of Hormuz or in the Gulf of Aden since October 2.

On Sunday, Iran’s top negotiator and parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until the United States accepts Tehran’s seven-day plan to reopen the waterway.

World.title: Who were the top teen athletes at the Asian Games?
World.content:
China’s Zhang Zhanshuo, 19, finished with seven gold medals while compatriot Yu Zidi won three record-breaking golds.

Share Who were the top teen athletes at the Asian Games? on social media

Teenage athletes have headlined some of the biggest Asian Games triumphs, leading their countries to historic gold medals, breaking records and cementing their legacy as formidable forces in the field.

Far from being intimidated by competitors double or triple their age, these schoolchildren remained cool and unfazed as they cruised to gold at their Asian Games debut.

Many are already familiar with the pressure and expectations of the world stage and have dominated their sport all season.

Al Jazeera Sport looks at some of the stars who left their mark in Japan:

Yu Zidi, 13

China: Swimming

At just 13, Yu was named female Most Valuable Player (MVP), as she bagged three gold medals and broke as many Asian Games records in a fairytale debut.

The schoolgirl stormed to victory in the women’s 200m butterfly, 200m and 400m individual medley (IM) and had a comfortable lead over her competitors.

Her time of two minutes and 6.10 seconds (2:06.10) in the 200m IM stands as a world junior record and second-fastest time ever.

“I don’t think I am what people describe as a prodigy,” she said after being crowned MVP. “I will continue to train hard, push myself and work alongside young athletes across Asia to inspire more young people to love and take part in sports, especially swimming.”

Zhang Zhanshuo, 19

China: Swimming

Zhang held up seven fingers after his 400m freestyle win to count out his gold medals at the Games – the most at this edition, and more than what 27 of the 45 participating nations had in their medal tally at the conclusion of the event.



He set Games records in the 400m and 800m freestyle, an Asian record in the 200m, and helped power China to gold and Asian records in the men’s 4x100m and 4x200m freestyle relays.

But the 19-year-old has bigger victories in sight.

“The Asian Games is not the goal. I’m still aiming for the Olympics and competing with the best,” he said.

The teenager’s haul helped China sign off from swimming with 30 golds out of 41 medal events in the pool, with chief rival Japan a distant second with seven titles.

Shin Ohashi, 17

Japan: Swimming

Ohashi broke the world record in the men’s 200m breaststroke (2:04.83) in front of a home crowd to become the first swimmer under the 2:05 mark.

The gold added to his title in the 100m breaststroke shared with China’s Dong Zhihao, bronze in the 50m breaststroke, and silver in the mixed and men’s 4x100m medley relays.

The teenager said he was surprised and honoured that Olympic champion Leon Marchand knew who he was, after the Frenchman described the 17-year-old as a “scary” prospect ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

“I respect him because I know just how strong he is. But if I want to win, he’s someone I know I’ll have to beat.”

Ohashi’s world record performance came just a week after the teenager recovered from COVID-19.

Yan Ziyi, 18

China: Athletics

Yan was already javelin world number one and Asian record holder when she stepped onto the field for her Games debut – her first and only throw of 70.46 metres was enough for gold and a Games record.

It was the sixth-best of all time and well ahead of Olympic champion and home hero Haruka Kitaguchi’s 62.70m.

Yan is closing in on the world record of 72.28m set by Barbora Spotakova in 2008. In May, she hurled a world-leading, record-breaking 71.74m to open an unprecedented season.

Chen Yujie, 17

China: Athletics

Chen stormed to a new Games record in the women’s 100m en route to her first gold as she announced herself as the new sprint queen in Asia.

“I have no limits,” was her response when asked how much faster she hopes to run.

She followed up her podium finish with a silver in the 200m and gold in the women’s and mixed 4x100m relays.

Taiju Goto, 17

Japan: Athletics

Goto narrowly missed gold in the men’s 400m hurdles, but his 47.93s was enough for a world under-18 best time, Asian under-20 best time, and a new personal best.



The teen star has run sub-50 seconds eight times this season alone, an impressive feat for a 17-year-old. His Asian Games silver added to the World Under-20 one he bagged in August.

Kumkum Mohod, 17

India: Archery

Mohod scripted history for India when she became the first Indian to win an individual recurve archery gold at the Games. The 17-year-old helped India to gold in the women’s team recurve, and partnered with Dhiraj Bommadevara for mixed team silver.

Mohod’s gold was no stroke of luck; she defeated South Korea’s reigning world champion and Olympic medallist Kang Chaeyoung in the quarterfinals before dominating China’s Zhu Jingyi in the semifinals.

“Ever since I’ve made it to the national team, I’ve been visualising this moment. I had visualised shooting an X, and that is exactly what happened,” she told reporters after the match, according to Indian media.

Anahat Singh, 18

India: Squash

World junior champion Anahat Singh has been India’s finest in the sport for several years now. Despite only being 18, Aichi-Nagoya was Singh’s second Asian Games outing after competing at Hangzhou 2023, where she won two bronze medals in the mixed doubles and women’s team events.
