This time round, she won a silver in the women’s singles against world number five Sivasangari Subramaniam of Malaysia. However, her semifinal match against Japan’s Satomi Watanabe was what she called the “best win” of her career after producing a stellar comeback to defeat the world number six.

Yuki Kurihara, 11

Japan: e-sports

At just 11 years of age, e-sports prodigy Kurihara became the youngest gold medallist in Asian Games history when he won Puyo Puyo Champions.

“I’m really happy. The gold medal is really beautiful, shiny and heavy,” Kurihara said after his final, where he barely broke a sweat.

Kurihara started playing Puyo Puyo in his first year of primary school – where he still studies – and soon started competing and winning in tournaments. He obtained his pro licence in April this year and regularly beats adults, often triple his age.

Ku Yong-yan, 12

Taipei: Skateboarding

Ku took silver in the men’s skateboarding park with 87.33 points, and was just one of several teenagers – in his case, a pre-teen – who medalled in skateboarding at the Games.

Japan’s Izuru Nagahara, 15, took gold in the event. China’s Zhu Yuanling, also 15, won gold in the women’s street skateboarding competition.

China’s Cao Shiqi finished fourth in women’s skateboarding park and was the youngest athlete in China’s delegation at the Games.

World.title: Samoa PM apologises after Nazi salute video emerges
World.content:
Pacific island nation’s leader says 2007 Nazi salute at family gathering does not reflect his beliefs.

Samoa’s Prime Minister La’auli Leuatea Schmidt has apologised after previously unseen video showed him leading a Nazi salute and saying “Heil Hitler” at a family gathering.

Schmidt issued the apology on Monday after the Samoa Observer, a local newspaper, published the seven-second clip the previous day.

The footage was recorded at a Schmidt family reunion on the island of Savai‘i in July 2007, when he was an MP and deputy speaker of parliament.

In the video, Schmidt is holding a microphone as he leads a “hip hip” exchange with the group before telling those present to raise their right hands and say “Heil Hitler”.

About a dozen people visible in the footage appear to follow him.

Radio New Zealand said it had independently verified the footage through its correspondent in Samoa.

Schmidt said on Monday that the words and gesture were inappropriate regardless of what was intended at the gathering and apologised for the offence they could cause.

“I reject Nazism, antisemitism, racism and all forms of political extremism,” he said, adding that the episode did not represent his beliefs or the values of Samoa’s government and people.

The apology followed criticism from academics contacted by the Samoa Observer.

Richard Evans, a historian of Nazi Germany, told the Samoa Observer by email that the footage was “shocking and disturbing”.

The paper also quoted University of Canterbury academic Anne-Marie Brady as saying Schmidt should explain and apologise.

Schmidt, who became prime minister in 2025, has made strong public expressions of support for Israel.



He wore a Jewish prayer shawl at his swearing-in, where a shofar, a horn used in Jewish religious ceremonies, was sounded.

He has also pledged to open a Samoan embassy in Jerusalem before the end of 2026, a step taken by only a handful of countries because of the city’s disputed status and Palestinian claims to East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state.

In his Monday statement, Schmidt said he considered the controversy addressed and would focus on the country’s economic and social challenges.

World.title: Bolsonaro beats expectations in Brazil vote, faces Lula in runoff
World.content:
Bolsonaro beats expectations in Brazil vote, faces Lula in runoff

NewsFeed Bolsonaro beats expectations in Brazil vote, faces Lula in runoff

Brazil’s tightly contested presidential election is heading to a run-off after incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro both fell short of the 50 percent needed to win outright. Al Jazeera’s Lucia Newman reports from Sao Paulo.

World.title: FBI arrests ‘Chinese foreign agent’ for spying on Taiwan president’s son
World.content:
A California woman allegedly sent photos and videos of President Lai’s son and his family to Chinese officials.

Share FBI arrests ‘Chinese foreign agent’ for spying on Taiwan president’s son on social media

The FBI has arrested a “Chinese foreign agent” at Los Angeles International Airport accused of spying on the Taiwanese president’s son.

Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, was arrested on Sunday before her planned departure to China, the first assistant US attorney for the Central District of California, Bill Essayli, said in a post on X.

Authorities charged Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, with acting as an unregistered foreign agent.

Zhang surveilled Taiwanese President William Lai Ching-te’s son, the FBI said. The agency did not directly name Zhang’s alleged target, but later shared a news article identifying him as Lai Ting-yu.

The US Justice Department said Zhang travelled to Seattle in 2025 at the behest of Chinese officials. She sent photos, video and license plate information of the Taiwanese leader’s son and his family to China.

Essayli called Zhang a “Chinese foreign agent” and said she “used tradecraft to avoid detection”.

“She never notified the Attorney General she was acting for a foreign government, a federal offense,” he added.

Essayli said Zhang will appear in a Los Angeles federal court on Monday.

William Lai Ching-te and his Democratic Progressive Party say that Taiwan is already an independent country separate from China. Beijing views the island as Chinese territory.

Washington does not have ⁠formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan, but the US is bound by law to provide the island with the means to ‌defend itself.

Earlier this week, the US delivered two F-16V ⁠Block 70 fighter jets to Taiwan as the island seeks to build its defence capabilities to deter a feared attack by China.



In January, Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged to achieve the “reunification” of China and Taiwan, calling Beijing’s long-held goal “unstoppable”.

World.title: Russian lab worker dies of suspected plague in Siberia; US monitoring case
World.content:
Share Russian lab worker dies of suspected plague in Siberia; US monitoring case on social media

An employee of a Russian anti-plague institute in the remote Siberian region of Irkutsk has reportedly died of a suspected pneumonic plague infection, according to a United States official.

“We are aware of reports of a fatal case of suspected pneumonic plague in Irkutsk Oblast, Russia. We are monitoring the situation closely with the CDC [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention] and our other interagency partners,” a State Department official told Al Jazeera

“Many details have not been confirmed. We encourage Russian authorities to share accurate information quickly and openly,” the official said.

Alexei Tsydenov, the governor of the Buryatia region, said in a post on his Telegram channel on October 3 that a woman in the neighbouring Irkutsk region had “died, maybe of the plague”.

Russia’s official TASS news agency reported on Sunday that the country’s consumer watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, said in a statement that an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East had been diagnosed with “pneumonia of unknown aetiology”.

The watchdog also said it expanded testing of samples from the patient and found no microorganisms associated with her professional activities.

Pneumonic plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, usually found in small mammals and their fleas. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the plague is highly infectious and can be fatal if not treated early.

Local media named the woman who died as 28-year-old laboratory technician Darya Shipilova.



Media reports say that authorities in Siberia’s Irkutsk region have placed nearly 200 people under medical observation.

World.title: Singapore turns matchmaker amid rock-bottom birthrate
World.content:
Singapore – Nur Aisyah, a 30-year-old civil servant, has spent the past couple of years looking for a partner, with little to show for it.

Nur rarely meets men through work or her hobbies and finds dating apps such as Tinder and Bumble “terrible”, with potential suitors either putting scant effort into their profile or struggling to hold a conversation over text.

Nur is open to having children but also struggles to imagine raising them in a city where housing and childcare costs are high, and where the burden of childcare typically falls hardest on women.

“I feel slightly pessimistic about the future as a whole,” Nur, who asked to use a pseudonym, told Al Jazeera.

So when Singapore’s technology agency GovTech recently rolled out FirstDate, a dating platform for public servants that uses a Nobel-winning algorithm, Nur signed up out of curiosity

“It’s more of the mindset of ‘Why not?’” she said. “It makes quite a funny story if something did come out of this.”

Born out of GovTech’s annual hackathon, where staff develop and test new ideas, FirstDate is being piloted among single government employees aged 21 to 35.

Participants log in using their national digital ID and answer a survey about their interests, habits and values before being matched with one prospective partner at a time.

Sign-ups for the pilot closed on Monday.

GovTech has told local media that no decision has been made on whether to expand the service beyond employees at government agencies.

Singapore’s decision to get into the matchmaking game is its latest attempt to lift a birthrate that has sunk to historic lows.



Fewer than 30,000 babies were born in the Southeast Asian city-state in 2025, bringing the fertility rate to a record low of 0.87.

In August, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced a series of new measures to support families, including almost 70,000 Singapore dollars ($55,000) worth of financial benefits for every child from birth until age 17.

For Singapore, whose six million citizens are practically the city-state’s only resource, the prospect of a shrinking, fast-ageing population is existential.

In February, Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong warned that without intervention, the citizen population could begin to shrink by the early 2040s, leaving fewer workers to care for the elderly.

Singapore already leans heavily on immigration to meet its workforce needs, with the government expecting to take in 25,000 to 30,000 new citizens annually over the next five years, a politically sensitive influx in a country whose 6.2 million inhabitants fill an area less than half the size of London.

Yet even as Singapore’s bureaucrats urge people to have babies, many Singaporeans have enthusiastically embraced a child-free lifestyle, preferring to reap the benefits of living in a double-income household with fewer bills or to lavish their attention on pets.

Singapore has never been shy about meddling in matters of the heart.

In a 1983 speech that sparked what became known as the “Great Marriage Debate”, Lee Kuan Yew, Singapore’s founding father and longest-serving prime minister, warned that graduates, especially women, were marrying late and having fewer children than the less educated.

The following year, Lee’s government introduced the controversial Graduate Mothers’ Scheme, which prioritised the children of university-educated mothers in school admissions.

Around the same time, the government established the Social Development Unit (SDU) to organise events where graduate singles could mingle, prompting some Singaporeans to joke that the body’s initials should stand for “Single, Desperate and Ugly”.

Critics called the agency elitist, and a separate body for those with only secondary school qualifications followed in 1985.

“We have a highly interventionist government, even in a private sphere of love and marriage,” Tan Ern Ser, adjunct principal research fellow at the Institute of Policy Studies in Singapore, told Al Jazeera.

Tan said that although past governments’ attempts to play matchmaker were neither “significant nor cost effective”, Singapore’s current generation of bureaucrats is no less eager to involve themselves in the dating game, using the power of technology.



Still, Tan said, a government-backed platform does not mark a return to the era of arranged marriages, and “couples who are identified as compatible could still have a love match.”

FirstDate relies on the Gale-Shapley algorithm, devised by mathematicians David Gale and Lloyd Shapley in 1962, which pairs people according to the ranked preferences of each side.

Shapley shared the 2012 Nobel memorial prize in economics for discovering the algorithm, versions of which are used in school admissions and medical residency placements.

“This is a fundamentally different approach from most dating apps,” Jean Liu, an associate professor of psychology at the Singapore Institute of Technology, told Al Jazeera.

“It is more akin to offline matchmaking, with endless profile swiping replaced by a single match.”

That FirstDate grew out of a hackathon, Liu said, reflects “an appetite to innovate on the nation’s ‘hard problems'”.

Whether it will help people find love any better than mainstream dating apps is another matter.

Questionnaires have limited value in predicting whether two people will hit it off, and the matches are only as good as the pool of people who join, Liu said.

“The process may break down if too few people sign up.”

The app’s greatest value, Liu said, may be in giving the government an opportunity to evaluate and publish dating data, something app companies, which treat their algorithms as sensitive company information, rarely do.

Singapore is not alone in trying to pair up singles.

Tokyo’s metropolitan government launched Tokyo Enmusubi, an AI-powered dating app, in 2024, while the Seoul government’s “Seoulting” programme hosts curated blind dates at landmarks such as the Han River.

Online, Singaporeans’ reactions to their government’s latest bid to play cupid have ranged from scorn to amusement.

Some commentators have dismissed FirstDate as a waste of public money, while others have joked about “state-assigned spouses” and whether finding love will now be included among their work targets.

Jamie, a government employee who works in education, received the email inviting her to join the platform but has no plans to sign up.

“I think it’s quite cringe. It just sounds like someone is trying too hard,” Jamie, who declined to give her last name, told Al Jazeera.

“Our social skills have atrophied. I am so exhausted after work that I just want to go home and lie down,” Jamie said.

She said she does make an effort through community groups, but has yet to meet anyone who shares her values or is emotionally ready for a relationship, so “nothing happens”.

Jamie said she also wonders about privacy.

“What kind of data are they collecting in order for a match, and what are they doing with said data?” she said.

According to FirstDate’s website, profiles are visible only to a person’s match, contact details are shared only when both parties agree, and data will not be monetised or shared with third parties except where the law requires or permits.

For Teo Kai Xiang, a PhD student and former Straits Times journalist, dating reduced to a list of preferences reflects “a deeply transactional and instrumentalist view of love”, in which partners become “co-owners of a financial venture” and “breeders of sought-after children”.



That mindset, Teo said, is sharpened by Singapore’s public housing system, where the rational move for couples chasing subsidies is to apply for an apartment before marriage.

This algorithm “does not fix or challenge this HR interviewer mindset”, said Teo, who also questions why those aged 36 and above are excluded.

Though he welcomes the experiment, Teo would like to see the government do more to revive the city-state’s third spaces and nightlife instead of “ramming pro-fertility rhetoric down our throats”.

The bigger barrier to dating, he said, is cost – from pricey late-night transport to high rents that keep many singletons living with their parents into their 30s.

Singles cannot buy public housing, home to about 80 percent of residents in Singapore, on their own until they turn 35.

“The truth is that we don’t really know what exactly makes love work, such that we can articulate and implement it on a societal scale,” Teo said. “It’s too messy, too complex, too idiosyncratic, and too human.”

World.title: US air force removes all bombers from British military base RAF Fairford
World.content:
The US has withdrawn all of its bombers from RAF Fairford, the UK military base at the centre of an incident being investigated by counter terror police.

A statement from a Pentagon official confirmed on Sunday it had removed its bombers - thought to be about a dozen B-1s - from the base back to their home stations in America.

The US did not give a reason for the withdrawal, but it follows a major incident on 27 September when police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase.

Five men were initially arrested on suspicion of terror offences near the base and subsequently released on bail. A sixth man, a UK-Iranian national, was also later arrested and released on bail.

Whitehall sources have not disputed the decision from Washington was in response to the incident at the airbase in Gloucestershire.

The BBC has also been told it was a military rather than a political decision - taken at an operational level - and communicated from the US military to its British counterparts.

The UK's Ministry of Defence has not commented.

Tracking websites showed B-1 bombers flying out of RAF Fairford on Sunday.

Days after the incident at RAF Fairford, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident but did not provide further details. Tehran has strongly denied any involvement.

Initially, five men aged between 23 and 25 were arrested in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base operated by the US Air Force (USAF). All five were UK nationals from London.

They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".

The sixth man, aged 25, was arrested in London on Thursday on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts. Counter terror police confirmed on Saturday he had also been released on bail.

RAF Fairford has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.

In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.

In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".

Days after the incident, and before the arrest of the sixth man, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Fox News that it "clearly involve[d] the hands of a foreign actor".

Rubio did not provide further details - saying at the time he was limited on what he could say on air.

US President Donald Trump separately said he was "surprised" the five men had been released on bail.

"We know everything about them, we would not have released them," he said, adding that the UK had worked with the US "very closely" on this.

Many B-1 bombers flown from the UK were armed with precision-guided "bunker busting" bombs, with thicker casings to penetrate hardened or buried targets such as weapons stores.

They also carried air-to-surface missiles used against more heavily defended targets deeper inside Iran.

Each bombing mission, depending on the location of the target, would likely have taken around 12 to 15 hours in total there and back, with air-to-air refuelling both ways.

The Pentagon has stressed its bombing aircraft remain able to conduct missions "anywhere, anytime", including through "operations that launch and recover from the continental United States".

Additional reporting by Chris Partridge.

World.title: Brazil election goes to run-off as right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro wins first round
World.content:
The right-wing FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro has won the first round of Brazil's presidential election, beating the incumbent left-wing President Lula da Silva. But he did not obtain more than 50% of the votes required to win outright.

There will be a run-off vote between these two candidates on 25 October.

FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro is the son of the former right-wing president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year prison sentence for masterminding a failed coup attempt after losing the last election.

The election was close, with President Lula polling slightly ahead during the campaign. With 99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro had 47.03% to Lula's 45.16% of the vote.

Bolsonaro's result exceeded expectations, meaning the second round now looks like his to lose, given some of the other presidential candidates who were knocked out in the first round were right-wing alternatives.

Bolsonaro's Liberal Party (PL) also had the most governors, senators and federal deputies elected in the results so far, meaning the party is expected to have the most influence in Congress.

The majority of Latin America has now elected right-wing presidents, aligned to the Trump administration, and the run-off will determine whether Brazil â Latin America's largest country and economy â will follow suit or not.

After casting his ballot, Lula, 80, warned that the choice was between democracy and "barbarism".

Bolsonaro, 45, said he wanted to "free the Brazilian people".

World.title: Watch: How Brazil's dramatic election unfolded
World.content:
Millions of Brazilians took to the polls on Sunday for the first round of the country's presidential elections.

President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, 80, is running for his fourth non-consecutive term in office, while his challenger, right-winger FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, 45, is competing in his first presidential race.

His father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, governed Brazil from 2019 to 2022.

With the election now heading to a run-off on 25 October, BBC correspondent Ione Wells unpacks the results.

World.title: Trump unveils 'Super Intelligence Force' to oversee AI policy
World.content:
US President Donald Trump says he has created a new taskforce focused on artificial intelligence, which will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.

The "Super Intelligence Force" will work to ensure that the US continues to lead in the technology's development and will coordinate the government's engagement with the public, Trump posted on Sunday.

It comes after the president signed an executive order on 29 September to rename AI as Super Intelligence, after previously saying the word artificial made it sound "fake".

Trump also said last week that he would set up a board to oversee AI safety after top tech bosses signed what he described as a "morally binding" pact.

"The Super Intelligence Force will coordinate the Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies," Trump wrote.

Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson and Undersecretary of Defense for Research, Engineering Emil Michael and Director of the Office of Personnel Management Scott Kupor will also be part of the taskforce.

It will report directly to the president and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles.

The taskforce's chief, Clayton, took office as the US national intelligence director in August after Trump's original choice, Bill Pulte, was rejected by lawmakers.

On AI, Clayton has previously said: "When something's both an opportunity and a threat, you better get your arms around it."

Clayton previously served as US attorney for the Southern District of New York, overseeing several prominent cases, including the drug trafficking case against former Venezuelan President Nicholas Maduro.

The announcement of the taskforce follows growing pressure from prominent figures in the industry, including executives of OpenAI and Anthropic, to tighten regulation of the technology.

World.title: France closes up to 500 schools Monday over student protests
World.content:
Up to 500 schools across France will be partially or totally closed on Monday after clashes between riot police and student protesters in recent days, the French education minister said on Sunday.

Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" in some "400 to 500" high schools as security conditions "have not been fulfilled", Ãdouard Geffray said.

He also said 24 schools had been "burned or ransacked" since the start of the protests.

Thousands of students have been demonstrating over education standards and the protests, which started last week, have spread from Paris to other cities, including Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille.

High school pupils and others have objected to a lack of teachers, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings.

On Friday, French Justice Minister GÃ©rald Darmanin said 735 of France's 3,700 schools had been affected "one way or another" by violent protests.

The education minister warned the number of schools potentially affected on Monday could be comparable to Friday's figure but promised a "partial, progressive return to lessons".

"There are activists - particularly from the far-left - who have infiltrated the high school student movement, hijacked it from the students themselves, and engaged in extreme violence," Ãdouard Geffray claimed.

"Clearly, this poses a risk to both our staff and our students," he said. Geffray added that 78 staff members in education had been wounded, which he described as "something we have never seen before".

On Friday 1,747 people were arrested, according to French Interior Minister Laurent NuÃ±ez.

Over 5,000 people have been arrested altogether since the start of the movement, according the AFP news agency, with around 85% of them minors.

World.title: All six passengers presumed dead after plane went missing off US coast
World.content:
Six people aboard a medical transport aircraft that went missing on Saturday while it was travelling from Bermuda to Boston are presumed dead, according to a statement from the flight's operator.

On Sunday evening, the United States Coast Guard said it was ending its search for survivors off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island.

"We must now face the heartbreaking reality that the four members of our Latitude team, our patient and the patient's family escort, who were aboard Heartbeat 104, are presumed to have died," Latitude Air Ambulance said in a statement shortly thereafter.

"Our thoughts are first and foremost with their families, loved ones, friends, and colleagues."

The Federal Aviation Administration lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 plane just after 01:00 local time (05:00 GMT) on Saturday morning.

On Saturday evening, authorities located a "debris field" confirmed to be from the aircraft.

The plane had departed from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at 23:40 local time on Friday night, according to flight data from FlightAware, and was due to land at Boston's Logan International at 01:30 EDT (05:30 GMT).

Four Canadian nationals and two Bermudian nationals were onboard.

"This is an unimaginable loss for our Latitude family and for everyone who loved the six people aboard Heartbeat 104," said Peter Byl, President of Latitude Air Ambulance, on Sunday evening.

"Our focus now is on supporting their families, supporting our people and assisting the authorities. We will honour our colleagues by remembering the care, professionalism, and commitment they brought to their work every day."

Latitude Air Ambulance is a Canadian company that provides international medical flights for patients returning home.

Two pilots and two medical staff, both Canadian, had flown to Bermuda to collect a patient and their relative, Clarence Togeretz, director of flight operations at Latitude, told CBC News.

FlightAware's tracker shows that the aircraft significantly dropped in altitude before its communications went dark, plummeting from around 7,300m (24,000ft) to 3,300m (11,000ft).

Radio transmissions show trouble with communications between the air traffic controller and the pilot, the Boston Globe reported, based on transmissions provided by LiveATC.net.

"You're coming in blind? Is that what you said?" the air traffic controller asked. "Are you declaring an emergency, or no?"

The pilot's response was inaudible.

"You're coming in a little weak so I didn't hear what your response was, if you were declaring an emergency or not," the air traffic controller said, according to the Globe.

The air traffic controller later confirmed the pilot had declared an emergency.

An area fire dispatcher asked emergency crews just after 01:00 EDT to prepare to meet a plane with an "electrical issue".

The dispatcher later said "the aircraft has lost radio and radar".

Latitude said in its statement on Sunday evening that it would continue to cooperate with relevant authorities during ongoing recovery efforts and investigations.

"Determining the circumstances and cause of an aviation accident is a careful and methodical process, and we will not speculate about what occurred," the company said.

World.title: Supporters of jailed ex-PM Imran Khan march to Pakistan capital
World.content:
Thousands of supporters of Pakistan's jailed ex-prime minister Imran Khan are marching to the capital Islamabad as they call for his release.

Concerns over the 73-year-old's health have grown louder in recent months. His family claims he has lost most of his vision in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action.

The cricket star-turned-politician, who faces charges in more than 100 cases, was jailed for 17 years over corruption last year. Khan said all the cases against him are politically motivated.

Even behind bars, he remains a force in Pakistani politics, and demonstrations in support for him have led to deadly violence and crackdowns in the past.

Sunday's march, which began in Lakki Marwat, a city 275km away from Islamabad, had paused for the night and is expected to resume around midday local time on Monday.

Originally scheduled for last week, it was postponed to allow for talks between the government and Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party but the talks ended in a deadlock.

Khan, who faces charges ranging from leaking state secrets to selling state gifts, was first imprisoned in August 2023. His wife Bushra Bibi was jailed along with him last year.

Sohail Afridi, chief minister for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province ruled by PTI, expects that the march will make its way to a town about 80km (50 miles) west of Islamabad by Thursday.

"[By then] this movement will have reached every corner of the country and every square will have become a centre of activity," he said on Sunday, urging the people to "play an active role in the political process".

Authorities in Islamabad have stacked up shipping containers to block key access routes to the capital city.

The PTI said talks with government failed because authorities rejected the party's request for access to Khan so that its leaders could consult him on national and political issues.

The party also said it had demanded that Khan be given an immediate medical examination and treatment.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi meanwhile accused Afridi of "sabotaging" negotiations, saying the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government had backed out of earlier commitments on counter-terrorism issues, according to Pakistan's local media reports.

In August, Khan was briefly transferred from jail to a state-run hospital for medical examination and treatment following complaints about his deteriorating health. The doctors later deemed him "medically fit".

The intervention was the most significant relief Khan has received from the courts since he was imprisoned in 2023 on corruption charges, which he says were politically motivated.

Khan's family and the PTI, however, criticised the authorities for defying a court order that he be examined by physicians at a specific private hospital.

On 20 September, Khan's sister Aleema Khanum was arrested in the eastern city of Lahore.

The arrest order said Khanum had been mobilising people to "create law and order situations" and "raising/chanting objectionable slogans amongst the general public against the Government".

Khan, who previously captained the Pakistan national cricket team, served as the country's prime minister from 2018 to 2022.

His arrest in May 2023 sparked large-scale, violent protests by supporters, who ransacked the corps commander's residence in Lahore, smashing chandeliers and making away with furniture, paintings, and even peacocks, among other things.

At least eight people died in the protests and the army had to be called in to quell the violence.

Former international cricket captains have made several appeals in recent months to Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urging Khan be accorded proper medical care.

World.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
World.content:
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people were injured in the latest Russian attack. He earlier said that the Pivnichnyi Bridge's roadway was hit.

Kyiv's eight bridges across the wide Dnipro River link the western (right) and eastern (left) parts, and many of the capital's estimated three million residents rely heavily on the metro lines and trains to travel across the city.

Some 500,000 vehicles use the bridges every day.

The two struck bridges are still standing - but the damage and restrictions to traffic and public transport have caused gridlock in parts of the capital at times.

"To get from the left bank to the right one and back - it's just hell," Kyiv resident Roman told the BBC on Sunday.

Large numbers of commuters cross the river, especially on weekdays. Repair teams are working to fix the damage and officials say they are planning temporary pontoon bridges, ferry services and even a tunnel under the river to keep Kyiv connected.

Klitschko also said a separate Russian drone strike had damaged a heating main, adding that there would be a temporary lack of hot water in the north-eastern Desnyanskyi district as a result.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenksy said on Sunday morning Russian drones had also attacked a warehouse in the north-eastern region of Sumy, killing one person.

Meanwhile, in the central city of Dnipro, six people were injured after a communications facility was struck, he said.

Ukraine's Air Force said that overnight Russia had launched 135 drones, including 52 jet-powered ones. It said that 125 projectiles had been shot down.

World.title: 2027: INEC to address Nigerians as election countdown hits 100 days
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will on Tuesday hold a world press conference and national stakeholders’ meeting as preparations for the 2027 general elections enter the final 100-day countdown.

The commission said the event would provide Nigerians and other stakeholders with updates on its preparations for the elections, including the voters’ register, candidate nominations, logistics and measures to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process.

The event will be addressed by INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, a professor and Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), alongside other key stakeholders involved in the electoral process.

According to a statement by Mr Amupitan’s spokesperson, Adedayo Oketola, the national stakeholders’ meeting is aimed at promoting transparency, public communication and collaboration among key actors in the electoral process.

The meeting will bring together political party leaders, security agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), members of the diplomatic corps, development partners, civil society organisations, observer groups, disability rights advocates, religious and traditional leaders, youth organisations and media executives.

The event is scheduled to hold at 10 a.m. on Tuesday at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre (BAT-ICC), Abuja.

INEC said attendance would be strictly by invitation, while accredited media representatives and guests would be required to present their invitation cards or accreditation badges at security checkpoints.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The commission said the event would be broadcast live on major national television networks and streamed on its official social media platforms.

2027 election

INEC has scheduled the 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections for 16 January 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will hold on 6 February 2027.

The commission has also published the final list of presidential candidates, with 18 political parties fielding candidates for the presidential election. Sixteen of the candidates are men, while two are women.

President Bola Tinubu is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), while former Vice President Atiku Abubakar is the candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi is contesting on the platform of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC).

Other presidential candidates include Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC), Donald Duke of the People’s Redemption Party (PRP), Adewole Adebayo of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Oluseyi Makinde of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), and Sandy Onor of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

The final list also includes candidates from the Action Alliance, Action Democratic Party, Allied Peoples Party, Boot Party, Democratic Leadership Alliance, National Democratic Party, National Rescue Movement, Young Progressive Party and Zenith Labour Party.

The 2027 presidential election will be the first major nationwide election to be conducted under Mr Amupitan, who became INEC chairman in 2025.

World.title: Nigeria’s gas turned into working assets
World.content:
Nigeria holds one of Africa’s largest natural gas resources. The opportunity is not simply to possess it, but to transform it into infrastructure that powers industries, moves people and goods, supports cleaner energy solutions and creates economic value.

The Midstream & Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF) is helping bridge that gap by deploying catalytic capital into commercially viable gas infrastructure, from CNG and LCNG stations to gas processing plants, pipelines, LNG facilities and LPG storage.

In under two years since its first Final Investment Decisions, MDGIF has approved an estimated ₦671 billion in FIDs, catalysed ₦1.6 trillion in total investments, and built a portfolio spanning 31 projects and 205 infrastructure assets.

This is what unlocking Africa’s energy potential looks like: mobilising capital, de-risking viable projects and converting natural resources into productive assets that can serve businesses, communities and economies.

Nigeria’s gas. African opportunity. Infrastructure built for growth.

World.title: Amnesty raises alarm over arrests, alleged crackdown on dissent in Borno
World.content:
Amnesty International has said there is escalating political repression in Borno State, alleging that authorities are using arrests and criminal charges to silence dissent in the northeastern state.

The rights group, in a post on X on Sunday, said 11 young men had been held at Maiduguri Maximum Prison since 28 August over allegations it described as politically motivated.

The men were arraigned before Chief Magistrate Court 1 in Wulari, Maiduguri, on 8 September.

They are Umar Mohammed, Yahaya Mohammed, Mohammed Ali, Abubakar Dauda, Hussaini Umar, Yunusa Salaima, Sulaiman Mohammed, Liti Adamu, Idris Yusuf, another Mohammed Ali, and a person identified as Warrata, Na Hannun Gomna, Yambo and One Five.

According to the First Information Report cited by Amnesty, the men were charged over conduct that allegedly included interrupting, shouting at and embarrassing government officials while they were delivering a speech.

Amnesty said the charges appeared to be politically motivated and accused the authorities of using the criminal justice system to suppress peaceful dissent.

“These bizarre charges and actions that followed have all the elements of political repression and abuse of power,” the organisation said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It said the arrests and detention raised concerns over the men’s rights to personal liberty, presumption of innocence, fair hearing, freedom of expression and peaceful dissent.

‘Tinubu Must Go’ arrests

The allegations come amid growing controversy over the arrest and prosecution of opposition supporters in Maiduguri.

On 25 September, police arrested five men wearing T-shirts bearing the inscription “Tinubu Must Go” around the West End Roundabout in Maiduguri.

The men, identified as Baba Gremami, Mustapha Yemen, Abacha Ali, Adam Gubio and Abdulhamid Mohammed, were charged with criminal conspiracy, inciting disturbance, disturbance of public peace and thuggery.

According to the charges seen by PREMIUM TIMES, the police alleged that the men conspired to print the T-shirts with the intention of causing a breach of public peace.

The Borno State Police Command later said officers arrested the men during a routine patrol and found them with items including 15 wraps of dried leaves suspected to be cannabis, 100 tablets suspected to be D5, a shisha pot and a pair of scissors. It also said two of the T-shirts bearing the “Tinubu Must Go” inscription were recovered.

The police maintained that the arrests were not based on the men’s political views and said the courts should determine the allegations against them.

Governor Babagana Zulum has also distanced himself from the arrests, saying he did not order the detention of opposition supporters.

Amnesty said the recent arrests reflected a worrying pattern in Borno.

It urged the state government to respect freedom of expression and association and uphold the rule of law.

The organisation said governments’ treatment of critical voices was an important measure of their commitment to human rights.

“The increasing clampdown on peaceful dissent in Borno State is disturbing,” Amnesty said.

World.title: EDITORIAL: King’s College concession: Mirroring government’s bad decisions
World.content:
Academic activities at King’s College, Lagos, have not taken off since the 2026/2027 session began about three weeks ago, as the government’s concessioning of the school to its Old Boys Association has hit a brick wall. It was utterly riotous at the gates of the school on 15 September, when members of the Parents Teachers Association (PTA), opposed to the move, squared up to the Old Boys and prevented their access to the college for a meeting. The resulting chaos, which led to some people getting hurt, subsequently attracted heavy police presence.

In Abuja, it was the same tumultuous scene at the Federal Ministry of Education, masterminded by organised labour, the staff and PTA delegation of the college. The Joint Congress of Unions of the Federal Ministry of Education and Trade Union Congress (TUC) ensured that solidarity actions were held simultaneously nationwide in other federal Unity Colleges.

Earlier, the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa’s announcement in August that the school had been transferred to the Old Boys Association in a 35-year concession plan had set off a wave of condemnation and resistance from various stakeholders, who in our view have genuine concerns.

King’s College (KC), Lagos, set up in 1909 by the colonial government, is one of the heritage institutions in the country, in the mould of Government College, Ibadan; Barewa College, Zaria; and Government College, Umuahia.

Regrettably, King’s College has become a shadow of its former self, run aground by the federal government, like other public institutions. This is obvious in its deplorable infrastructure – dilapidated buildings, overcrowded hostels, fallen standards, and moral decadence. In 2025, a 12-year-old pupil died in the hostel from diphtheria.

For many senior students, bullying of their junior ones is a pastime. This has often elicited the outrage of parents, who then pull their children out of the school’s dormitory. The Old Boys Association was concerned about all this, and sought to rebuild the college and restore its fame.

While there is nothing wrong with such intentions, yet what really mattered was the method of the intervention. All over the world, Old Boys give back to their alma maters through a number of measures, such as the building and rehabilitation of classrooms, hostels and the setting up of educational endowments.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In the context of KC, the parents are concerned about the sort of access their children/wards would have to the school and the amount of fees they would be required to pay once the government’s funding ceases. The teachers and other members of staff equally fear for the security of their jobs, salaries, and pension benefits in a private ownership structure.

Unable to prevail in its enforcement of the concession, the government suspended its order for two weeks following consultations with union members. This is to enable a seven-member committee that was set up to review the disputed concession agreement. Its work began last Monday, and will focus on the duration of the concession, the school fees payable, continued public funding, staff welfare, operational control and financial obligation of the Old Boys.

This ought to have been the federal government’s first step, rather than its accustomed policy of putting the cart before the horse. Such informed the fuel subsidy removal by President Bola Tinubu in 2023.

The PTA Chairman of the school, Peter Oluwaleye, in decrying the concession, stated categorically that the federal government would cease funding the school after the concession is completed. Equally enraged is the forum of ex-principals of the college, which described the plan as being “inconceivable.” It declared that, “A system under which the federal government ceases to fund the daily operations and infrastructural development of King’s College would amount to abandonment of one of its critical social responsibilities – the education and development of the nation’s future human capital.” We couldn’t agree more with this.

The minister’s uncompromising stance of “no going back” on the concession is not salutary in the present circumstance. In fact, it presents a fait accompli to the seven-member committee tasked with a review, which makes an amicable resolution very difficult. PREMIUM TIMES is of the position that KC should remain a public school; its place in our national history protected, and it should be properly funded.

A controversial policy like this dramatises the government’s historical amnesia, time and time again. It would be recalled that in 2006, the policy of the concession or sale of 102 Unity Colleges was attempted under the Olusegun Obasanjo presidency, with Oby Ezekwesili as the education minister.

Nigeria is probably the only country in the world where the government would glibly choose to auction off or concession national monuments. The Tafawa Balewa Square (TBS), Lagos – the iconic site where the country’s independence was observed on 1st October 1960 – was almost sold off 19 years ago. Revenues from the transaction were projected to fund the deficits in the 2007, 2017 and 2022 budgets, which were riddled with corruption and opacity.

However, the sale stalled as a result of the legal tango between the federal government and the Lagos State government at the Supreme Court, for about two decades now, over the real ownership of the structure. The National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos, presently renamed the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, has gone through almost the same fate, for the sake of lucre.

If the government sails through with its concession agenda at KC, being the most pre-eminent public college in the country, the prospect of other unity colleges going the same way would likely be just another walk in the park. This is why the solidarity of the 104 such schools with KC needs to be sustained for the sake of public education in the country.

The progressive decline of the education budget since 2024 (from 7.9 per cent of the total, to 7.08 per cent in 2025, and 6 per cent in 2026), amid the receipt of more revenues to the public treasury is an oxymoron that the government would be hard put to explain. It should let public schools be!

World.title: National Sports Festival: Mbah inspects facilities, reassures of world-class games
World.content:
Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, says his administration is committed to delivering a world-class and memorable 23rd National Sports Festival (NSF), tagged “Coal City Games.”

Mbah also assured of the readiness of all the facilities ahead of the Games slated for 27th November to 11th December 2026.

The Governor spoke at the weekend during a tour of Awgu Games Village, one of the venues slated for the NSF, for a firsthand assessment of the quality and speed of work at the site, stressing that the Awgu Games Village, which had long been abandoned, would emerge as a world-standard sports facility in less than two months.

“Recall the commitment we made as a government that we are going to make the 23rd National Sports Festival one of the most memorable festivals in the history of the event.

“So, the construction of a one-thousand-capacity-bed hostel is ongoing. We also have the construction of outdoor and indoor courts ongoing.

“A standard FIFA pitch is also under construction. We equally have an eight-lane track, and these are all world-class.

“I have to come because we have a very tight timeline and this project must be ready. It means that in less than two months, this place will no longer be a construction site. It will become a world-class Games Village. In less than two months, what you will have here is a proper venue that will be hosting contingents from across the country,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mbah, however, added that his administration was not just building for the NSF, noting that the massive development of sports facilities was in line with his campaign promise to make Enugu State the preferred destination for investment, business, tourism, and for living.

He said the Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium was already being upgraded into a FIFA-standard stadium, describing sports as not just recreation and a veritable tool for social cohesion, but also big business if well harnessed.

“As you also know, the Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium is receiving serious attention. We are upgrading it to a world-class standard.

“These facilities will be ready. I have personally committed to the team from the National Sports Commission, who came on a monitoring visit, that we are not interested in shifting the date. The dates are already fixed for the 23rd National Sports Festival.

“We are carrying out a comprehensive reconstruction and transformation of the Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium. We are installing a new FIFA-standard football pitch and a new athletics track. We are rehabilitating and reinstalling the spectator seats, replacing damaged ones, and constructing a new roofing and canopy system to cover the entire spectator stands.

“We are upgrading the VIP and VVIP stands, the players’ changing rooms and other associated facilities. We are upgrading the stadium gates and access-control system to an electronic system, installing two new LCD scoreboards, perimeter LED display boards and protective perimeter mesh fencing around the main bowl. The floodlighting system and other electrical and mechanical services are also being upgraded.

“We are also cladding the external areas of the stadium to give the entire complex a new, modern architectural appearance and aesthetic ambience. There are extensive finishing works, external works, landscaping and improvements to the access and general environment of the stadium.

“Beyond the main stadium bowl, we are building a new Olympic-size swimming pool with its associated facilities. We are transforming the Indoor Sports Hall and constructing and upgrading indoor and outdoor sporting facilities, including volleyball, basketball, squash and other sports, together with their pavilions and supporting facilities.

“So, what we are doing is not simply renovating a football stadium. We are transforming the entire Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium complex into a modern, world-class multi-sport facility.

“Therefore, for us, it is not just about the efficiency of organising the festival. We are equally interested in the Enugu experience of the athletes. We are interested in their accommodation, their logistics and their overall experience, and we are putting everything in place to make this festival a truly memorable event for the contingents, officials and everyone involved in the management of the Games.”

In Mbah’s company during the tour were the Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development, Barr. Lloyd Ekweremadu; Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Engr. Osita Okoh; Commissioner for Human Development and Poverty Eradication, Prof. Benedett Okoli; Special Adviser to the Governor on Project Development and Implementation, Arch. Uche Nwatu; and Chairman of Awgu Local Government Council, Hon. Uchenna Okolo.

The host Council Chairman, Okolo, commended Mbah for bringing life back to Awgu Games Village, noting that the transformation of the Games Village would speed up the development of the local government and the state in general.

World.title: Police rescue kidnap victim, arrest suspected cultists
World.content:
The police in Delta State have rescued a kidnapped woman and arrested five suspects in separate operations in the state.

The police spokesperson in the state, Bright Edafe, disclosed this in a statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Sunday.

Mr Edafe, a superintendent of police, said the operations also led to the recovery of several items, including a fabricated Beretta pistol, a magazine, two rounds of live ammunition, a battle axe, four cutlasses and a hammer.

Kidnapped woman rescued

The police said operatives of the Otu-Jeremi Division rescued a 25-year-old woman who was allegedly assaulted and held hostage at Usiefrun Community.

The rescue operation was carried out on Saturday following intelligence shared by the Divisional Police Officer of the Ovwian-Aladja Division, the statement said.

A 29-year-old man, Brotugbare Onome, was arrested in connection with the incident.

A search of the premises where the woman was rescued led to the recovery of a fabricated Beretta pistol, one magazine and two rounds of live ammunition, according to the police.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Two arrested over alleged cult killing

In a separate incident, operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) arrested two suspected cultists over the alleged killing of a 25-year-old man identified as Godfrey.

The police said Godfrey was allegedly killed at Jesse Main Market in Ethiope West Local Government Area on 24 March.

The arrests followed intelligence allegedly obtained from a viral video showing suspected cultists celebrating the killing.

PREMIUM TIMES has not seen the video.

The VCRU operatives, acting on the intelligence, raided a suspected criminal hideout in Oghara on 1 October.

The operation led to the arrest of Ezekiel Izomor, 23, and Emmanuel Ogaganefe, 23, the police said.

A battle axe, four cutlasses and a hammer were recovered during the operation, according to the statement.

The police said, “Preliminary investigation indicated that a suspect identified as Collins allegedly wanted to become the leader of the Aro Bagger confraternity and believed that killing a rival cult member would help him secure the leadership position.”

The police said Collins allegedly connived with Mr Izomor, Mr Ogaganefe and another suspect identified as Richman, who was a close friend of the deceased.

“Richman and Collins are at large, but efforts to arrest them is on top gear,” Mr Edafe said.

Two arrested over alleged kidnap plot

In another separate incident, the police arrested two men over an alleged plot to kidnap a woman in Abraka.

The police identified the suspects as Endurance Akpade, 37, and Edwin Morgan, 43.

The suspects, the police said, remain in custody and are assisting with the investigation.

The latest operations come amid increased police action against cultism and drug-related crimes in Delta State.

The command recently announced the arrest of a suspected drug peddler and the recovery of illicit drugs in another operation.

In a separate operation, the police said they raided a suspected drug spot, arrested suspects and recovered firearms.

The Commissioner of Police in the state, Samuel Erale, commended the officers involved in the operations.

Mr Erale urged residents to provide credible and timely information to the police to assist efforts against kidnapping, cultism and other violent crimes.

He also warned youths against cultism, saying the practice could destroy their future.

World.title: Vice Chancellor speaks on Anthony Kila’s fake professorship
World.content:
The Vice-Chancellor of the Michael and Cecilia Ibru University, Delta State, Ibiyinka Fuwape, has said his institution would soon respond to questions arising from a PREMIUM TIMES investigation that found no evidence to support claims by its pro-chancellor, Anthony Kila, that he is a professor.

The investigation, published on Saturday morning, examined Mr Kila’s academic credentials and found that contrary to his claims, he does not hold the rank of professor and was never so confirmed by any university.

More than 24 hours after the publication, however, the university has yet to issue a public statement on the findings or clarify its position regarding Mr Kila’s designation.

PREMIUM TIMES made repeated attempts to obtain the institution’s reaction.

A telephone line listed on the university’s website for general enquiries did not connect. One number identified as belonging to the registry rang without being answered, while another registry contact was answered by a person who said the line was private and had no connection with the university.

The newspaper eventually reached the university’s Vice-Chancellor and Professor of Physics, Ibiyinka Fuwape, who said the institution would respond after internal consultations.

“We will reply you very soon. The PRO will get in touch with you. The council is yet to meet. I can’t give you any information other than that,” Ms Fuwape said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Asked when the public should expect a response, she said: “I can’t divulge that information to you. The PRO will get across to you.”

The vice chancellor’s remarks are the first official acknowledgement by the institution since the publication of the investigation.

University’s earlier position

Before the publication of the report, the university had maintained that it had no information contradicting Mr Kila’s claim to the title of professor.

PREMIUM TIMES had contacted Thomas Kolo, a former registrar of the institution, seeking to speak with the university’s spokesperson. Mr Kolo passed the phone to a man who identified himself as the spokesperson but declined to disclose his name.

The spokesperson said the university had no evidence suggesting that Mr Kila was not a professor.

“We don’t debate issues. You can go up with whatever you are going up with. If there’s a need to respond, we will respond when we see the article,” he said.

The university’s pending response is expected to clarify whether it conducted any independent verification of Mr Kila’s academic rank before associating him with the title.

The issue has drawn public attention because universities are regarded as custodians of academic integrity, where claims relating to scholarly qualifications are expected to undergo rigorous checks.

World.title: One dead, another injured as tanker inferno burns shops, vehicles in Cross River
World.content:
One person has been confirmed dead while another sustained serious injuries after a petroleum tanker overturned and caught fire opposite the Odukpani Local Government Secretariat in Cross River State.

The inferno, which occurred on Sunday, also affected several shops, buildings and vehicles around the scene.

The police spokesperson, Sunday Eitokpah, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday.

According to the statement, the tanker was conveying petroleum products when it was involved in a road crash and overturned, triggering the fire.

“The driver of the tanker, who was reportedly caught in the fire, has been rescued and taken to a hospital for medical attention,” Mr Eitokpah said in the initial update.

He said police officers from the Odukpani Division were deployed to the scene to maintain safety, secure the area, and prevent further harm to members of the public.

The fire service was also alerted to deploy personnel to contain and extinguish the fire.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The police initially said no death had been confirmed, although several shops and vehicles had reportedly been affected.

However, in a subsequent update, Mr Eitokpah confirmed that one person died while another sustained serious injury and was receiving medical treatment.

The identities of the victims were not immediately disclosed.

The police urged residents, motorists and other members of the public to stay away from the immediate area to allow emergency responders unhindered access to the scene.

One in many cases

The incident adds to a series of recent fire emergencies recorded in the state.

In September, the state fire service said 17 fire incidents were recorded across the state between January and September 2026, resulting in an estimated N2.5 billion in property losses and six injuries. The incidents included a tanker spill, according to the fire service.

The state also recently witnessed a major fire at the SPAR shopping mall in Calabar on 22 August, which affected several businesses and reportedly destroyed property worth billions of naira. The federal government subsequently approved N515 million in relief for affected business owners, Channels TV reported.

Authorities have continued to urge residents to exercise caution and allow emergency agencies unhindered access during fire emergencies.

World.title: Joint Army, DSS, Amotekun operation kills ISWAP leader planning terrorist attacks
World.content:
An intelligence-led operation by a combined team of troops of the Nigerian Army, Department of Department of State Services (DSS) personnel, and Western Nigeria Security Network aka Amotekun officers, at the weekend in Owo forest, Ondo State, eliminated a senior leader of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), Abdussamad Ohida.

Security sources said Ohida aka Anwar, who was on the verge of planning massive terrorist attacks in some southern states, was killed alongside many members of the terrorist organization by the security forces who led a surprise attack on their forest hideout.

According to the sources, the eliminated ISWAP leader previously served as deputy to ISWAP Central Nigeria leader Abu Ikrimah, also known as Abu Uwais. Ikrimah was arrested by the DSS in 2023.

Following Ikrimah’s arrest, continued the sources, Ohida assumed leadership of ISWAP activities across parts of North central and southern parts of the country, where he subsequently played a key role in the planning, coordination and execution of terrorist operations.

Through the interrogation of Abu Uwais, continued the sources, the DSS was able to gather credible intelligence on plans by Ohida toattack innocent persons during the forthcoming Yuletide.



“The plan was to attack civilians during the festive period and ultimately disrupt the 2027 general elections. This Intelligence was corroborated by intelligence partners from the United Kingdom, who supported the elimination operation,” offered one of the sources.

He said Ohida planned and executed the 31st December 2025, invasion of Ipele Divisional Police Station, Owo, Ondo State, carting away right AK-47 rifles before bringing down the station with an explosive. He mentioned the 28 July 2022 Suleja–Zuba Road, Niger State military checkpoint attack in which several soldiers, officers and civilians were killed.

He also blamed on Ohida, the July 11, 2022, attack on Kuje Correctional Centre, Abuja; the 23rd April, 2022 attack on Ogaminana Police Station, Adavi LGA, Kogi State, which resulted in the death of five police officers, and the February 7, 2022, attack on Okene Area Command police station.

“The terrorist planned and executed the 24th December, 2020 attack on a Naval checkpoint in Okene, Kogi State, which resulted in the death of two naval officers, not to mention the several attacks he launched across parts of the country,” he added.

“We may not immediately realize it, but the elimination of Abdussamad Ohida represents a significant disruption to ISWAP’s leadership structure, operational network and expansion efforts in central and southern Nigeria.

“Ohida’s elimination, coming a few months after after the killing of ISIS leader Abu Bilal al-Minuki, is a very big blow to ISWAP’s efforts to expand its operational presence in Nigeria, and underscores the growing efficiency of our security services,” he declared.

World.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 5, 2026
World.content:
The Nigerian Naira maintained a stable posture across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market as trading commenced for the week.

At the official NFEM window, the United States Dollar traded at approximately ₦1,327.08, holding steady following a stretch of robust liquidity inflows and increased turnover supported by the Central Bank of Nigeria’s ongoing policy adjustments. Market participants noted that robust foreign reserves—bolstered significantly over the preceding months—have provided a strong buffer, keeping official rates anchored within a tight band.

Meanwhile, operations in the parallel (street) market saw the greenback exchanging hands between ₦1,370 and ₦1,390 per dollar. Currency traders reported steady demand for physical cash, keeping the parallel market premium over the official window relatively narrow. Financial analysts attribute this sustained convergence to improved transparency and liquidity within official channels, which continue to discourage speculative hoarding and drive routine transactions toward formal banking structures.

World.title: APC, ADC in verbal war over Amaechi’s late mum
World.content:
lAmaechi incapable of earning living outside public office —APC lHis mother’s death not political material, ADC fires back

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA—The All Progressives Congress, APC, and African Democratic Congress, ADC, were yesterday locked in a verbalwar over claims credited to the latter’s Vice President candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, that his mother’s death should be blamed on the unfriendly economic policies of President Bola Tinubu’s government.

Recall that Amaechi had in a television interview on Friday, said the rising cost of medicines made it increasingly difficult for him to provide the drugs his mother needed to save her life.

But APC in a reaction yesterday, declared that Amaechi was incapable of earning a living outside public office.

ADC, however, criticised APC over its attack on Amaechi, saying a mother’s death was no political material.

Mary Amaechi, died on July 16, 2026, at 89.

APC in a statement by the National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, said Amaechi’s statement was irresponsible.

“For four decades, Rotimi Amaechi freeloaded at the highest levels of public office. He was never hungry and could afford medications for himself and his family. Just three years out of office, he has become destitute, unable to fend for himself and his loved ones,” the statement said.

It listed his record as a two-term speaker of Rivers State House of Assembly, two-term governor, two-term Minister of Transportation and former presidential aspirant.

The APC added: “If Amaechi is not struggling with some kind of Peter Pan syndrome, then he must be a loafer, aimless and irresponsible for his inability to be productive and earn a living outside the patronage of public office.”

The party also accused him of using his vice presidential bid as a route back to public funds, saying “the same Rotimi Amaechi now asks Nigerians to make him vice president come 2027 so he can continue leeching on public treasury and keep the predatory lifestyle he has grown accustomed to.’’

The statement had earlier opened with condolences to Amaechi over the death of his mother, Dame Ezinne Mary Oduah Amaechi and then offered a wish forAmaechi’a future.

“The All Progressives Congress, APC, prays that the soul of Dame Ezinne Mary Oduah Amaechi continues to rest in perfect peace. Amen.

“It is our sincere wish that employers of labour in his hometown of Ubima in Ikwerre Local Government Area of Rivers State may find him suitable for a job that pays wages sufficient for him to feed and buy medications for himself and his beloved family the rest of his retirement. Amen.

“The presidency is not a soup kitchen, and will not be a soup kitchen for Rotimi Amaechi. There can be no better speaker of Rotimi Amaechi’s unfitness for the office of vice president than Rotimi Amaechi himself,” APC stated.

A mother’s death is not political material, ADC fires back

Firing back in a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communications of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, the party described the APC’s response as “political cruelty” rather than an answer to the hardship facing Nigerians.

Shaibu said the death of Amaechi’s mother and his family’s grief should not be turned into material for partisan ridicule.

“A mother’s death and a family’s grief should never be turned into material for partisan ridicule. If Rotimi Amaechi says he struggled to afford his mother’s medication, the humane response is compassion.

“Shaibu said Morka’s description of Amaechi reflected what he described as the APC’s contempt for ordinary Nigerians struggling with the cost of living.

“Morka calls Amaechi a loafer for struggling outside public office. That insult says more about the APC’s contempt for ordinary people than it says about Amaechi,’’ the party stated.

The ADC-PCC said Nigerians struggling to afford treatment, electricity and transportation should not be labelled loafers.

ADC-PCC stated further: “Nigerians who cannot afford treatment, keep the lights on or travel safely on their roads are not loafers. They are citizens living through the consequences of a government that has failed them.”

Shaibu said the APC should focus on the economic and social difficulties facing Nigerians instead of attacking Amaechi.

“The reality is plain: the roads are bad, the economy is bad, electricity is bad, security is bad and the welfare of the people is bad.

“Tinubu’s name is increasingly associated with poverty, insecurity and hardship. No amount of mockery can make those conditions disappear,” the campaign council said.

It said the performance of a government should be measured by whether citizens could live safely, afford medical treatment and earn a decent living.

“The test of government is not how viciously its spokesmen can insult their opponents. It is whether people can live safely, afford treatment and earn a decent living. On that test, Tinubu’s government has failed,” ADC-PCC said.

World.title: S’Court ruling: Tension as INEC keeps affected candidates guessing
World.content:
•Applies for CTC to decide candidates’ fate

•To publish final list of gov, assembly candidates Oct 10

•Meets with parties, stakeholders tomorrow

By Clifford Ndujihe & Omeiza Ajayi

THERE is anxiety among political parties and candidates affected by penultimate week’s decision of Supreme Court ahead of the publication of final list of governorship and State Houses of Assembly candidates by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, on October 10.

Yesterday, the electoral umpire, which will meet with parties and stakeholders on Tuesday, kept the candidates guessing.

The INEC said it has applied for the certified true copy of the Supreme Court’s latest judgement and hopes to receive it today, a day before the Commission’s scheduled national engagement with stakeholders and a World Press Conference.

Its National Commissioner in charge of Information and Voter Education Committee, Malam Mohammed Kudu Haruna, told Vanguard that the document had not yet reached the Commission as of Sunday(yesterday).

“The commission is yet to receive the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgement. Hopefully we will do so tomorrow, (Monday). Until we do so and deliberate on it we cannot make any pronouncement on the issue,” he said.

The Director of Voter Education and Publicity at INEC, Mrs Victoria Eta-Messi, confirmed that the application had been made. “The Commission had applied for the CTC and an opinion will be offered on the import of the latest Judgment of the Supreme Court,” she said.

On September 23, 2026, before the judgement was delivered, INEC had announced that it would hold a World Press Conference and National Stakeholders Engagement on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, as part of continuing preparations for the 2027 general election.

None of the official said whether or not the commission will address the judgement at the event, and no timeline has been given for its opinion.

The commission’s position comes 10 days after the Supreme Court, on September 24, 2026, delivered its ruling on Section 77 of the Electoral Act 2026. The court set aside the July 16, 2026 judgement of the Court of Appeal, which had voided several restrictive sections of the Act as unconstitutional.

The ruling restored the requirement that political parties submit verified membership registers to INEC at least 21 days before any primary, congress or convention. Only persons whose names appear on the submitted register are eligible to vote or contest.

Political parties held several congresses and primaries while the Court of Appeal judgement stood. Those processes now face legal uncertainty, with opposition parties reported to be reviewing the registers submitted to INEC against the dates on which candidates defected.

INEC’s silence leaves open the question of how it will treat candidates whose names have already been published. The commission says an opinion will come only after it studies the judgement.

World.title: Manufacturers deepen local raw materials sourcing, up 11% in 3yrs
World.content:
economy

By Yinka Kolawole

Nigeria’s manufacturing sector recorded a steady increase in the use of locally sourced raw materials between 2021 and 2024, with the share rising from 51.5 per cent in 2021 to 57.1 per cent in 2024, as foreign exchange pressures, naira depreciation and rising import costs pushed manufacturers towards domestic alternatives.

Data from the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria, MAN, showed that local raw material sourcing averaged 51.5 per cent in 2021, rising marginally to 52.8 per cent in 2022 and 53.5 per cent in 2023, before climbing sharply to 57.1 per cent in 2024.

The 5.6 percentage-point increase recorded between 2021 and 2024 represents an improvement of about 10.9 per cent over the four-year period.

Director-General of MAN, Segun Ajayi-Kadir, attributed the latest improvement to increased efforts by manufacturers to deepen backward integration amid persistent foreign exchange challenges and high import costs.

According to him, notable improvements in local sourcing were recorded in the Wood and Wood Products, Textile, Apparel and Footwear, and Chemical and Pharmaceutical subsectors, while Electrical and Electronics remained heavily dependent on imported components.

The naira’s sharp depreciation in 2023 and 2024 significantly increased the cost of imported machinery and raw materials, but also encouraged manufacturers to seek domestic alternatives.

Ajayi-Kadir cited Chemical and Allied Products as an example, noting that the company now sources about 90 per cent of its calcium carbonate locally.

The increase in local sourcing has also coincided with improved capacity utilisation in some manufacturing subsectors.

Recent CBN data showed that overall manufacturing capacity utilisation rose from 51.33 per cent in the first quarter of 2025 to 57.50 per cent in the second quarter.

Non-metallic products recorded the highest capacity utilisation at 74.11 per cent in Q2 2025, followed by Food, Beverage and Tobacco at 60.73 per cent. Ajayi-Kadir attributed the performance of the leading sectors to rising domestic demand, favourable policy measures and increased local sourcing of raw materials.

He said the MAN Economic Report for H1 2025 showed that capacity utilisation in the non-metallic sector rose from 57.1 per cent in H2 2024 to 62.3 per cent in H1 2025, while Food, Beverage and Tobacco increased from 57.6 per cent to 62.52 per cent.

“The non-metallic mineral products, such as cement, tiles and construction materials, benefit from increased demand tied to housing construction, especially in urban areas,” he said.

Similarly, the MAN DG said the Food, Beverage and Tobacco sector was supported by rising food demand driven by Nigeria’s large and growing population, particularly in urban areas.

Ajayi-Kadir stressed that deeper local sourcing would reduce manufacturers’ exposure to foreign exchange volatility and import bottlenecks.

“The two mentioned sectors access a higher percentage of raw material inputs locally, thereby facing less foreign exchange pressures and import constraints.

This aids planning, allowing expansion, increasing capacity, and development along the value chain,” he stated.

World.title: Kidnappers torture 20 corps members, reduce ransom to N100m — Relatives
World.content:
File image

***Transport firm withholding passengers’ next-of-kin details— Parents

***FG should tell us what it’s doing—Oyo govt

By Chidi Nkwopara & Adeola Badru

IBADAN— AS the deadline for payment expires within hours, the 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, members abducted in Imo State are being subjected to severe beatings by their captors, including the female victims, Vanguard has learned.

This came as it was learned yesterday that the kidnappers reduced their ransom to N5million each.

Recall that the prospective corps members were abducted last Thursday while travelling from Ibadan to their respective NYSC orientation camps.The vehicles were attacked by gunmen along the Owerri-Onitsha Road in Umunoha, Imo State, while the graduates were travelling to orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states.
